# Antares





<Meta title="Welcome" />

[Documentation](https://godaddy.github.io/antares) | [Storybook](https://godaddy.github.io/antares/storybook)

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

Install the package:

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

Import and use a component:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@godaddy/antares';

export default function App() {
  return <Button variant="primary">Get Started</Button>;
}
```

### Per-Component Imports [#per-component-imports]

Each component is available as a standalone entry point. This lets your bundler load only the JavaScript and CSS for the components you use:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@godaddy/antares/Button';
import { Flex } from '@godaddy/antares/Layout';
import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares/Chart';
```

This also works with autocomplete in IDEs and LLMs, so you can import from the root package and let your editor/agent suggest the available components.

## Framework Setup [#framework-setup]

Antares ships CSS alongside its JavaScript modules. Each component chunk imports a corresponding `.css` file (e.g., `import './src-BZhWcxqJ.css'`). Most bundlers handle this automatically, but some frameworks need extra configuration to process CSS imports from `node_modules`.

### Next.js [#nextjs]

Add `@godaddy/antares` to [`transpilePackages`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/transpilePackages) so Next.js processes the package through its own CSS pipeline instead of treating it as a pre-built external:

```js
// next.config.js
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  transpilePackages: ['@godaddy/antares'],
};

module.exports = nextConfig;
```

Without this, Next.js will throw:

```text
Global CSS cannot be imported from within node_modules.
```

### Remix [#remix]

Remix with Vite handles CSS imports from `node_modules` in the client bundle automatically. However, during SSR, Vite treats `node_modules` as externals by default, which bypasses CSS processing. Add `@godaddy/antares` to [`ssr.noExternal`](https://vite.dev/config/ssr-options#ssr-noexternal) to fix this:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  ssr: {
    noExternal: ['@godaddy/antares'],
  },
});
```

### Vite [#vite]

Vite processes CSS imports from `node_modules` out of the box. No additional configuration is needed for client-side SPAs.

If you are using Vite with SSR (e.g., custom SSR setup, not Remix), add `@godaddy/antares` to `ssr.noExternal` as shown in the [Remix section](#remix).

### Other Bundlers [#other-bundlers]

Any bundler that supports CSS imports will work with Antares. If your bundler does not process CSS imports from `node_modules` by default, ensure it is configured to do so. For example, with raw webpack you may need [`css-loader`](https://webpack.js.org/loaders/css-loader/) configured to handle `.css` files from `node_modules`.

# Alert















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A minimal alert with a title and body text.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Alert, type AlertProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: Partial<AlertProps>) {\n  return (\n    <Alert emphasis=\&#x22;info\&#x22; title=\&#x22;Your domain is ready\&#x22; {...props}>\n      You can now start building your website.\n    </Alert>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Emphasis Variants [#emphasis-variants]

All 7 emphasis categories. Each variant carries a distinct visual accent and semantic icon so the type of message is never communicated by color alone.

<Story of="EmphasesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Alert, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst emphases = ['critical', 'warning', 'success', 'info', 'highlight', 'premium', 'internal'] as const;\n\nexport function EmphasesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;1rem\&#x22;>\n      {emphases.map((emphasis) => (\n        <Alert key={emphasis} emphasis={emphasis} title={`This is a ${emphasis} alert`}>\n          Description for the {emphasis} emphasis variant.\n        </Alert>\n      ))}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Dismissible [#dismissible]

When an \`onClose\` callback is provided, a dismiss button is rendered. The component does not manage its own visibility — the parent is responsible for unmounting or hiding the alert when \`onClose\` fires.

<Story of="DismissibleExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Alert, type AlertProps, Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function DismissibleExample(props?: Partial<AlertProps>) {\n  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(true);\n\n  if (!visible) return <Button onPress={() => setVisible(true)}>Show alert</Button>;\n\n  return (\n    <Alert emphasis=\&#x22;success\&#x22; title=\&#x22;Your account's been verified\&#x22; onClose={() => setVisible(false)} {...props}>\n      We've successfully verified your identity.\n    </Alert>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### With Action [#with-action]

Pass a \`Button\` to the \`actions\` slot to give the user a clear path to resolve the alert.

<Story of="WithActionExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Alert, Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function WithActionExample() {\n  return (\n    <Alert\n      emphasis=\&#x22;warning\&#x22;\n      title=\&#x22;Your payment method is expiring\&#x22;\n      actions={\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n          Update Payment Method\n        </Button>\n      }\n      onClose={() => undefined}\n    >\n      Please update your payment method before it expires.\n    </Alert>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key               | Description                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`             | Moves focus to the dismiss button or action button |
| `Space` / `Enter` | Activates the focused button                       |

### Screen readers [#screen-readers]

The alert container uses `role="alert"`, which creates an ARIA live region. When an alert is rendered or its content changes, screen readers announce the message automatically — the user does not need to navigate to the alert to hear it.

### Dismiss button label [#dismiss-button-label]

The dismiss button defaults to `aria-label="Close"`. Override it via `ariaLabels={{ close: '...' }}` to provide more specific context for screen readers (e.g. `"Dismiss payment warning"`). This is especially useful when multiple alerts are visible at the same time.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Write alert content from the user's perspective: describe what happened and what they can do next, not the underlying technical error.
* Use `critical` only when the user truly cannot continue without resolving the issue. Overusing it reduces its impact.
* Always provide a `title` when the alert includes a dismiss button — it improves the reading experience for screen reader users.
* When using `actions`, prefer `secondary` or `tertiary` Button variants. Avoid placing a primary action inside an alert.
* Do not stack multiple alerts of the same emphasis; consolidate the message into a single alert.

# Button



























<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

Use the `LinkButton` component instead when you need navigation functionality with a button-like appearance.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

The default/tertiary button is the base for all other buttons in the system. It provides no significant visual treatment other than to provide indication for the user to take a common action.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <Button>Click me!</Button>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Primary [#primary]

The primary button should be used to indicate the most important action for the user to take in their current experience.

<Story of="PrimaryExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, type ButtonProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function PrimaryExample(props: ButtonProps) {\n  return (\n    <Button {...props} variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>\n      Primary Button\n    </Button>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Secondary [#secondary]

The secondary button indicates an action of secondary importance.

<Story of="SecondaryExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SecondaryExample() {\n  return <Button variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22;>Secondary Button</Button>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Tertiary [#tertiary]

The tertiary button is the default, low-emphasis style used for common, non-critical actions.

<Story of="TertiaryExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TertiaryExample() {\n  return <Button variant=\&#x22;tertiary\&#x22;>Tertiary Button</Button>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Critical [#critical]

The critical button signifies to the user a destructive action will take place.

<Story of="CriticalExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CriticalExample() {\n  return <Button variant=\&#x22;critical\&#x22;>Critical Button</Button>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled [#disabled]

Any button variant can be disabled to prevent interaction, communicated with reduced opacity and a not-allowed cursor.

<Story of="DisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, Flex, LinkButton } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DisabledExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22;>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; isDisabled>\n        Primary Disabled\n      </Button>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22; isDisabled>\n        Secondary Disabled\n      </Button>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;tertiary\&#x22; isDisabled>\n        Tertiary Disabled\n      </Button>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;critical\&#x22; isDisabled>\n        Critical Disabled\n      </Button>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;inline\&#x22; isDisabled>\n        Inline Disabled\n      </Button>\n      <LinkButton variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22; href=\&#x22;#\&#x22; isDisabled>\n        Link Disabled\n      </LinkButton>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Icon [#icon]

You may provide an optional \`Icon\` component to the button. If you do not include text, you must provide an aria-label attribute to identify the purpose of the button. This will produce a square button.

<Story of="IconExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, Flex, Icon, LinkButton, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function IconExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <div>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>\n          <Icon icon=\&#x22;star\&#x22; />\n          <Text>With an icon!</Text>\n        </Button>\n      </div>\n\n      <div>\n        <LinkButton variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22; href=\&#x22;#\&#x22; isExternal>\n          <Text>An external link!</Text>\n        </LinkButton>\n      </div>\n\n      <Flex alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Text>Icon only button:</Text>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Star\&#x22;>\n          <Icon icon=\&#x22;star\&#x22; />\n        </Button>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <div>\n        <Text>\n          Hey look at me!{' '}\n          <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;inline\&#x22; isExternal>\n            link button\n          </LinkButton>{' '}\n          I have an icon!\n        </Text>\n      </div>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Inline [#inline]

The inline button sits within a run of text, styled like a link while retaining button semantics.

<Story of="InlineExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function InlineExample() {\n  return (\n    <Text>\n      I am an <Button variant=\&#x22;inline\&#x22;>inline button</Button> surrounded by text!\n    </Text>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Minimal [#minimal]

The minimal button is an icon-only button that's used when space is limited and/or when the action is universally understood.

<Story of="MinimalExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, Flex, Icon } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function MinimalExample() {\n  return (\n    <table className=\&#x22;button-story-table\&#x22;>\n      <thead>\n        <tr>\n          <th scope=\&#x22;col\&#x22;>\n            <Flex blockPadding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; />\n              </Button>\n              <Button variant=\&#x22;minimal\&#x22; size=\&#x22;md\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Edit\&#x22;>\n                <Icon icon=\&#x22;edit\&#x22; />\n              </Button>\n              <Button variant=\&#x22;minimal\&#x22; ### Sizes [#sizes]

Buttons come in small and medium sizes to fit different layout densities.

<Story of="SizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, Flex, Icon, LinkButton, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22;>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Star\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;star\&#x22; />\n      </Button>\n\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        Small\n      </Button>\n\n      <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Star\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;star\&#x22; />\n        <Text>Link Small</Text>\n      </LinkButton>\n\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Star\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;star\&#x22; />\n      </Button>\n\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Medium</Button>\n\n      <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;star\&#x22; />\n        <Text>Link Medium</Text>\n      </LinkButton>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

# Calendar



















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* Single-date (`Calendar`) and range (`RangeCalendar`) grids built on React Aria
* Month dropdown plus a typeable year input in the header for fast navigation
* Keyboard navigable and screen-reader announced
* `minValue` / `maxValue` bounds and `isDateUnavailable` per-day disabling
* Date-only values via `@internationalized/date`'s `CalendarDate`

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Working with dates [#working-with-dates]

`Calendar` values are `CalendarDate` objects. Import the date primitives you need from the `@godaddy/antares/date` subpath:

```tsx
import { parseDate, today, getLocalTimeZone } from '@godaddy/antares/date';
import { Calendar } from '@godaddy/antares';

<Calendar aria-label="Date" defaultValue={parseDate('2024-03-15')} />;
<Calendar aria-label="Today" defaultValue={today(getLocalTimeZone())} />;
```

`@godaddy/antares/date` re-exports [`@internationalized/date`](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/internationalized/date/), the package behind these date primitives.

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A single-date calendar.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Calendar } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { parseDate } from '@godaddy/antares/date';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <Calendar aria-label=\&#x22;Event date\&#x22; defaultFocusedValue={parseDate('2024-03-01')} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### With value [#with-value]

A calendar with a pre-selected date.

<Story of="CalendarWithValueExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Calendar } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { parseDate } from '@godaddy/antares/date';\n\nexport function CalendarWithValueExample() {\n  return <Calendar aria-label=\&#x22;Event date\&#x22; defaultValue={parseDate('2024-03-15')} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Range [#range]

Selecting a start and end date.

<Story of="RangeCalendarExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RangeCalendar } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { parseDate } from '@godaddy/antares/date';\n\nexport function RangeCalendarExample() {\n  return (\n    <RangeCalendar\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Trip dates\&#x22;\n      defaultValue={{ start: parseDate('2024-03-10'), end: parseDate('2024-03-15') }}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Min / Max [#min--max]

Bounding selectable dates.

<Story of="CalendarMinMaxExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Calendar } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { parseDate } from '@godaddy/antares/date';\n\nexport function CalendarMinMaxExample() {\n  return (\n    <Calendar\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Booking date\&#x22;\n      defaultValue={parseDate('2024-03-15')}\n      minValue={parseDate('2024-03-05')}\n      maxValue={parseDate('2024-03-25')}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Unavailable [#unavailable]

Disabling scattered individual dates with \`isDateUnavailable\`.

<Story of="CalendarUnavailableExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Calendar } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { isWeekend, parseDate } from '@godaddy/antares/date';\n\nexport function CalendarUnavailableExample() {\n  return (\n    <Calendar\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Weekday only\&#x22;\n      defaultValue={parseDate('2024-03-15')}\n      isDateUnavailable={(date) => isWeekend(date, 'en-US')}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled [#disabled]

A fully disabled calendar.

<Story of="CalendarDisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Calendar } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { parseDate } from '@internationalized/date';\n\nexport function CalendarDisabledExample() {\n  return <Calendar aria-label=\&#x22;Event date\&#x22; defaultValue={parseDate('2024-03-15')} isDisabled />;\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

* Arrow keys move by day; PageUp/PageDown by month; Home/End to row edges
* Focus-visible outline; disabled days are not focusable
* Out-of-month days render at reduced opacity and are not selectable

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Always provide an `aria-label` on standalone calendars.
* Use `isDateUnavailable` for scattered disabled days; use `minValue` / `maxValue` for contiguous bounds.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

* Dates not formatting per locale? Ensure the app is wrapped in `<I18nProvider locale="…">`.

# Carousel























<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

The default carousel is a carousel that is uncontrolled, it shows the first slide by default. You can also pass the \`defaultActiveIndex\` prop to the \`Carousel\` component to set the initial active slide index.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Carousel, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <Carousel style={{ maxWidth: 400 }}>\n      {Array.from({ length: 3 }).map((_, index) => (\n        <Flex key={index} alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; style={{ height: 300, background: 'lavender' }}>\n          Slide {index + 1}\n        </Flex>\n      ))}\n    </Carousel>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

The controlled carousel is a carousel that is controlled by the \`activeIndex\` prop.

<Story of="ControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Carousel, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function ControlledExample() {\n  const [activeIndex, setActiveIndex] = useState(1);\n\n  function handlePrev(index: number, _values: { atFirstSlide: boolean; atLastSlide: boolean }) {\n    setActiveIndex(Math.max(0, index - 1));\n  }\n\n  function handleNext(index: number, _values: { atFirstSlide: boolean; atLastSlide: boolean }) {\n    setActiveIndex(Math.min(2, index + 1));\n  }\n\n  function handleChange(index: number) {\n    setActiveIndex(index);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Carousel\n      style={{ maxWidth: 400 }}\n      activeIndex={activeIndex}\n      onPrev={handlePrev}\n      onNext={handleNext}\n      onChange={handleChange}\n    >\n      {Array.from({ length: 3 }).map((_, index) => (\n        <Flex key={index} alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; style={{ height: 300, background: 'lavender' }}>\n          Slide {index + 1}\n        </Flex>\n      ))}\n    </Carousel>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### External Controls (Uncontrolled) [#external-controls-uncontrolled]

You can control the carousel externally by passing the \`ref\` prop to the \`Carousel\` component and using the \`emblaApi\` to control the carousel imperatively.

<Story of="ExternalControlsUncontrolledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, Icon, Carousel, Flex, type CarouselRef } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useRef } from 'react';\n\nconst TOTAL_SLIDES = 3;\n\nexport function ExternalControlsUncontrolledExample() {\n  const carouselRef = useRef<CarouselRef>(null);\n\n  function handlePrev() {\n    carouselRef.current?.emblaApi?.goToPrev();\n  }\n\n  function handleNext() {\n    carouselRef.current?.emblaApi?.goToNext();\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ maxWidth: 400 }}>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;row\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; alignSelf=\&#x22;end\&#x22;>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;External prev slide\&#x22; onClick={handlePrev}>\n          <Icon icon=\&#x22;chevron-left\&#x22; />\n        </Button>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;External next slide\&#x22; onClick={handleNext}>\n          <Icon icon=\&#x22;chevron-right\&#x22; />\n        </Button>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Carousel hideNavigationControls ref={carouselRef} id=\&#x22;carousel\&#x22;>\n        {Array.from({ length: TOTAL_SLIDES }).map((_, index) => (\n          <Flex key={index} alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; style={{ height: 300, background: 'lavender' }}>\n            Slide {index + 1}\n          </Flex>\n        ))}\n      </Carousel>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### External Controls (Controlled) [#external-controls-controlled]

You can control the carousel externally by using the \`activeIndex\` prop to control the active slide index.

<Story of="ExternalControlsControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, Icon, Carousel, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nconst TOTAL_SLIDES = 3;\n\nexport function ExternalControlsControlledExample() {\n  const [activeIndex, setActiveIndex] = useState(1);\n\n  function handlePrev() {\n    setActiveIndex(Math.max(0, activeIndex - 1));\n  }\n\n  function handleNext() {\n    setActiveIndex(Math.min(TOTAL_SLIDES - 1, activeIndex + 1));\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ maxWidth: 400 }}>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;row\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; alignSelf=\&#x22;end\&#x22;>\n        <Button\n          variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22;\n          aria-label=\&#x22;External prev slide\&#x22;\n          onClick={handlePrev}\n          isDisabled={activeIndex === 0}\n        >\n          <Icon icon=\&#x22;chevron-left\&#x22; />\n        </Button>\n        <Button\n          variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22;\n          aria-label=\&#x22;External next slide\&#x22;\n          onClick={handleNext}\n          isDisabled={activeIndex === TOTAL_SLIDES - 1}\n        >\n          <Icon icon=\&#x22;chevron-right\&#x22; />\n        </Button>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Carousel hideDots hideNavigationControls activeIndex={activeIndex}>\n        {Array.from({ length: TOTAL_SLIDES }).map((_, index) => (\n          <Flex key={index} alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; style={{ height: 300, background: 'lavender' }}>\n            Slide {index + 1}\n          </Flex>\n        ))}\n      </Carousel>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Hide Controls [#hide-controls]

The hide controls carousel is a carousel that hides the navigation controls.

<Story of="HideControlsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Carousel, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function HideControlsExample() {\n  return (\n    <Carousel style={{ maxWidth: 400 }} hideNavigationControls hideDots>\n      {Array.from({ length: 3 }).map((_, index) => (\n        <Flex key={index} alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; style={{ height: 300, background: 'lavender' }}>\n          Slide {index + 1}\n        </Flex>\n      ))}\n    </Carousel>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Variable Widths [#variable-widths]

It supports multiple slides with different widths.

<Story of="VariableWidthsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Carousel, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst SLIDE_WIDTHS = [200, 100, 300, 100, 200];\n\nexport function VariableWidthsExample() {\n  return (\n    <Carousel style={{ maxWidth: 400 }}>\n      {SLIDE_WIDTHS.map((width, index) => (\n        <Flex\n          key={index}\n          alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;\n          justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;\n          style={{ width, height: 300, background: 'lavender' }}\n        >\n          Slide {index + 1}\n        </Flex>\n      ))}\n    </Carousel>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Events [#events]

You can listen to events like \`onChange\`, \`onPrev\`, or \`onNext\`.

<Story of="EventsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Box, Carousel, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function EventsExample() {\n  const [message, setMessage] = useState('Listening for change events...');\n  const [messagePrev, setMessagePrev] = useState('Listening for prev events...');\n  const [messageNext, setMessageNext] = useState('Listening for next events...');\n\n  function handleChange(index: number, values: { atFirstSlide: boolean; atLastSlide: boolean }) {\n    setMessage(`onChange: ${index}, firstSlide: ${values.atFirstSlide}, lastSlide: ${values.atLastSlide}`);\n  }\n\n  function handlePrev(index: number, values: { atFirstSlide: boolean; atLastSlide: boolean }) {\n    setMessagePrev(`onPrev: ${index}, firstSlide: ${values.atFirstSlide}, lastSlide: ${values.atLastSlide}`);\n  }\n\n  function handleNext(index: number, values: { atFirstSlide: boolean; atLastSlide: boolean }) {\n    setMessageNext(`onNext: ${index}, firstSlide: ${values.atFirstSlide}, lastSlide: ${values.atLastSlide}`);\n  }\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <Box>{message}</Box>\n      <Box>{messagePrev}</Box>\n      <Box>{messageNext}</Box>\n\n      <Carousel\n        style={{ maxWidth: 400 }}\n        defaultActiveIndex={2}\n        onChange={handleChange}\n        onPrev={handlePrev}\n        onNext={handleNext}\n      >\n        {Array.from({ length: 3 }).map((_, index) => (\n          <Flex key={index} alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; style={{ height: 300, background: 'lavender' }}>\n            Slide {index + 1}\n          </Flex>\n        ))}\n      </Carousel>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### RTL Direction [#rtl-direction]

The carousel follows the current \*\*layout direction\*\* (LTR or RTL). By default, that direction is detected automatically from the browser or system settings.

<Story of="RTLDirectionExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Carousel, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { RTLProvider } from '../../../utils/rtl-locale-provider.tsx';\n\nexport function RTLDirectionExample() {\n  return (\n    <RTLProvider>\n      <Carousel style={{ maxWidth: 400 }}>\n        {Array.from({ length: 3 }).map((_, index) => (\n          <Flex key={index} alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; style={{ height: 300, background: 'lavender' }}>\n            Slide {index + 1}\n          </Flex>\n        ))}\n      </Carousel>\n    </RTLProvider>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

# Checkbox























<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A single checkbox with a label.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Checkbox } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <Checkbox>One checkbox</Checkbox>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Indeterminate [#indeterminate]

Checkboxes can display an indeterminate state (neither checked nor unchecked), with the use of the \`isIndeterminate\` prop, commonly used for "select all" functionality when some but not all child items are selected.

<Story of="CheckboxIndeterminateExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Checkbox } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CheckboxIndeterminateExample() {\n  return <Checkbox isIndeterminate>Option 1</Checkbox>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Checkbox Group [#checkbox-group]

Group multiple checkboxes together with a shared label and description.

<Story of="CheckboxGroupBasicExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CheckboxGroupBasicExample() {\n  return (\n    <CheckboxGroup label=\&#x22;Favorite colors\&#x22;>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;blue\&#x22;>Blue</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;red\&#x22;>Red</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;green\&#x22;>Green</Checkbox>\n    </CheckboxGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

Manage checkbox group state programmatically with controlled component pattern.

<Story of="CheckboxGroupControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CheckboxGroupControlledExample() {\n  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>(['baseball', 'tennis']);\n\n  return (\n    <CheckboxGroup\n      label=\&#x22;Favorite sports\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;Select your favorite sports\&#x22;\n      value={selected}\n      onChange={setSelected}\n    >\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;basketball\&#x22;>Basketball</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;soccer\&#x22;>Soccer</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;baseball\&#x22;>Baseball</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;tennis\&#x22;>Tennis</Checkbox>\n    </CheckboxGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Horizontal Layout [#horizontal-layout]

Display checkboxes in a horizontal row instead of vertical stack.

<Story of="CheckboxGroupHorizontalExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CheckboxGroupHorizontalExample() {\n  return (\n    <CheckboxGroup label=\&#x22;Favorite colors\&#x22; orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22;>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;blue\&#x22;>Blue</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;red\&#x22;>Red</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;green\&#x22;>Green</Checkbox>\n    </CheckboxGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled States [#disabled-states]

Individual checkboxes within a group can be disabled while others remain interactive.

<Story of="CheckboxGroupDisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CheckboxGroupDisabledExample() {\n  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>(['purple', 'red']);\n\n  return (\n    <CheckboxGroup\n      label=\&#x22;Favorite colors\&#x22;\n      value={selected}\n      onChange={setSelected}\n      errorMessage=\&#x22;At least one color must be selected\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;Choose your favorite color\&#x22;\n      isDisabled\n    >\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;blue\&#x22;>Blue</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;red\&#x22;>Red</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;green\&#x22;>Green</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;purple\&#x22;>Purple</Checkbox>\n    </CheckboxGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Required Indicator [#required-indicator]

Mark a checkbox group as required with visual indicator and validation.

<Story of="CheckboxGroupRequiredExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CheckboxGroupRequiredExample() {\n  return (\n    <CheckboxGroup\n      label=\&#x22;Favorite colors\&#x22;\n      errorMessage=\&#x22;At least one color must be selected\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;Choose your favorite color\&#x22;\n      isRequired\n    >\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;blue\&#x22;>Blue</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;red\&#x22;>Red</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;green\&#x22;>Green</Checkbox>\n    </CheckboxGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Invalid State [#invalid-state]

Display error state and error message for validation feedback.

<Story of="CheckboxGroupInvalidExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CheckboxGroupInvalidExample() {\n  return (\n    <CheckboxGroup label=\&#x22;Favorite colors\&#x22; isInvalid description=\&#x22;Choose your favorite color\&#x22;>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;blue\&#x22;>Blue</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;red\&#x22;>Red</Checkbox>\n      <Checkbox value=\&#x22;green\&#x22;>Green</Checkbox>\n    </CheckboxGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

Components automatically add data attributes for styling different states:

**CheckboxGroup Container:** `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-orientation`

**Checkbox:** `data-selected`, `data-indeterminate`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focused`, `data-disabled`

```css
.my-checkbox-group [data-selected] {
  color: #09757a;
  font-weight: 500;
}

.my-checkbox-group[data-invalid] {
  border-color: #db1802;
}

.my-checkbox-group [data-focused] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

.my-checkbox-group [data-indeterminate] {
  background-color: #1976d2;
}

.my-checkbox-group [data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.4;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Pass `className` or `style` to customize a checkbox field container. Use descendant data-attribute selectors to style the interactive checkbox state:

```jsx
<CheckboxGroup label="Select options" className="custom-checkbox-group">
  <Checkbox value="option1" className="custom-checkbox">
    Option 1
  </Checkbox>
  <Checkbox value="option2" className="highlighted-checkbox">
    Option 2
  </Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>
```

## Key Features [#key-features]

### Indeterminate State [#indeterminate-state]

The `isIndeterminate` prop displays a minus icon to represent a partial selection state. This is useful for "select all" checkboxes when only some items in a collection are selected.

```jsx
<Checkbox isIndeterminate onChange={handleSelectAll}>
  Select All
</Checkbox>
```

### Group Validation [#group-validation]

CheckboxGroup supports validation states and error messages:

* **isRequired**: Marks the group as required with visual indicator
* **isInvalid**: Shows error state styling
* **errorMessage**: Displays validation error text below the group

```jsx
<CheckboxGroup
  label="Required selection"
  isRequired
  isInvalid={!hasSelection}
  errorMessage="At least one option must be selected"
>
  <Checkbox value="a">Option A</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox value="b">Option B</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>
```

### Orientation [#orientation]

Control the layout with the `orientation` prop (matching `RadioGroup`):

* `vertical` (default): Stacks checkboxes vertically
* `horizontal`: Arranges checkboxes in a horizontal row

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard Navigation [#keyboard-navigation]

* **Tab**: Moves focus to the next/previous checkbox
* **Space**: Toggles the focused checkbox
* **Shift + Tab**: Moves focus to the previous checkbox

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

* `aria-disabled` for disabled checkboxes
* `aria-required` when selection is required
* `aria-invalid` for validation errors
* Proper labeling with `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Selection Not Updating [#selection-not-updating]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: Using both value and defaultValue
<CheckboxGroup value={value} defaultValue={["a"]}>
  <Checkbox value="a">Option A</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<CheckboxGroup value={value} onChange={setValue}>
  <Checkbox value="a">Option A</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<CheckboxGroup defaultValue={["a"]}>
  <Checkbox value="a">Option A</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>
```

### Indeterminate State Not Updating [#indeterminate-state-not-updating]

The `isIndeterminate` prop must be explicitly managed - it doesn't automatically reflect parent-child relationships:

```jsx
// ✅ Correct: Manually manage indeterminate state
const [childSelections, setChildSelections] = React.useState([]);
const allSelected = childSelections.length === totalChildren;
const someSelected = childSelections.length > 0 && !allSelected;

<Checkbox
  isSelected={allSelected}
  isIndeterminate={someSelected}
  onChange={handleSelectAll}
>
  Select All
</Checkbox>
```

### Styling Overrides Not Applying [#styling-overrides-not-applying]

```css
/* ❌ May not have enough specificity */
.my-custom-checkbox {
  color: red;
}

/* ✅ Use data attributes with className for higher specificity */
.my-checkbox-group [data-selected] {
  color: red;
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

### Keyboard Navigation Not Working [#keyboard-navigation-not-working]

```css
/* ❌ Don't remove focus outlines without replacement */
[data-focused] {
  outline: none;
}

/* ✅ Provide visible focus indicator */
.my-checkbox-group [data-focused] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use Checkboxes [#when-to-use-checkboxes]

* ✅ For selecting multiple independent options
* ✅ When users can select zero, one, or many items
* ✅ For toggling settings or features on/off
* ✅ When all available options should be visible
* ❌ For mutually exclusive options (use Radio instead)
* ❌ For simple on/off toggles without labels (use Toggle/Switch instead)

### Label Guidelines [#label-guidelines]

* Use clear, concise labels that describe what selecting the option means
* Keep labels short (1-5 words when possible)
* Ensure labels are descriptive without being verbose
* Place the most commonly selected options first in groups

### Validation [#validation]

Always provide clear error messages and use appropriate validation states:

```jsx
<CheckboxGroup
  label="Terms and conditions"
  isRequired
  isInvalid={!agreedToTerms}
  errorMessage="You must agree to the terms to continue"
>
  <Checkbox value="terms">I agree to the terms and conditions</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox value="privacy">I agree to the privacy policy</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>
```

### Group Organization [#group-organization]

* Limit checkbox groups to 7-10 options for better usability
* Use logical ordering (alphabetical, frequency of use, or importance)
* Consider using CheckboxGroup for related options, even if there are only 2-3
* Provide a group label that clearly describes the choice being made

## Props [#props]

The `Checkbox` component has the following props:

<PropTable />

The `CheckboxGroup` component has the following props:

<PropTable />


# CircularProgress













<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A basic determinate progress indicator with a label and helper text.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { CircularProgress } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <CircularProgress value={60} label=\&#x22;Uploading…\&#x22; helperText=\&#x22;3 of 5 files uploaded\&#x22; />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Sizes [#sizes]

Four circle diameters are available: \`sm\` (64px), \`md\` (96px), \`lg\` (128px), and \`xl\` (160px).

<Story of="SizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { CircularProgress, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;flex-end\&#x22;>\n      <CircularProgress size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; value={40} label=\&#x22;Small\&#x22; />\n      <CircularProgress size=\&#x22;md\&#x22; value={60} label=\&#x22;Medium\&#x22; />\n      <CircularProgress size=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; value={75} label=\&#x22;Large\&#x22; />\n      <CircularProgress size=\&#x22;xl\&#x22; value={90} label=\&#x22;Extra Large\&#x22; />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Emphasis [#emphasis]

Use the \`emphasis\` prop to communicate status: \`success\`, \`warning\`, or \`critical\`. When omitted, the default teal fill is used.

<Story of="EmphasisExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { CircularProgress, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function EmphasisExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;flex-end\&#x22;>\n      <CircularProgress value={60} label=\&#x22;Default\&#x22; />\n      <CircularProgress emphasis=\&#x22;success\&#x22; value={100} label=\&#x22;Success\&#x22; helperText=\&#x22;Complete\&#x22; />\n      <CircularProgress emphasis=\&#x22;warning\&#x22; value={70} label=\&#x22;Warning\&#x22; helperText=\&#x22;Storage almost full\&#x22; />\n      <CircularProgress emphasis=\&#x22;critical\&#x22; value={30} label=\&#x22;Critical\&#x22; helperText=\&#x22;Action required\&#x22; />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

* `role="progressbar"` on the container
* `aria-valuenow` reflects the current value (clamped to 0–100)
* `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` define the range (default `0`–`100`)
* `aria-valuetext` provides a formatted string (e.g. `"60%"`) via `Intl.NumberFormat`; the same string is rendered inside the circle. Override the text with the `aria-valuetext` prop, or control formatting with `formatOptions`
* `aria-labelledby` associates the visible label when the `label` prop is provided
* `aria-describedby` wires the `helperText` to the progressbar for screen readers
* The decorative SVG and output text are hidden via `aria-hidden="true"`

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# DatePicker





















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* `DatePicker` (single) and `DateRangePicker` (range): a read-only formatted date label; the whole field opens a calendar popover
* Built on React Aria — native form integration, validation, focus management, and screen-reader support
* Consumer-controlled label formatting via `formatOptions`
* `minValue` / `maxValue` bounds and `isDateUnavailable` per-day disabling

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Working with dates [#working-with-dates]

Values are `CalendarDate` objects. Import the date primitives you need from the `@godaddy/antares/date` subpath:

```tsx
import { parseDate, today, getLocalTimeZone } from '@godaddy/antares/date';
import { DatePicker } from '@godaddy/antares';

<DatePicker label="Event" defaultValue={parseDate('2024-03-15')} />;
<DatePicker label="Today" defaultValue={today(getLocalTimeZone())} />;
```

`@godaddy/antares/date` re-exports [`@internationalized/date`](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/internationalized/date/), the package behind these date primitives. Locale comes from a host `<I18nProvider>`. This version has no typed/segmented entry - selection is via the calendar.

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A single date picker.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DatePicker } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <DatePicker label=\&#x22;Event date\&#x22; />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Range [#range]

A start/end range picker.

<Story of="DateRangePickerExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DateRangePicker } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DateRangePickerExample() {\n  return <DateRangePicker label=\&#x22;Trip dates\&#x22; />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

Driving the value with \`useState\`.

<Story of="DatePickerControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { DatePicker } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { type CalendarDate, parseDate } from '@godaddy/antares/date';\n\nexport function DatePickerControlledExample() {\n  const [value, setValue] = useState<CalendarDate | null>(parseDate('2024-03-15'));\n  return <DatePicker label=\&#x22;Event date\&#x22; value={value} onChange={setValue} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Custom format [#custom-format]

<Story of="DatePickerFormatOptionsExample" />

### Error [#error]

<Story of="DatePickerWithErrorExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DatePicker } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DatePickerWithErrorExample() {\n  return <DatePicker label=\&#x22;Event date\&#x22; isInvalid errorMessage=\&#x22;Please choose a date\&#x22; />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled [#disabled]

<Story of="DatePickerDisabledExample" />

## Customization [#customization]

`formatOptions` accepts any `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` (e.g. `{ dateStyle: 'short' }`, `{ month: 'long', year: 'numeric' }`). `placeholder` sets the empty-state text.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

* The whole field is a single focusable button; Enter/Space opens the popover
* Focus is trapped in the open popover and returns to the trigger on close
* Esc and outside-click dismiss the popover
* The calendar grid is fully keyboard navigable and screen-reader announced

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Provide a `label` (or `aria-label`) on every picker.
* For typed/keyboard-fast date entry far from today, use the calendar's month dropdown and year input.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

* Dates not localizing? Wrap the app in `<I18nProvider locale="…">`.
* Form value missing on submit? Pass a `name` — React Aria renders the hidden input.

# Drawer

















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

An overlay panel that slides in from a screen edge. Built like `Modal` (a RAC modal overlay with an `elevation="overlay"` panel and CSS transitions), it supports sidebar navigation and bottom sheets.

`DrawerTrigger` is the composition helper: it wraps a trigger button and a `<Drawer>`, handling open state and `aria-controls` linkage automatically. Based on RAC `DialogTrigger`.

## Features [#features]

* Slides in from any screen edge (top, bottom, left, right)
* `overlay` elevation panel over a dimmed backdrop, matching `Modal`
* Physical `placement` (does not flip for RTL)
* Focus trapping, backdrop dismiss, and scroll lock via RAC Modal
* CSS transitions with `prefers-reduced-motion` support

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Use \`\<DrawerTrigger>\` to wrap a trigger button and a \`\<Drawer>\`. The drawer opens when the trigger is pressed.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Drawer, DrawerTrigger, Button, Text, Box } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <DrawerTrigger>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open drawer</Button>\n      <Drawer placement=\&#x22;right\&#x22; isDismissable aria-label=\&#x22;Drawer\&#x22;>\n        <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n          <Text>Drawer content goes here.</Text>\n        </Box>\n      </Drawer>\n    </DrawerTrigger>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Bottom Sheet [#bottom-sheet]

Use \`placement="bottom"\` with controlled state for a bottom sheet pattern.

<Story of="BottomSheetExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Drawer, Button, Text, Box } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function BottomSheetExample() {\n  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>\n        Open bottom sheet\n      </Button>\n      <Drawer\n        placement=\&#x22;bottom\&#x22;\n        isOpen={open}\n        onOpenChange={setOpen}\n        isDismissable\n        showCloseButton\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Bottom sheet\&#x22;\n      >\n        <Box elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n          <Text as=\&#x22;p\&#x22;>Bottom sheet with close button.</Text>\n          <Text as=\&#x22;p\&#x22;>This is the content</Text>\n        </Box>\n      </Drawer>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Placements [#placements]

The drawer slides in from whichever edge you set with \`placement\`.

<Story of="PlacementsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Drawer, Button, Flex, Text, type DrawerPlacement, Box } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst PLACEMENTS: DrawerPlacement[] = ['left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom'];\n\nexport function PlacementsExample() {\n  const [placement, setPlacement] = useState<DrawerPlacement>('right');\n  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22;>\n      {PLACEMENTS.map(function renderButton(p) {\n        return (\n          <Button\n            key={p}\n            variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;\n            onPress={function openAt() {\n              setPlacement(p);\n              setOpen(true);\n            }}\n          >\n            Open {p}\n          </Button>\n        );\n      })}\n      <Drawer\n        placement={placement}\n        isOpen={open}\n        onOpenChange={setOpen}\n        isDismissable\n        aria-label={`${placement} drawer`}\n      >\n        <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n          <Text>Placement: {placement}</Text>\n        </Box>\n      </Drawer>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Nested Popover [#nested-popover]

Popovers rendered inside a drawer stay open without dismissing the drawer.

<Story of="NestedPopoverExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Drawer, Button, Text, Popover, PopoverTrigger, Box } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NestedPopoverExample() {\n  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>\n        Open drawer\n      </Button>\n      <Drawer placement=\&#x22;right\&#x22; isOpen={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} isDismissable aria-label=\&#x22;Nested popover\&#x22;>\n        <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n          <PopoverTrigger>\n            <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open popover</Button>\n            <Popover>\n              <Text>Popover inside drawer</Text>\n            </Popover>\n          </PopoverTrigger>\n        </Box>\n      </Drawer>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### No Escape Dismiss [#no-escape-dismiss]

Use \`isKeyboardDismissDisabled\` to prevent the drawer from being dismissed by the escape key.

<Story of="NoEscapeDismissExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Drawer, Button, Text, Box } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NoEscapeDismissExample() {\n  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);\n  return (\n    <>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>\n        Open\n      </Button>\n      <Drawer\n        placement=\&#x22;right\&#x22;\n        isOpen={open}\n        onOpenChange={setOpen}\n        isDismissable\n        isKeyboardDismissDisabled\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Drawer\&#x22;\n      >\n        <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n          <Text>Cannot escape</Text>\n        </Box>\n      </Drawer>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key      | Action                                                |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `Escape` | Close the drawer (unless `isKeyboardDismissDisabled`) |
| `Tab`    | Move focus within the drawer (focus is trapped)       |

### ARIA [#aria]

* `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"` on the drawer panel (via RAC Modal)
* Dialog accessible name via `aria-label`
* `aria-label="Close"` on the built-in close button

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Always provide an `aria-label` so the dialog has an accessible name.
* Use `isDismissable` to allow closing via backdrop click.
* Don't nest drawers.

# DropZone

















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A minimal drop zone. The \`onDrop\` callback receives the dropped items; use the exported \`isFileDropItem\` guard to narrow them to files. Wrap the instructional text in \`\<Text slot="label">\` so it labels the visually hidden drop button for screen readers.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DropZone, isFileDropItem, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <DropZone\n      onDrop={function handleDrop(e) {\n        const files = e.items.filter(isFileDropItem);\n        console.log('Dropped files:', files);\n      }}\n    >\n      <Text slot=\&#x22;label\&#x22;>Drop files to upload.</Text>\n    </DropZone>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled [#disabled]

Set \`isDisabled\` to prevent the drop zone from accepting interactions. The zone is dimmed and the cursor indicates it is not interactive.

<Story of="DisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DropZone, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DisabledExample() {\n  return (\n    <DropZone isDisabled>\n      <Text slot=\&#x22;label\&#x22;>Drop files to upload.</Text>\n    </DropZone>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### File Upload [#file-upload]

A reference composition combining \`DropZone\` with \`FileTrigger\` to support both click-to-browse and drag-and-drop. Use this as a starting point and adapt the accepted formats, size limit, and handlers to your product's requirements.

<Story of="FileUploadExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\nimport { Button, DropZone, FileTrigger, Flex, Icon, isFileDropItem, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst ACCEPTED_TYPES = ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif', 'application/pdf'];\n\ntype Preview = { name: string; url?: string };\n\nexport function FileUploadExample() {\n  const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[]>([]);\n  const [previews, setPreviews] = useState<Preview[]>([]);\n\n  useEffect(\n    function buildPreviews() {\n      const next: Preview[] = files.map(function toPreview(file) {\n        return {\n          name: file.name,\n          url: file.type.startsWith('image/') ? URL.createObjectURL(file) : undefined\n        };\n      });\n      setPreviews(next);\n\n      return function revoke() {\n        for (const preview of next) {\n          if (preview.url) URL.revokeObjectURL(preview.url);\n        }\n      };\n    },\n    [files]\n  );\n\n  function handleFiles(list: FileList | File[] | null) {\n    if (!list) return;\n    setFiles(Array.from(list));\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <DropZone\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Add files or drag them here\&#x22;\n        getDropOperation={function getDropOperation(types) {\n          return ACCEPTED_TYPES.some(function matches(type) {\n            return types.has(type);\n          })\n            ? 'copy'\n            : 'cancel';\n        }}\n        onDrop={async function handleDrop(e) {\n          const dropped = await Promise.all(\n            e.items.filter(isFileDropItem).map(function getFile(item) {\n              return item.getFile();\n            })\n          );\n          handleFiles(dropped);\n        }}\n        gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;\n      >\n        <FileTrigger acceptedFileTypes={ACCEPTED_TYPES} allowsMultiple onSelect={handleFiles}>\n          <Button variant=\&#x22;inline\&#x22; style={{ fontSize: '0.984rem', fontWeight: 700 }}>\n            <Icon icon=\&#x22;add\&#x22; aria-hidden=\&#x22;true\&#x22; />\n            Add files\n          </Button>\n        </FileTrigger>\n        <Text style={{ fontSize: '0.778rem' }}>The file must be less than 256MB</Text>\n      </DropZone>\n\n      <Flex justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22;>\n        <Text style={{ fontSize: '0.778rem' }}>Supported formats:</Text>\n        <Text as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22; style={{ fontSize: '0.778rem' }}>\n          .pdf, .jpg, .gif, .png\n        </Text>\n      </Flex>\n\n      {previews.length > 0 ? (\n        <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Selected files\&#x22;>\n          {previews.map(function renderPreview(preview) {\n            return (\n              <Flex key={preview.name} direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22;>\n                {preview.url ? (\n                  <img\n                    src={preview.url}\n                    alt={preview.name}\n                    style={{ width: 64, height: 64, objectFit: 'cover', borderRadius: 8 }}\n                  />\n                ) : (\n                  <Flex\n                    alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;\n                    justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;\n                    style={{ width: 64, height: 64, borderRadius: 8, background: '#f5f5f5' }}\n                  >\n                    <Text style={{ textTransform: 'uppercase' }}>{preview.name.split('.').pop()}</Text>\n                  </Flex>\n                )}\n                <Text maxLines={1} style={{ maxWidth: 64 }}>\n                  {preview.name}\n                </Text>\n              </Flex>\n            );\n          })}\n        </Flex>\n      ) : null}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Drop Target Label [#drop-target-label]

Pass a render-prop function as \`children\` to change the zone's content while a valid drag is active. Branching on \`isDropTarget\` requires no extra state. Pair it with \`getDropOperation\` to reject unsupported types - the label only appears when the drag is accepted.

<Story of="DropTargetLabelExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DropZone, type DropZoneRenderProps, isFileDropItem, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst ACCEPTED_TYPES = ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif', 'application/pdf'];\n\nexport function DropTargetLabelExample() {\n  return (\n    <DropZone\n      getDropOperation={function getDropOperation(types) {\n        return ACCEPTED_TYPES.some(function matches(type) {\n          return types.has(type);\n        })\n          ? 'copy'\n          : 'cancel';\n      }}\n      onDrop={async function handleDrop(e) {\n        const files = await Promise.all(\n          e.items.filter(isFileDropItem).map(function getFile(item) {\n            return item.getFile();\n          })\n        );\n        console.log(\n          'Dropped files:',\n          files.map(function getName(f) {\n            return f.name;\n          })\n        );\n      }}\n    >\n      {function renderContent({ isDropTarget }: DropZoneRenderProps) {\n        return isDropTarget ? (\n          <Text as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>Drop files to upload.</Text>\n        ) : (\n          <Text slot=\&#x22;label\&#x22;>Add files or drag them here.</Text>\n        );\n      }}\n    </DropZone>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Replace Existing File [#replace-existing-file]

Use \`children\` as a render function to show different content based on the current zone state - here, swapping the default label for "Drop to replace" when a file is already selected and a new drag is active. The same \`onDrop\` handler services both the drag path and the \`FileTrigger\` click path, so either gesture replaces the selection.

<Story of="ReplaceFileExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';\nimport {\n  Button,\n  DropZone,\n  type DropZoneRenderProps,\n  FileTrigger,\n  Flex,\n  Icon,\n  isFileDropItem,\n  Text\n} from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst ACCEPTED_TYPES = ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif', 'application/pdf'];\n\ntype Preview = { name: string; url?: string };\n\nexport function ReplaceFileExample() {\n  const [file, setFile] = useState<File | null>(null);\n  const [preview, setPreview] = useState<Preview | null>(null);\n\n  useEffect(\n    function buildPreview() {\n      if (!file) {\n        setPreview(null);\n        return;\n      }\n      const url = file.type.startsWith('image/') ? URL.createObjectURL(file) : undefined;\n      setPreview({ name: file.name, url });\n      return function revoke() {\n        if (url) URL.revokeObjectURL(url);\n      };\n    },\n    [file]\n  );\n\n  function handleFiles(list: FileList | File[] | null) {\n    if (!list) return;\n    const f = Array.from(list)[0];\n    if (f) setFile(f);\n  }\n\n  const isFilled = file !== null;\n\n  return (\n    <div style={{ width: 200 }}>\n      <DropZone\n        aria-label={isFilled ? 'Replace uploaded file' : 'Add a file'}\n        getDropOperation={function getDropOperation(types) {\n          return ACCEPTED_TYPES.some(function matches(type) {\n            return types.has(type);\n          })\n            ? 'copy'\n            : 'cancel';\n        }}\n        onDrop={async function handleDrop(e) {\n          const dropped = await Promise.all(\n            e.items.filter(isFileDropItem).map(function getFile(item) {\n              return item.getFile();\n            })\n          );\n          handleFiles(dropped);\n        }}\n        gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;\n        style={{ minHeight: 200 }}\n      >\n        {function renderContent({ isDropTarget }: DropZoneRenderProps) {\n          if (isFilled && isDropTarget) {\n            return <Text as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>Drop to replace</Text>;\n          }\n\n          if (isFilled) {\n            return (\n              <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22;>\n                {preview?.url ? (\n                  <img\n                    src={preview.url}\n                    alt={preview.name}\n                    style={{ width: 64, height: 48, objectFit: 'cover', borderRadius: 4 }}\n                  />\n                ) : (\n                  <Flex\n                    alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;\n                    justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;\n                    style={{ width: 64, height: 48, background: '#f5f5f5', borderRadius: 4 }}\n                  >\n                    <Text style={{ textTransform: 'uppercase' }}>{file?.name.split('.').pop()}</Text>\n                  </Flex>\n                )}\n                <Text maxLines={1} style={{ maxWidth: 96 }}>\n                  {file?.name}\n                </Text>\n                <FileTrigger acceptedFileTypes={ACCEPTED_TYPES} onSelect={handleFiles}>\n                  <Button variant=\&#x22;inline\&#x22;>Replace</Button>\n                </FileTrigger>\n              </Flex>\n            );\n          }\n\n          return (\n            <FileTrigger acceptedFileTypes={ACCEPTED_TYPES} onSelect={handleFiles}>\n              <Button\n                variant=\&#x22;inline\&#x22;\n                style={{\n                  position: 'absolute',\n                  inset: 0,\n                  display: 'flex',\n                  flexDirection: 'column',\n                  alignItems: 'center',\n                  justifyContent: 'center',\n                  gap: '0.5rem',\n                  fontSize: '0.984rem',\n                  fontWeight: 700\n                }}\n              >\n                <Icon icon=\&#x22;add\&#x22; aria-hidden=\&#x22;true\&#x22; />\n                Add files\n              </Button>\n            </FileTrigger>\n          );\n        }}\n      </DropZone>\n    </div>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key               | Description                                                      |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`             | Moves focus to the drop zone                                     |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Opens the file picker so files can be selected without a pointer |

### Screen readers [#screen-readers]

The drop zone renders a visually hidden `<button>` inside the container. Assistive technology discovers and announces this button as an interactive element — activating it opens the native file picker without a pointer.

The button's accessible name is built from two sources, combined in order:

1. **`<Text slot="label">`** — any `Text` child with `slot="label"` has its `id` linked to the button via `aria-labelledby`. This is the recommended way to provide a contextual label that is also visible to sighted users.
2. **`aria-label`** — pass `aria-label` on the `DropZone` component to override or supplement the label (e.g. `aria-label="Upload profile photo"`). When no `Text slot="label"` is present and no `aria-label` is set, the button falls back to the default "DropZone" label provided by React Aria.

```tsx
<DropZone onDrop={handleDrop}>
  <Text slot="label">Drop files to upload.</Text>
</DropZone>
```

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Use the drop zone alongside a button-based file picker — drag-and-drop is a convenience, never the only way to upload.
* Replace the default text with `children` to communicate the accepted file types and size limits up front.
* Let the drop zone fill its container; constrain it with the surrounding layout rather than setting a fixed width on the component itself.
* Reflect upload state (validating, uploading, error) outside the drop zone so the target area stays clear and predictable.

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# Field primitives















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

**Composition primitives.** The field components (TextField, NumberField, DateField, Select, RadioGroup, CheckboxGroup) compose these internally — reach for those first. These primitives are also the building blocks for custom composite fields, e.g. an input and a select sharing one bordered box.

The field decoration is split into granular, composable pieces so the same structure is shared across every field:

* **`Field`** — stacks a field's label, control, description, and error in one consistently spaced column (pure layout — a `Flex` column with the standard field gap).
* **`FieldLabel`** — names the field and flags whether it's required (wraps React Aria `Label`, rendering an optional `*` indicator).
* **`FieldGroup`** — the bordered box that visually unites a field's controls and reflects their shared focus, disabled, and invalid state. Used only by "boxed" fields (TextField, NumberField, Select, DateField); presentationally it is a React Aria `Group`.
* **`FieldInput`** — the single-line control the user types into (a normalized React Aria `Input` given antares spacing via `Box`).
* **`FieldTextArea`** — the multiline control the user types into (a normalized React Aria `TextArea` given antares spacing via `Box`).
* **`FieldButton`** — an actionable control placed inside the box, such as the NumberField steppers or a search submit (a click target within the group).
* **`FieldTrigger`** — a full-width value-display button inside the box that opens an overlay (used by Select and DatePicker): a value area plus a trailing icon, laid out across the group. `variant="select"` is transparent and input-like; `variant="control"` is a filled segment inside a shared group.
* **`FieldDescription`** — helper text that explains the field; renders nothing when empty (wraps the antares `Text` with `slot="description"`).
* **`FieldError`** — surfaces the field's validation messages when it is invalid, and nothing when valid (a thin wrapper over React Aria `FieldError`).

`FieldLabel`, `FieldDescription`, and `FieldError` each render `null` when they have no content, so callers pass `label` / `description` / `errorMessage` straight through without guarding.

## Usage [#usage]

## Composition [#composition]

A boxed field composes the primitives inside its React Aria field wrapper. Use
`Field as={...}` to merge the field wrapper and the layout column into a single
element:

```text
Field as={RACTextField}                   ← field wrapper + layout column (one element)
├── FieldLabel                            ← when label provided (+ required indicator)
├── FieldGroup                            ← the bordered Group; styles inner controls via CSS
│   └── {children}                        ← FieldInput, FieldButton, DateInput, etc.
├── FieldDescription                      ← when description provided
└── FieldError                            ← renders validation messages when invalid
```

A field without a box (RadioGroup / CheckboxGroup) composes `Field` + `FieldLabel` + `FieldError` and omits `FieldGroup`.

`FieldGroup` is purely presentational — it renders the styled `Group` and holds no React Aria context. The surrounding field wires value, disabled, and validation state into its controls.

### Positioning controls inside the group [#positioning-controls-inside-the-group]

`FieldGroup` rounds its outer corners from DOM order: the group's CSS rounds the start corners of its **first child** and the end corners of its **last child**, so controls are seamless inside and rounded only at the box edges. Author children in visual order and the rounding follows — no per-control positioning prop. A lone control (a TextField input, a Select trigger) is both first and last, so it rounds both edges. The rules are RTL-safe (they use logical `start`/`end` corners).

### States [#states]

The states **disabled**, **readonly**, and **invalid** are applied by the field wrapper (e.g. TextField, NumberField, Select). The group reflects them via data attributes on the group.

| State                                                                                    | CSS Selector      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| disabled — Applied when the field wrapper is disabled.                                   | `[data-disabled]` |
| invalid — Applied when the field wrapper is invalid (e.g. validation failed).            | `[data-invalid]`  |
| focus — Whether an element within the group has keyboard focus (for focus-ring styling). | `[data-focused]`  |

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Composes the presentational field primitives (Field, FieldLabel, FieldGroup,
FieldDescription) into a minimal boxed field, showing how the group and its
position markers are assembled. The fill is a static placeholder - real value,
focus, and validation behavior is wired up by the field components (TextField,
NumberField, Select).

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldGroup, FieldLabel, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\n/** Props for the composed field-group examples. */\nexport interface FieldGroupBasicProps {\n  /** Class name merged onto the FieldGroup. */\n  className?: string;\n\n  /** Helper text shown below the group. */\n  description?: string;\n\n  /** Whether the control is disabled. */\n  isDisabled?: boolean;\n\n  /** Whether the field is required. */\n  isRequired?: boolean;\n\n  /** Label text shown above the group. */\n  label?: string;\n}\n\nexport function DefaultExample({ className, description, isDisabled, isRequired, label }: FieldGroupBasicProps) {\n  return (\n    <Field>\n      <FieldLabel isRequired={isRequired}>{label}</FieldLabel>\n      <FieldGroup className={className} isDisabled={isDisabled} gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;span\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n          Placeholder content\n        </Flex>\n      </FieldGroup>\n      <FieldDescription>{description}</FieldDescription>\n    </Field>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />
