# FileTrigger











<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* Turns any pressable component (such as an Antares `Button`) into a file picker trigger.
* Renders a visually hidden `<input type="file">` — no styling of its own.
* Restricts selection by MIME type, allows multiple files, directory selection, and camera capture.
* Resets the input value before every open, so re-selecting the same file still fires `onSelect`.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Wrap any pressable component. Activating the child opens the native file picker; the selected files arrive in \`onSelect\`.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, FileTrigger } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <FileTrigger\n      onSelect={function handleSelect(files) {\n        if (!files) return;\n        console.log('Selected files:', Array.from(files));\n      }}\n    >\n      <Button>Select a file</Button>\n    </FileTrigger>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Accepted Types [#accepted-types]

Restrict the picker to specific MIME types with \`acceptedFileTypes\`, and allow more than one file with \`allowsMultiple\`.

<Story of="AcceptedTypesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Button, FileTrigger } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function AcceptedTypesExample() {\n  return (\n    <FileTrigger\n      acceptedFileTypes={['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif']}\n      allowsMultiple\n      onSelect={function handleSelect(files) {\n        if (!files) return;\n        console.log('Selected images:', Array.from(files));\n      }}\n    >\n      <Button>Select images</Button>\n    </FileTrigger>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

`FileTrigger` adds no visuals or ARIA of its own — accessibility comes from the pressable child you provide. Use a component with an accessible name (e.g. an Antares `Button` with clear label text) so assistive technology announces the action. The underlying `<input>` is visually hidden but remains operable by keyboard through the child's press behavior.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* `acceptedFileTypes` is a best-effort filter for the OS picker — always validate file type and size again in your `onSelect` handler, since it can be bypassed.
* Pair `FileTrigger` with `DropZone` to offer both click-to-browse and drag-and-drop. See the DropZone "File Upload" example.
* Keep the child a single pressable element; `FileTrigger` forwards press behavior to whatever you nest inside it.

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# Icon







<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

The `Icon` component provides a flexible and performant way to display SVG icons with extensive customization options. Built on top of the Bento Icon system, it features on-demand loading from a CDN, automatic caching, and enhanced props for the Antares design system.

## Features [#features]

* **On-demand loading**: Icons are loaded asynchronously from CDN only when needed
* **Automatic caching**: Once loaded, icons are cached for optimal performance
* **Flexible sizing**: Support for `width` and `height` props
* **Color inheritance**: Uses `currentColor` by default for seamless theme integration
* **Accessibility ready**: Built-in support for screen readers and keyboard navigation
* **TypeScript support**: Fully typed with comprehensive prop interfaces
* **Bento integration**: Extends Bento Icon with additional Antares-specific features

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Props [#props]

The `Icon` component accepts the following props:

<PropTable />

### Prop Inheritance [#prop-inheritance]

The component extends `BentoIconProps` and passes through all standard HTML attributes and accessibility props to the underlying Bento Icon component. This includes:

* **Accessibility**: `aria-label`, `aria-describedby`, `role`, `title`
* **Events**: `onClick`, `onMouseOver`, `onFocus`, etc.
* **Styling**: `className`, `style`, `data-*` attributes
* **Transform**: `rotate`, `flip` for icon transformations

## Basic Usage [#basic-usage]

<Story of="Stories.Icon" />

<Source language="tsx" code="SourceIcon" />

## Size Variants [#size-variants]

Specify explicit width and height values:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" width={24} height={24} />
```

You can use different values for width and height:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" width={32} height={16} />
```

## Customization [#customization]

### Slots [#slots]

The Icon component uses Bento's slot system with the following component hierarchy and available slot override points:

#### Component Hierarchy [#component-hierarchy]

```text
Icon (registered as "Icon")
└── BentoIcon (registered as "BentoIcon", slot="icon")
    └── BentoIllustration (registered as "BentoIllustration", slot="content")
```

#### Available Slot Overrides [#available-slot-overrides]

* **`icon`**: Overrides the entire BentoIcon component - affects icon loading, caching, sprite/SVG mode switching, data attributes, and the overall icon wrapper
* **`icon.content`**: Overrides the BentoIllustration component - affects SVG transformations (rotate, flip), accessibility attributes (`role`, `focusable`, `aria-labelledby`), viewBox calculations, and final SVG element rendering

For complete slot override patterns and examples, see the `@bento/slots` package documentation.

### Custom Icons [#custom-icons]

While the Icon component loads design system approved icons from the CDN by default, teams can introduce custom icons using the underlying Bento Icon system.

#### Adding Icons Synchronously [#adding-icons-synchronously]

Use the `set` method to add custom icons that are available immediately:

```jsx
import { Icon, set, parser } from '@godaddy/antares';

// Add a custom icon from an SVG string
const customIconSvg = '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="..."/></svg>';

set({
  'custom-logo': parser(customIconSvg),
  'team-icon': (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">
      <path d="M12 2l3.09 6.26L22 9.27l-5 4.87 1.18 6.88L12 17.77l-6.18 3.25L7 14.14 2 9.27l6.91-1.01L12 2z" />
    </svg>
  )
});

// Now use your custom icon
<Icon icon="custom-logo" />
<Icon icon="team-icon" />
```

#### Adding Icons Asynchronously [#adding-icons-asynchronously]

Use the `ondemand` method to load custom icons from your own sources:

```jsx
import { Icon, ondemand, parser } from '@godaddy/antares';

// Add a custom loader for team-specific icons
const unregister = ondemand(async function loadTeamIcons(iconName) {
  if (iconName.startsWith('team-')) {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/team-icons/${iconName}.svg`);
    const svgContent = await response.text();
    return parser(svgContent);
  }
  // Return undefined to let other loaders handle this icon
});

// Icons prefixed with 'team-' will load from your custom endpoint
<Icon icon="team-dashboard" />
<Icon icon="team-settings" />

// Later, if needed, unregister the loader
unregister();
```

#### Custom Icon APIs [#custom-icon-apis]

The following methods are exported from `@godaddy/antares` for custom icon management:

* **`set(icons)`**: Synchronously add icons to the store
* **`ondemand(loader)`**: Register an asynchronous icon loader (returns unregister function)
* **`parser(svgString)`**: Parse SVG strings into React elements

These are re-exports of the underlying Bento Icon system methods. For complete API documentation, advanced usage patterns, and implementation details, see the `@bento/icon` and `@bento/svg-parser` package documentation.

#### Notes [#notes]

* Custom icons integrate seamlessly with all Icon component features (transformations, accessibility, sprite mode, etc.)
* Multiple `ondemand` loaders can be registered and will be called in order until one returns content
* Use the `parser` function to convert SVG strings to React elements
* Custom icons are cached automatically just like CDN icons

### Styling [#styling]

#### CSS Classes [#css-classes]

The component accepts standard `className` and `style` props:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" className="my-icon" style={{ margin: '10px' }} />
```

**Important**: When you supply a `className`, you make a commitment to take over all styling of the component as it will remove the standard class names. Use data attributes for targeted styling instead.

#### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

The component automatically adds data attributes for styling hooks:

* `data-icon`: The icon name (always present)
* `data-color`: Applied when color prop is set
* `data-loading`: Applied during icon loading from CDN
* `data-mode`: Applied when mode prop is set (e.g., "sprite")
* `data-flip`: Applied when flip prop is set ("horizontal" or "vertical")
* `data-rotate`: Applied when rotate prop is set (90, 180, or 270)

The component also includes accessibility attributes:

* `role="presentation"`: For decorative icons
* `role="img"`: When title prop is provided
* `focusable="false"`: Prevents keyboard focus

```css
/* Style by icon name */
[data-icon="star"] {
  color: gold;
}

/* Style by color */
[data-color="red"] {
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
}

/* Style loading state */
[data-loading="true"] {
  opacity: 0.5;
}

/* Style sprite mode */
[data-mode="sprite"] {
  filter: drop-shadow(0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1));
}

/* Style flipped icons */
[data-flip="horizontal"] {
  transform-origin: center;
}

/* Style rotated icons */
[data-rotate="90"] {
  transition: transform 0.2s ease;
}
```

## Color Customization [#color-customization]

### Inherit from Parent (Default) [#inherit-from-parent-default]

By default, icons inherit the color from their parent element via `currentColor`:

```jsx
<div style={{ color: 'blue' }}>
  <Icon icon="star" /> {/* Will be blue */}
</div>
```

### Explicit Colors [#explicit-colors]

Override the color with specific values:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" color="#ff6b35" />          // Hex color
<Icon icon="star" color="rgb(255, 107, 53)" /> // RGB color
<Icon icon="star" color="var(--primary-color)" /> // CSS variable
<Icon icon="star" color="currentColor" />     // Explicit inheritance
```

## Icon Transformations [#icon-transformations]

Transform capabilities are inherited from the Bento Illustration component. For complete transformation options and implementation details, see the `@bento/illustration` package documentation.

### Rotation [#rotation]

Rotate icons by 90-degree increments:

```jsx
<Icon icon="arrow" rotate={90} />   // 90 degrees
<Icon icon="arrow" rotate={180} />  // 180 degrees
<Icon icon="arrow" rotate={270} />  // 270 degrees
```

### Flipping [#flipping]

Flip icons horizontally or vertically:

```jsx
<Icon icon="arrow" flip="horizontal" />
<Icon icon="arrow" flip="vertical" />
```

## Loading States [#loading-states]

### Placeholder Content [#placeholder-content]

Provide fallback SVG content while icons load from the CDN:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor">
    <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3" />
  </svg>
</Icon>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Decorative Icons [#decorative-icons]

For purely decorative icons, no additional attributes are needed. The icon will have `role="presentation"` and be ignored by screen readers:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" /> {/* Decorative, screen readers will ignore */}
```

### Semantic Icons [#semantic-icons]

For icons that convey meaning, use the `title` prop. This automatically adds `role="img"` and provides screen reader accessible text:

```jsx
{/* Semantic icon - use title prop */}
<Icon icon="star" title="Favorite item" />

{/* Warning icon with semantic meaning */}
<Icon icon="alert" title="Warning: Your session will expire soon" />

{/* Status indicator with meaning */}
<Icon icon="check-circle" title="Task completed successfully" />
```

### Interactive Icons [#interactive-icons]

For interactive icons within buttons or links, use the `title` prop on the icon and `aria-label` on the interactive element:

```jsx
{/* Button with icon - label the button, not the icon */}
<button aria-label="Close dialog">
  <Icon icon="close" />
</button>

{/* Icon button where icon has semantic meaning */}
<button aria-label="Mark as favorite">
  <Icon icon="star" title="Favorite" />
</button>

{/* Link with icon */}
<a href="/settings" aria-label="Go to settings">
  <Icon icon="settings" />
</a>
```

## Performance Considerations [#performance-considerations]

### Default Icon Loading [#default-icon-loading]

Icons are loaded on-demand from a CDN using the following process:

1. **First Request**: When an icon is first encountered, it triggers an asynchronous fetch from the CDN
2. **SVG Parsing**: The fetched SVG string is parsed into a React element using `@bento/svg-parser`
3. **Automatic Caching**: Once loaded, the icon is cached in memory to avoid subsequent network requests
4. **Full SVG Rendering**: Each icon instance renders as a complete SVG element with all path data

```jsx
// Each icon renders as a full SVG element
<Icon icon="star" />  // <svg><path d="M3 22v-20l18 10-18 10z" /></svg>
<Icon icon="star" />  // <svg><path d="M3 22v-20l18 10-18 10z" /></svg>
<Icon icon="star" />  // <svg><path d="M3 22v-20l18 10-18 10z" /></svg>
```

This approach works well for SSR and small numbers of icons, but can lead to DOM bloat when the same icon appears many times.

### Sprite Mode Optimization [#sprite-mode-optimization]

When `mode="sprite"` is enabled, the component switches to a more efficient rendering strategy:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" mode="sprite" />
<Icon icon="star" mode="sprite" />
<Icon icon="star" mode="sprite" />
```

**What happens with sprite mode:**

1. **Sprite Sheet Creation**: A hidden SVG sprite sheet is automatically injected into the DOM containing symbol definitions
2. **Reference Rendering**: Each icon renders as a lightweight `<use>` element that references the sprite
3. **Deduplication**: Icon path data only exists once in the sprite sheet, regardless of how many times it's used
4. **Client-Side Hydration**: The sprite sheet is generated and injected after hydration, causing a brief paint event

**DOM Output:**

```html
<!-- Hidden sprite sheet (created automatically) -->
<svg id="bento-svg-sprite" style="display: none;">
  <symbol id="bento-svg-spritesheet-star" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
    <path d="M3 22v-20l18 10-18 10z" />
  </symbol>
</svg>

<!-- Lightweight icon references -->
<svg><use xlink:href="#bento-svg-spritesheet-star" /></svg>
<svg><use xlink:href="#bento-svg-spritesheet-star" /></svg>
<svg><use xlink:href="#bento-svg-spritesheet-star" /></svg>
```

**Performance Benefits:**

* **Reduced DOM Size**: Path data stored once instead of duplicated
* **Lower Memory Usage**: Especially beneficial with many repeated icons
* **Faster Rendering**: Browser optimizations for `<use>` elements

**Trade-offs:**

* **SSR Limitation**: Sprite references render empty until client-side hydration
* **Initial Flash**: Brief moment where icons appear/disappear during sprite injection

### Recommendations [#recommendations]

* **Use default mode** for SSR applications or when icons appear infrequently
* **Use sprite mode** when the same icons appear many times (navigation, lists, tables)
* **Consider preloading** frequently used icons to reduce loading delays
* **Provide fallback content** for critical icons to handle loading states

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Icon Not Loading [#icon-not-loading]

If an icon fails to load:

1. **Check icon name**: Ensure the icon exists in the CDN
2. **Network connectivity**: Verify CDN is accessible
3. **Check browser console**: Look for network errors
4. **Fallback content**: Provide placeholder content for loading states

### Performance Issues [#performance-issues]

For performance optimization:

1. **Preload common icons**: Consider preloading frequently used icons
2. **Use sprite mode**: For repeated icons, consider sprite mode which consolidates multiple icons into a single SVG sprite sheet, reducing DOM size and improving performance when the same icon appears multiple times
3. **Minimize icon sets**: Only load icons that are actually used


# InlineDrawer













<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

`InlineDrawerPanel` is the collapsible content for the accordion pattern — a thin wrapper over RAC `DisclosurePanel` that hides when collapsed. The trigger is any component you slot in with `slot="trigger"` — there's no dedicated trigger component.

## Features [#features]

* In-flow collapsible built on RAC Disclosure — bring your own trigger via `slot="trigger"`
* Animated by default; `animate={false}` disables the transition
* `placement` selects the collapse axis (`left`/`right` → width, `top`/`bottom` → height)
* Controlled and uncontrolled modes (`isExpanded` / `defaultExpanded` / `onExpandedChange`)
* Accordion collapse uses the browser's `hidden="until-found"` for find-in-page
* `prefers-reduced-motion` support

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Put a \`\<Button slot="trigger">\` and an \`\<InlineDrawerPanel>\` inside \`InlineDrawer\`. The panel hides when collapsed and animates open.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { InlineDrawer, InlineDrawerPanel, Button, Box, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <Box style={{ maxInlineSize: 360 }}>\n      <InlineDrawer>\n        <Button slot=\&#x22;trigger\&#x22;>Toggle details</Button>\n        <InlineDrawerPanel>\n          <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n            <Text>Collapsible content goes here.</Text>\n          </Box>\n        </InlineDrawerPanel>\n      </InlineDrawer>\n    </Box>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

Use \`isExpanded\` and \`onExpandedChange\` to drive state externally.

<Story of="ControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { InlineDrawer, InlineDrawerPanel, Button, Box, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ControlledExample() {\n  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; onPress={() => setExpanded(!expanded)}>\n        {expanded ? 'Collapse' : 'Expand'}\n      </Button>\n      <Text>Expanded: {String(expanded)}</Text>\n      <Box style={{ maxInlineSize: 360 }}>\n        <InlineDrawer isExpanded={expanded} onExpandedChange={setExpanded}>\n          <Button slot=\&#x22;trigger\&#x22;>Details</Button>\n          <InlineDrawerPanel>\n            <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n              <Text>Controlled panel content.</Text>\n            </Box>\n          </InlineDrawerPanel>\n        </InlineDrawer>\n      </Box>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Sidebar Nav [#sidebar-nav]

A rail whose content stays visible when collapsed is a composition, not a mode: drive \`isExpanded\` yourself, render always-visible children (no \`InlineDrawerPanel\`), and let \`minSize\`/\`maxSize\` size the rail. Use numeric (px) sizes so the width animates; intrinsic keywords like \`min-content\`/\`max-content\` fit the content exactly but don't animate.

<Story of="SidebarNavExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { InlineDrawer, Flex, ToggleButton, LinkButton, Icon, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst NAV = [\n  { icon: 'grid', label: 'Dashboard', href: '#' },\n  { icon: 'star', label: 'Favorites', href: '#' },\n  { icon: 'comment', label: 'Messages', href: '#' }\n] as const;\n\nexport function SidebarNavExample() {\n  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;row\&#x22;>\n      <InlineDrawer placement=\&#x22;left\&#x22; isExpanded={expanded} onExpandedChange={setExpanded} minSize={35} maxSize={150}>\n        <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;xs\&#x22;>\n          <ToggleButton isSelected={expanded} onChange={setExpanded} aria-label=\&#x22;Menu\&#x22;>\n            <Icon icon=\&#x22;bulleted-list\&#x22; />\n          </ToggleButton>\n          {NAV.map(function renderItem(item) {\n            return (\n              <LinkButton\n                key={item.label}\n                href={item.href}\n                aria-label={!expanded ? item.label : undefined}\n                variant=\&#x22;minimal\&#x22;\n                style={{ justifyContent: 'flex-start' }}\n              >\n                <Icon icon={item.icon} />\n                {expanded ? item.label : null}\n              </LinkButton>\n            );\n          })}\n        </Flex>\n      </InlineDrawer>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ flex: 1, borderInlineStart: '1px solid var(--bd-base)' }}>\n        <Text>Main content area</Text>\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key               | Action                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Toggle via the slotted trigger |
| `Tab`             | Move focus through the content |

### ARIA [#aria]

* A `<Button slot="trigger">` gets `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` wired to the `InlineDrawerPanel` automatically (via RAC Disclosure).
* For the sidebar rail, the toggle is your own control (e.g. a `ToggleButton`) — give icon-only buttons an `aria-label`, and the content stays in the DOM and accessible since nothing is hidden.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Accordion → `Button slot="trigger"` + `InlineDrawerPanel`. Sidebar rail → controlled state + always-visible children.
* For the rail, use numeric (px) `minSize`/`maxSize` so the width animates; `min-content`/`max-content` fit the content exactly but won't animate.
* `placement` does not flip in RTL; the side is decided by document/flex order.
* Don't nest InlineDrawers.

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />

The `InlineDrawerPanel` component accepts the following props:

<PropTable />


# ListBox













<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* **Single or multiple selection**: Set `selectionMode="single"` or `"multiple"`.
* **Controlled or uncontrolled**: Use `selectedKeys` and `onSelectionChange` for controlled state, or `defaultSelectedKeys` for uncontrolled.
* **Layout primitive**: `ListBox` and `ListBoxItem` accept layout props (`gap`, `padding`, etc.) — they extend `FlexOwnProps`.
* **Composes into other components**: `Select` uses `ListBox` internally; reach for `ListBox` directly when you need an inline list rather than a popover dropdown.
* **React Aria integration**: Built on React Aria ListBox for accessibility, keyboard navigation, and typeahead.

`ListBox` requires either `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. For a labeled, popover-style picker, prefer `Select`.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Single selection with static children. Use \`aria-label\` to give the listbox an accessible name.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ListBox, ListBoxItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <ListBox aria-label=\&#x22;Coffee\&#x22; selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;>\n      <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</ListBoxItem>\n      <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</ListBoxItem>\n      <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</ListBoxItem>\n      <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;americano\&#x22;>Americano</ListBoxItem>\n      <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;mocha\&#x22;>Mocha</ListBoxItem>\n    </ListBox>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### List Box Controlled [#list-box-controlled]

Use \`selectedKeys\` and \`onSelectionChange\` for controlled state.

<Story of="ListBoxControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { ListBox, ListBoxItem, Text, type ListBoxKey } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ListBoxControlledExample() {\n  const [selectedKeys, setSelectedKeys] = useState<Set<ListBoxKey>>(new Set(['latte']));\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <ListBox\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Coffee\&#x22;\n        selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;\n        selectedKeys={selectedKeys}\n        onSelectionChange={(keys) => setSelectedKeys(keys === 'all' ? new Set() : new Set(keys))}\n      >\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</ListBoxItem>\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</ListBoxItem>\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</ListBoxItem>\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;americano\&#x22;>Americano</ListBoxItem>\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;mocha\&#x22;>Mocha</ListBoxItem>\n      </ListBox>\n      <Text>\n        <strong>Value:</strong> {selectedKeys.size === 0 ? '(none)' : Array.from(selectedKeys).join(', ')}\n      </Text>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### List Box Multiple [#list-box-multiple]

Set \`selectionMode="multiple"\` to allow multiple values. \`selectedKeys\` is a \`Set\<Key>\` (or the literal \`'all'\`).

<Story of="ListBoxMultipleExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { ListBox, ListBoxItem, Text, type ListBoxKey } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ListBoxMultipleExample() {\n  const [selectedKeys, setSelectedKeys] = useState<'all' | Set<ListBoxKey>>(new Set(['latte', 'mocha']));\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <ListBox\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Coffees you like\&#x22;\n        selectionMode=\&#x22;multiple\&#x22;\n        selectedKeys={selectedKeys}\n        onSelectionChange={(keys) => setSelectedKeys(keys === 'all' ? 'all' : new Set(keys))}\n      >\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</ListBoxItem>\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</ListBoxItem>\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</ListBoxItem>\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;americano\&#x22;>Americano</ListBoxItem>\n        <ListBoxItem id=\&#x22;mocha\&#x22;>Mocha</ListBoxItem>\n      </ListBox>\n      <Text>\n        <strong>Selected:</strong>{' '}\n        {selectedKeys === 'all' ? '(all)' : selectedKeys.size === 0 ? '(none)' : Array.from(selectedKeys).join(', ')}\n      </Text>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

# Menu





<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

Accessible dropdown menu supporting keyboard navigation, nested submenus, single/multiple selection modes, and flexible item rendering with links and sections.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

React Aria Components automatically adds data attributes for styling different states:

**Menu Items:** `data-hovered`, `data-focused`, `data-pressed`, `data-selected`, `data-disabled`

**Popover:** `data-entering`, `data-exiting`

```css
[data-selected] {
  background-color: #eff6ff;
  color: #1e40af;
}

[data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.5;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

[data-entering] {
  animation: slideIn 0.2s ease-out;
}
```

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Individual child components can be styled by passing `className` props:

```jsx
<Menu>
  <MenuItem id="special" className="premium-item">
    Premium Feature
  </MenuItem>
  <MenuSection className="featured-section">
    <MenuHeader>Featured</MenuHeader>
    <MenuItem id="new">What's New</MenuItem>
  </MenuSection>
</Menu>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard Navigation [#keyboard-navigation]

* **Space/Enter**: Opens menu and activates items
* **Arrow Down/Up**: Navigate through items
* **Arrow Right**: Opens submenu
* **Arrow Left**: Closes submenu
* **Home/End**: Jump to first/last item
* **Escape**: Closes menu
* **Tab**: Closes menu and moves to next element
* **Type to select**: Type to jump to matching items

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Submenu Not Opening [#submenu-not-opening]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: MenuItem used directly
<MenuItem id="share">
  Share
  <Menu>
    <MenuItem id="email">Email</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
</MenuItem>

// ✅ Correct: SubmenuTrigger wrapping MenuItem and Menu
<SubmenuTrigger>
  <MenuItem id="share">Share</MenuItem>
  <Menu>
    <MenuItem id="email">Email</MenuItem>
  </Menu>
</SubmenuTrigger>
```

### Selection Not Working [#selection-not-working]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: Using both controlled and uncontrolled props
<Menu
  selectedKeys={selected}
  defaultSelectedKeys={['option1']}
  selectionMode="single"
>
  <MenuItem id="option1">Option 1</MenuItem>
</Menu>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<Menu
  selectionMode="single"
  selectedKeys={selected}
  onSelectionChange={setSelected}
>
  <MenuItem id="option1">Option 1</MenuItem>
</Menu>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<Menu
  selectionMode="single"
  defaultSelectedKeys={['option1']}
>
  <MenuItem id="option1">Option 1</MenuItem>
</Menu>
```

### Styling Not Applying [#styling-not-applying]

```css
/* ❌ May not have enough specificity */
.item {
  background-color: red;
}

/* ✅ Use data attributes for higher specificity */
.my-menu [data-selected] {
  background-color: red;
}
```


# MetricsLockup













<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

MetricsLockup displays a metric value prominently, with an optional title and tooltip for context, an optional trend icon to show direction of change, and a description label below the value.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A metric with a title, info tooltip, value, and description.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { MetricsLockup, type MetricsLockupProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: Partial<MetricsLockupProps> = {}) {\n  return (\n    <MetricsLockup\n      title=\&#x22;Total Revenue\&#x22;\n      titleInfo=\&#x22;The total revenue across all products for the selected period.\&#x22;\n      data=\&#x22;$1,234.56\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;vs. last month\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### With Trend [#with-trend]

Use the \`trend\` prop to show a directional icon next to the description. Accepts \`'positive'\`, \`'negative'\`, or \`'neutral'\`.

<Story of="WithTrendExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { MetricsLockup } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function WithTrendExample() {\n  return <MetricsLockup title=\&#x22;Conversion Rate\&#x22; data=\&#x22;42%\&#x22; description=\&#x22;+3.2% vs. last month\&#x22; trend=\&#x22;positive\&#x22; />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Compact [#compact]

Use the \`compact\` prop to render the metric value and description inline rather than stacked.

<Story of="CompactExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { MetricsLockup } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CompactExample() {\n  return <MetricsLockup title=\&#x22;Sessions\&#x22; data=\&#x22;8,021\&#x22; description=\&#x22;-12% vs. last week\&#x22; trend=\&#x22;negative\&#x22; compact />;\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key    | Description                                                  |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tab    | Moves focus to the info trigger button and shows the tooltip |
| Escape | Closes the tooltip                                           |

### ARIA [#aria]

* The info trigger button uses `aria-label="More information"` to describe its purpose.
* The tooltip uses `role="tooltip"` and is associated with the info trigger via `aria-describedby`.
* The info trigger has a minimum touch target of 44×44px, achieved via a CSS pseudo-element, to meet WCAG 2.5.5.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Keep tooltip content concise and informative.
* The `data` prop accepts strings or numbers — format currency and percentages before passing them in.
* `titleInfo` requires `title` to be set — the info icon is contextually tied to the title label. If `title` is absent, `titleInfo` has no effect.
* `trend` is intended to accompany `description` to provide temporal context (e.g. "↑ +3% vs. last month"). A trend icon alone, with no description, leaves the direction unanchored ("up since *when*?"). If `description` is not provided, `trend` has no effect.

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# Modal

















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

Use `ModalTrigger` to wire a trigger element (typically a `Button`) to a `Modal`. The `Modal` exposes high-level slots for `title`, `description`, `actions`, and `media`, while still accepting arbitrary `children` for custom content.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

The default modal exposes a \`title\`, \`description\`, and \`children\` content area. Open and close state is managed automatically by \`ModalTrigger\`.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ModalTrigger, Modal, Button, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <ModalTrigger>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open modal</Button>\n      <Modal\n        title=\&#x22;Modal title\&#x22;\n        description=\&#x22;She expressed her gratitude again, but as it was too painful a subject to each, to be dwelt on farther.\&#x22;\n      >\n        <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n          This is the children content\n        </Flex>\n      </Modal>\n    </ModalTrigger>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

Pass \`isOpen\` and \`onOpenChange\` to \`ModalTrigger\` to control the open state externally.

<Story of="ControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ModalTrigger, Modal, Button, Flex, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function ControlledExample() {\n  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>\n      <ModalTrigger isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={setIsOpen}>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open modal</Button>\n        <Modal\n          title=\&#x22;Modal title\&#x22;\n          description=\&#x22;She expressed her gratitude again, but as it was too painful a subject to each, to be dwelt on farther.\&#x22;\n          actions={[\n            <Button key=\&#x22;close\&#x22; slot=\&#x22;close\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>\n              Close\n            </Button>\n          ]}\n        />\n      </ModalTrigger>\n\n      <Text>The modal is currently {isOpen ? 'open' : 'closed'}.</Text>\n\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22; onPress={() => setIsOpen(true)}>\n        Open from outside\n      </Button>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### With actions [#with-actions]

Render footer buttons via the \`actions\` prop. Use \`slot="close"\` on a button to close the modal automatically when pressed.

<Story of="WithActionsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ModalTrigger, Modal, Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function WithActionsExample() {\n  return (\n    <ModalTrigger>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open modal</Button>\n      <Modal\n        title=\&#x22;Modal title\&#x22;\n        description=\&#x22;She expressed her gratitude again, but as it was too painful a subject to each, to be dwelt on farther.\&#x22;\n        actions={[\n          <Button key=\&#x22;cancel\&#x22; slot=\&#x22;close\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22;>\n            Cancel\n          </Button>,\n          <Button key=\&#x22;confirm\&#x22; slot=\&#x22;close\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>\n            Confirm\n          </Button>\n        ]}\n      />\n    </ModalTrigger>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Alignment [#alignment]

Use \`centered\` to center the title and description, and \`actionProps\` to control the alignment and direction of the action buttons.

<Story of="AlignmentExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ModalTrigger, Modal, Button, RadioGroup, Radio, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function AlignmentExample() {\n  const [alignment, setAlignment] = useState<string>();\n  const [actionsAlignment, setActionsAlignment] = useState<string>();\n  const [actionsDirection, setActionsDirection] = useState<string>();\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>\n      <ModalTrigger>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open modal</Button>\n\n        <Modal\n          title=\&#x22;Modal title\&#x22;\n          description=\&#x22;She expressed her gratitude again, but as it was too painful a subject to each, to be dwelt on farther.\&#x22;\n          centered={alignment === 'center'}\n          actionProps={{\n            ...(actionsAlignment ? { justifyContent: actionsAlignment } : {}),\n            ...(actionsDirection ? { direction: actionsDirection as 'row' | 'column' } : {})\n          }}\n          actions={[\n            <Button key=\&#x22;cancel\&#x22; slot=\&#x22;close\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22;>\n              Cancel\n            </Button>,\n            <Button key=\&#x22;confirm\&#x22; slot=\&#x22;close\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>\n              Confirm\n            </Button>\n          ]}\n        />\n      </ModalTrigger>\n\n      <RadioGroup orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22; label=\&#x22;Modal alignment\&#x22; value={alignment} onChange={setAlignment}>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;\&#x22;>Start (Default)</Radio>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>Centered</Radio>\n      </RadioGroup>\n\n      <RadioGroup\n        orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22;\n        label=\&#x22;Actions alignment\&#x22;\n        value={actionsAlignment}\n        onChange={setActionsAlignment}\n      >\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>Start</Radio>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>Centered</Radio>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;\&#x22;>End (Default)</Radio>\n      </RadioGroup>\n\n      <RadioGroup\n        orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22;\n        label=\&#x22;Actions direction\&#x22;\n        value={actionsDirection}\n        onChange={setActionsDirection}\n      >\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;row\&#x22;>Row (Default)</Radio>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;column\&#x22;>Column</Radio>\n      </RadioGroup>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### With Media [#with-media]

Pass a \`media\` element to display imagery alongside the content. Configure its layout with \`mediaVariant\` (\`full\` or \`inset\`), \`mediaDirection\` (\`column\` or \`row\`), and \`mediaPosition\` (\`start\` or \`end\`).

<Story of="WithMediaExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ModalTrigger, Modal, Button, RadioGroup, Radio, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function WithMediaExample() {\n  const [mediaVariant, setMediaVariant] = useState<string>();\n  const [mediaDirection, setMediaDirection] = useState<string>();\n  const [mediaPosition, setMediaPosition] = useState<string>();\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>\n      <ModalTrigger>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open modal</Button>\n        <Modal\n          title=\&#x22;Modal title\&#x22;\n          description=\&#x22;She expressed her gratitude again, but as it was too painful a subject to each, to be dwelt on farther.\&#x22;\n          media={\n            <Flex style={{ width: '100%', height: '100%', minWidth: 350, minHeight: 200, backgroundColor: 'teal' }} />\n          }\n          mediaVariant={mediaVariant as 'inset' | 'full' | undefined}\n          mediaDirection={mediaDirection as 'column' | 'row' | undefined}\n          mediaPosition={mediaPosition as 'start' | 'end' | undefined}\n          actions={[\n            <Button key=\&#x22;cancel\&#x22; slot=\&#x22;close\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22;>\n              Cancel\n            </Button>,\n            <Button key=\&#x22;confirm\&#x22; slot=\&#x22;close\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>\n              Confirm\n            </Button>\n          ]}\n        >\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n            This is the children content\n          </Flex>\n        </Modal>\n      </ModalTrigger>\n\n      <RadioGroup orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22; label=\&#x22;Variant\&#x22; value={mediaVariant} onChange={setMediaVariant}>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;inset\&#x22;>Inset</Radio>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;full\&#x22;>Full (Default)</Radio>\n      </RadioGroup>\n\n      <RadioGroup orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22; label=\&#x22;Direction\&#x22; value={mediaDirection} onChange={setMediaDirection}>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;row\&#x22;>Row</Radio>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;column\&#x22;>Column (Default)</Radio>\n      </RadioGroup>\n\n      <RadioGroup orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22; label=\&#x22;Position\&#x22; value={mediaPosition} onChange={setMediaPosition}>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>Start (Default)</Radio>\n        <Radio value=\&#x22;end\&#x22;>End</Radio>\n      </RadioGroup>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard interaction [#keyboard-interaction]

| Key           | Action                                                         |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`         | Moves focus to the next focusable element inside the modal     |
| `Shift + Tab` | Moves focus to the previous focusable element inside the modal |
| `Escape`      | Closes the modal (when dismissable)                            |

### ARIA [#aria]

* `role="dialog"` is applied automatically by the underlying React Aria `Dialog`
* The `title` is rendered as an `<h2>` and linked to the dialog via `aria-labelledby`
* The close button is rendered with `aria-label="Close"`
* Focus is trapped within the modal while open and returned to the trigger on close

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Always provide a `title` so the dialog has an accessible name
* Pair every footer action with `slot="close"` when it should dismiss the modal
* Set `isDismissable={false}` for required confirmations the user must explicitly answer
* Provide meaningful `alt` text for image media, or `alt=""` if it's purely decorative
* Prefer the `actions` prop over manually adding footer buttons in `children` so they get consistent spacing and alignment

## Props [#props]

The `Modal` component accepts the following props:

<PropTable />


# NumberField























<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Minimal usage with label, placeholder, and min/max.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { NumberField, type NumberFieldProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: NumberFieldProps) {\n  return <NumberField label=\&#x22;Quantity\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;0\&#x22; defaultValue={0} {...props} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Number Field Controlled [#number-field-controlled]

Use \`value\` and \`onChange\` for controlled state.

<Story of="NumberFieldControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { NumberField, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NumberFieldControlledExample() {\n  const [value, setValue] = useState(10);\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <NumberField label=\&#x22;Quantity\&#x22; minValue={0} maxValue={100} value={value} onChange={setValue} />\n      <Text>\n        <strong>Value:</strong> {value ?? '(empty)'}\n      </Text>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Number Field Invalid [#number-field-invalid]

Use \`isInvalid\` with \`errorMessage\` for validation feedback.

<Story of="NumberFieldInvalidExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { NumberField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NumberFieldInvalidExample() {\n  return (\n    <NumberField\n      label=\&#x22;Quantity\&#x22;\n      minValue={0}\n      maxValue={100}\n      errorMessage=\&#x22;Please enter a value between 0 and 100\&#x22;\n      isInvalid\n      isRequired\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Number Field Disabled [#number-field-disabled]

Use \`isDisabled\` to prevent input.

<Story of="NumberFieldDisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { NumberField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NumberFieldDisabledExample() {\n  return <NumberField label=\&#x22;Quantity\&#x22; defaultValue={42} minValue={0} maxValue={100} isDisabled />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Number Field Hide Stepper [#number-field-hide-stepper]

Use \`hideStepper\` to show only the input without +/- buttons.

<Story of="NumberFieldHideStepperExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { NumberField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NumberFieldHideStepperExample() {\n  return (\n    <NumberField\n      label=\&#x22;Quantity\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;Enter a value between 0 and 100.\&#x22;\n      placeholder=\&#x22;0\&#x22;\n      minValue={0}\n      maxValue={100}\n      hideStepper\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Number Field Value Scale [#number-field-value-scale]

Use \`minValue\`, \`maxValue\`, and \`step\` to set the allowed values. Steps are calculated from the minimum value.

<Story of="NumberFieldValueScaleExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { NumberField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NumberFieldValueScaleExample() {\n  return (\n    <NumberField\n      label=\&#x22;Step value\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;Steps are from the minimum: minValue={2}, step={3} gives 2, 5, 8, 11, …\&#x22;\n      placeholder=\&#x22;2\&#x22;\n      minValue={2}\n      maxValue={20}\n      step={3}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Format options (numbering system) [#format-options-numbering-system]

By default, NumberField displays the value using the numbering system for the user's locale. Use the \`formatOptions\` prop to override the numbering system by setting the Unicode numbering system locale extension.

<Story of="NumberFieldFormatOptionsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { NumberField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst devanagariFormatOptions = Intl.NumberFormat('hi-IN-u-nu-deva').resolvedOptions();\n\nexport function NumberFieldFormatOptionsExample() {\n  return (\n    <NumberField\n      label=\&#x22;Number (Devanagari)\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;By default, NumberField uses the user's locale. Use formatOptions to override with a Unicode numbering system locale extension (e.g. nu-deva).\&#x22;\n      hideStepper\n      value={1024}\n      formatOptions={devanagariFormatOptions}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Number Field Sizes [#number-field-sizes]

Compare the supported \`md\` and \`sm\` visual sizes.

<Story of="NumberFieldSizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, NumberField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NumberFieldSizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <NumberField label=\&#x22;Quantity (md)\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;0\&#x22; minValue={0} maxValue={100} />\n      <NumberField label=\&#x22;Quantity (sm)\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;0\&#x22; minValue={0} maxValue={100} size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

When focus is in the input (and the field is not read-only), keyboard behavior follows common spinbutton-style conventions:

* **Arrow Up** / **Arrow Down** (or **Up** / **Down**): increase or decrease by `step`
* **Page Up** / **Page Down**: larger increase or decrease when supported
* **Home** / **End**: jump to `minValue` or `maxValue` when those props are set

Stepper buttons are real buttons and follow standard button keyboard activation. Use &#x2A;*`incrementAriaLabel`*&#x2A; and &#x2A;*`decrementAriaLabel`** when the default labels are not enough in your locale or UI.

### ARIA and labeling [#aria-and-labeling]

* The input is associated with the visible label and optional description and error content for assistive technologies.
* Invalid and required states are exposed to assistive technologies when you use `isInvalid`, `errorMessage`, and `isRequired`.
* Set &#x2A;*`isWheelDisabled`** if the value should not change when the user scrolls with a pointer wheel while the field is focused.

## Best practices [#best-practices]

* Pair &#x2A;*`isInvalid`*&#x2A; with &#x2A;*`errorMessage`** so users get both visual and programmatic feedback.
* Remember valid steps start from &#x2A;*`minValue`**.
* Use &#x2A;*`isDisabled`*&#x2A; when the value cannot be changed; use &#x2A;*`isReadOnly`** when the value should be visible but not editable. Do not use them interchangeably.
* For currency or units, ensure &#x2A;*`formatOptions`** (and locale) match what users are allowed to type.

## Props [#props]

The `NumberField` component accepts the following props:

# Pagination

















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

The default pagination is uncontrolled. It renders prev/next buttons and one dot per page. The \`total\` prop sets the number of items.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Pagination } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  const [page, setPage] = useState(0);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <Pagination total={5} onChange={setPage} />\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;span\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n        Current page: {page}\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

Pass \`activeIndex\` and \`onChange\` to control the active page externally.

<Story of="ControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Pagination } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function ControlledExample() {\n  const [page, setPage] = useState(2);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <Pagination total={4} activeIndex={page} onChange={setPage} />\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;span\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n        Current page: {page}\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Default Active [#default-active]

Use \`defaultActiveIndex\` to set the starting page in uncontrolled mode.

<Story of="DefaultActiveExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Pagination } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultActiveExample() {\n  return <Pagination total={5} defaultActiveIndex={2} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### With Limit [#with-limit]

Limit the number of items shown per page. When \`limit\` is greater than 1, the number of pages (dots) is derived from \`Math.ceil(total / limit)\`. For example, 10 items with a limit of 3 produces 4 pages (dots).

<Story of="WithLimitExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Pagination } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function WithLimitExample() {\n  return <Pagination total={10} limit={3} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### onChange Event [#onchange-event]

The \`onChange\` callback fires with the new page index whenever the user navigates.

<Story of="OnChangeExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Pagination } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function OnChangeExample() {\n  const [onChangeValue, setOnChangeValue] = useState<number | undefined>(undefined);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <Pagination total={3} onChange={setOnChangeValue} />\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;span\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n        onChange: {onChangeValue ?? 'none'}\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

# Popover













<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Use it with \`\<PopoverTrigger>\`, which wraps both the popover content and an interactive trigger element (for example, a \`Button\`).

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <PopoverTrigger>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open popover</Button>\n      <Popover>This is the popover content!</Popover>\n    </PopoverTrigger>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Custom Anchor [#custom-anchor]

To position a popover relative to a different element than its trigger, use the \`triggerRef\` and \`isOpen\` props instead of \`\<PopoverTrigger>\`. \`onOpenChange\` is called when the user opens or closes the popover.

<Story of="CustomAnchorExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Popover, Box, Flex, Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useRef, useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function CustomAnchorExample() {\n  const [isOpen, setOpen] = useState(false);\n  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22; onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>\n        Open Popover\n      </Button>\n\n      <Box elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; ref={triggerRef}>\n        Popover will be positioned relative to me\n      </Box>\n\n      <Popover triggerRef={triggerRef} isOpen={isOpen} onOpenChange={setOpen}>\n        Popover content!\n      </Popover>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Close Button and Header [#close-button-and-header]

Use \`showCloseButton\` to show a close button in the popover header. Use the \`header\` prop to render content alongside it.

<Story of="WithCloseButtonExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, Button, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function WithCloseButtonExample() {\n  return (\n    <PopoverTrigger>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Open popover</Button>\n      <Popover showCloseButton header={<Text>Content to show next to the close button</Text>}>\n        This is the popover content!\n      </Popover>\n    </PopoverTrigger>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

Popover width is determined by its content, and it’s recommended to keep it under 400px.

# ProgressBar













<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A determinate progress bar with a label and helper text.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressBar } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <ProgressBar label=\&#x22;Loading…\&#x22; value={60} helperText=\&#x22;Please wait while we process your request\&#x22; />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Sizes [#sizes]

Three track heights are available: \`xs\` (6px), \`sm\` (12px), and \`md\` (24px).

<Story of="SizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressBar, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <ProgressBar label=\&#x22;Extra Small\&#x22; size=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; value={40} />\n      <ProgressBar label=\&#x22;Small\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; value={60} />\n      <ProgressBar label=\&#x22;Medium\&#x22; size=\&#x22;md\&#x22; value={80} />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Statuses [#statuses]

Use the \`status\` prop to communicate intent: \`default\`, \`success\`, \`warning\`, or \`critical\`. Pair with \`helperText\` to provide additional context.

<Story of="StatusesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressBar, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function StatusesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <ProgressBar label=\&#x22;Default\&#x22; status=\&#x22;default\&#x22; value={50} helperText=\&#x22;In progress\&#x22; />\n      <ProgressBar label=\&#x22;Success\&#x22; status=\&#x22;success\&#x22; value={100} helperText=\&#x22;Complete\&#x22; />\n      <ProgressBar label=\&#x22;Warning\&#x22; status=\&#x22;warning\&#x22; value={70} helperText=\&#x22;Storage almost full\&#x22; />\n      <ProgressBar label=\&#x22;Critical\&#x22; status=\&#x22;critical\&#x22; value={30} helperText=\&#x22;Action required\&#x22; />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

* `role="progressbar"` on the container
* `aria-valuenow` reflects the current value
* `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` define the range (default `0`–`100`)
* `aria-valuetext` provides a formatted string (e.g. `"60%"`)
* `aria-labelledby` associates the visible label when the `label` prop is provided

# ProgressSteps



















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* Horizontal and vertical orientations
* Four completion statuses (`none`, `partial`, `complete`, `error`) with status icons
* Timeline (past / current / future) derived from a single `currentStep` prop
* Auto-generated step numbers (opt out with `hideStepNumbers`)
* Interactive (navigable) and inert (display-only) steps
* Title truncation and RTL support
* Rendered as a `<nav>` landmark with an ordered list for assistive technology

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A horizontal stepper. \`currentStep\` marks the active step; earlier steps are \`past\`, later are \`future\`. Each \`status\` sets the step's icon, and an \`error\` step turns its accent bar red.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressSteps, ProgressStep } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <ProgressSteps aria-label=\&#x22;Checkout\&#x22; currentStep={1}>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;complete\&#x22;>Cart</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;partial\&#x22;>Shipping</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;error\&#x22;>Payment</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep>Review</ProgressStep>\n    </ProgressSteps>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Not started [#not-started]

No \`currentStep\`: the flow hasn't started, so every step is \`future\` and none is marked current.

<Story of="NotStartedExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressSteps, ProgressStep } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NotStartedExample() {\n  return (\n    <ProgressSteps aria-label=\&#x22;Checkout\&#x22;>\n      <ProgressStep>Cart</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep>Shipping</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep>Payment</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep>Review</ProgressStep>\n    </ProgressSteps>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Vertical [#vertical]

Vertical orientation: accent bar on the leading edge, steps stacked in a column.

<Story of="VerticalExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressSteps, ProgressStep } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function VerticalExample() {\n  return (\n    <ProgressSteps aria-label=\&#x22;Onboarding\&#x22; orientation=\&#x22;vertical\&#x22; currentStep={1}>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;complete\&#x22;>Create account</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;partial\&#x22;>Verify email</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep>Add payment method</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep>Invite your team</ProgressStep>\n    </ProgressSteps>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Interactive [#interactive]

Interactive steps: each \`onPress\` navigates the wizard by updating \`currentStep\`.

<Story of="InteractiveExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressSteps, ProgressStep } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nconst steps = ['Cart', 'Shipping', 'Payment', 'Review'];\n\nexport function InteractiveExample() {\n  const [currentStep, setCurrentStep] = useState(1);\n\n  return (\n    <ProgressSteps aria-label=\&#x22;Checkout\&#x22; currentStep={currentStep}>\n      {steps.map((label, index) => (\n        <ProgressStep\n          key={label}\n          status={index < currentStep ? 'complete' : index === currentStep ? 'partial' : 'none'}\n          onPress={() => setCurrentStep(index)}\n        >\n          {label}\n        </ProgressStep>\n      ))}\n    </ProgressSteps>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled [#disabled]

A disabled interactive step is muted, not focusable, and cannot be activated.

<Story of="DisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressSteps, ProgressStep } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DisabledExample() {\n  return (\n    <ProgressSteps aria-label=\&#x22;Checkout\&#x22; currentStep={1}>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;complete\&#x22; onPress={() => undefined}>\n        Cart\n      </ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;partial\&#x22; onPress={() => undefined}>\n        Shipping\n      </ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep onPress={() => undefined} isDisabled>\n        Payment\n      </ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep onPress={() => undefined} isDisabled>\n        Review\n      </ProgressStep>\n    </ProgressSteps>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Hide Step Numbers [#hide-step-numbers]

Step numbers are shown by default; \`hideStepNumbers\` omits the "N. " prefix.

<Story of="HideStepNumbersExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ProgressSteps, ProgressStep } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function HideStepNumbersExample() {\n  return (\n    <ProgressSteps aria-label=\&#x22;Checkout\&#x22; currentStep={1} hideStepNumbers>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;complete\&#x22;>Cart</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep status=\&#x22;partial\&#x22;>Shipping</ProgressStep>\n      <ProgressStep>Payment</ProgressStep>\n    </ProgressSteps>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Customization [#customization]

* Step numbers (`"N. "`) are prepended automatically — keep them where possible, as user testing shows people recognize the component better with them. Set `hideStepNumbers` to omit them.
* `orientation` switches between `horizontal` (accent bar on top) and `vertical` (accent bar on the leading edge).
* `currentStep` is the single source of truth for the timeline. Omit it for a not-yet-started flow where every step is `future`; pass the step count for a fully completed flow where every step is `past`.
* `status` is independent of timeline and only controls the status icon and (for `error`) the accent bar color.
* Pass `className` to the container or an individual step to extend the styles.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

* The container renders a `<nav>` landmark; set `aria-label` to name it (defaults to `"Progress"`).
* Steps are an ordered list (`<ol>`/`<li>`) so assistive technology conveys position and count.
* The current step is marked with `aria-current="step"`.
* Interactive steps are real buttons: focusable in the natural **Tab** order and activated with **Enter** or **Space**. Status icons are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
* Focus is shown with a visible outline; disabled steps use `0.4` opacity and are not focusable.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Drive the timeline from `currentStep` rather than styling individual steps.
* Provide `onPress` only for steps a user can actually navigate to; leave it off for display-only steps.
* Keep titles short — they truncate with an ellipsis when space is tight.
* Always give the container an `aria-label` that describes the flow (e.g. `"Checkout progress"`).

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

* **No step is highlighted:** `currentStep` is omitted, negative, or out of range. Set it to the active step's 0-based index.
* **A step isn't clickable:** it has no `onPress`, so it's inert by design. Add `onPress` to make it interactive.
* **Titles overflow:** that's expected — titles truncate. Shorten the title.

## Props [#props]

The `ProgressSteps` component has the following props:

<PropTable />

The `ProgressStep` component has the following props:

<PropTable />

### Form Submission [#form-submission]

A radio group integrated with native form submission.

<Story of="RadioFormExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Radio, RadioGroup } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { type FormEvent, useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function RadioFormExample() {\n  const [submittedValue, setSubmittedValue] = useState<string | null>(null);\n\n  function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {\n    event.preventDefault();\n    const value = new FormData(event.currentTarget).get('plan');\n    setSubmittedValue(value != null ? String(value) : null);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>\n        <RadioGroup name=\&#x22;plan\&#x22; label=\&#x22;Select your plan\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;standard\&#x22;>\n          <Radio value=\&#x22;basic\&#x22;>Basic</Radio>\n          <Radio value=\&#x22;standard\&#x22;>Standard</Radio>\n          <Radio value=\&#x22;premium\&#x22;>Premium</Radio>\n        </RadioGroup>\n        <button type=\&#x22;submit\&#x22; style={{ marginTop: '1rem' }}>\n          Submit\n        </button>\n      </form>\n      {submittedValue && <p>Form submitted with value: {submittedValue}</p>}\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

Components automatically add data attributes for styling different states:

**RadioGroup Container:** `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-orientation`

**Radio Button:** `data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focused`, `data-disabled`

```css
.my-radio-group [data-selected] {
  color: #09757a;
  font-weight: 500;
}

.my-radio-group[data-invalid] {
  border-color: #db1802;
}

.my-radio-group [data-focused] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

.my-radio-group [data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.4;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Pass `className` or `style` to customize a radio field container. Use descendant data-attribute selectors to style the interactive radio state:

```jsx
<RadioGroup label="Select plan" className="custom-radio-group">
  <Radio value="basic" className="custom-radio">
    Basic
  </Radio>
  <Radio value="premium" className="premium-radio">
    Premium
  </Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard Navigation [#keyboard-navigation]

* **Tab**: Moves focus to/from the radio group
* **Arrow Down/Right**: Move to next radio button
* **Arrow Up/Left**: Move to previous radio button
* **Space**: Select the focused radio button

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

* `role="radiogroup"` on the container
* `role="radio"` on each option
* `aria-checked` indicates selection state
* `aria-disabled` for disabled options
* `aria-required` when selection is required
* `aria-invalid` for validation errors

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Selection Not Updating [#selection-not-updating]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: Using both value and defaultValue
<RadioGroup value={value} defaultValue="basic">
  <Radio value="basic">Basic</Radio>
</RadioGroup>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<RadioGroup value={value} onChange={setValue}>
  <Radio value="basic">Basic</Radio>
</RadioGroup>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<RadioGroup defaultValue="basic">
  <Radio value="basic">Basic</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Styling Overrides Not Applying [#styling-overrides-not-applying]

```css
/* ❌ May not have enough specificity */
.my-custom-radio {
  color: red;
}

/* ✅ Use data attributes and className for higher specificity */
.my-radio-group [data-selected] {
  color: red;
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

### Keyboard Navigation Not Working [#keyboard-navigation-not-working]

```css
/* ❌ Don't remove focus outlines without replacement */
[data-focused] {
  outline: none;
}

/* ✅ Provide visible focus indicator */
.my-radio-group [data-focused] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use Radio Buttons [#when-to-use-radio-buttons]

* ✅ When there are 2-7 mutually exclusive options
* ✅ When all options should be visible at once
* ✅ When the decision is important and deserves space
* ❌ For more than 7 options (use Select instead)
* ❌ For binary yes/no choices (use Checkbox or Toggle instead)
* ❌ When space is limited (use Select dropdown)

### Label Guidelines [#label-guidelines]

* Use clear, concise labels
* Keep labels short (1-3 words when possible)
* Place the most common option first
* Ensure labels are descriptive without being verbose

### Validation [#validation]

Always provide clear error messages:

```jsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Select shipping method"
  isRequired
  isInvalid={!selectedShipping}
  errorMessage="Please select a shipping method"
>
  <Radio value="standard">Standard</Radio>
  <Radio value="express">Express</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

The `Radio` component has the following props:

<PropTable />

The `RadioGroup` component has the following props:
