# RangeField





















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* Select one value or render one thumb for each value in an array
* Supports controlled and uncontrolled values with typed change callbacks
* Provides localized value output, endpoint labels, descriptions, and markers
* Integrates with native forms, keyboard, pointer, and touch interaction through React Aria

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Minimal usage with a single value and min/max bounds.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RangeField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <RangeField aria-label=\&#x22;Volume\&#x22; defaultValue={50} minValue={0} maxValue={100} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

Use \`onChange\` for immediate updates and \`onChangeEnd\` for work that should run after interaction finishes.

<Story of="ControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, RangeField } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function ControlledExample() {\n  const [value, setValue] = useState(50);\n  const [committedValue, setCommittedValue] = useState(50);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <RangeField<number>\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Volume\&#x22;\n        value={value}\n        onChange={setValue}\n        onChangeEnd={setCommittedValue}\n        step={10}\n      />\n      <p>Current value: {value}</p>\n      <p>Committed value: {committedValue}</p>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled [#disabled]

Use \`isDisabled\` when the value is visible but unavailable for interaction.

<Story of="DisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RangeField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DisabledExample() {\n  return (\n    <RangeField\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Volume\&#x22;\n      label=\&#x22;Volume\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;This is a description\&#x22;\n      minLabel=\&#x22;Low\&#x22;\n      maxLabel=\&#x22;High\&#x22;\n      defaultValue={50}\n      isDisabled\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Labels [#labels]

Combine an input label, value label, range labels, and helper text when users need additional context.

<Story of="LabelsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RangeField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function LabelsExample() {\n  return (\n    <RangeField\n      label=\&#x22;Price limit\&#x22;\n      defaultValue={50}\n      formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD', maximumFractionDigits: 0 }}\n      valueLabel\n      minLabel=\&#x22;$0\&#x22;\n      maxLabel=\&#x22;$100\&#x22;\n      description=\&#x22;Choose the maximum price.\&#x22;\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Value Display [#value-display]

Use \`valueLabel\` to show formatted values, static context, or output derived from the current slider state.

<Story of="ValueDisplayExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, RangeField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ValueDisplayExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <RangeField\n        label=\&#x22;Monthly budget\&#x22;\n        defaultValue={50}\n        formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'USD', maximumFractionDigits: 0 }}\n        valueLabel\n      />\n      <RangeField label=\&#x22;Storage quota\&#x22; defaultValue={50} valueLabel={<span>Recommended</span>} />\n      <RangeField\n        label=\&#x22;Volume\&#x22;\n        defaultValue={50}\n        valueLabel={function renderValue({ state }) {\n          return `Current: ${state.values[0]}%`;\n        }}\n      />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Markers [#markers]

Use \`markers\` to expose a manageable set of discrete steps for a single value.

<Story of="MarkersExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RangeField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function MarkersExample() {\n  return <RangeField aria-label=\&#x22;Volume\&#x22; defaultValue={50} minValue={0} maxValue={100} step={10} markers />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Range [#range]

Pass a \`number\[]\` to render a range with two thumbs and step markers.

<Story of="RangeExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RangeField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function RangeExample() {\n  return (\n    <RangeField\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Price range\&#x22;\n      defaultValue={[25, 75]}\n      thumbLabels={['Minimum price', 'Maximum price']}\n      minValue={0}\n      maxValue={100}\n      step={25}\n      markers\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Accessible names [#accessible-names]

For a single value, prefer a visible `label`; use `aria-label` only when equivalent visible context already exists.

For an array, provide one descriptive `thumbLabels` entry for every value. Entries are matched by index, so keep them aligned when values are added, removed, or reordered. Describe each thumb's purpose, such as `Lower warning threshold`, rather than its current number.

`thumbNames` configures native form field names and does not provide accessible labels. Likewise, `valueLabel`, `minLabel`, and `maxLabel` are visual context rather than substitutes for accessible naming.

### Keyboard interaction [#keyboard-interaction]

Each thumb follows the React Aria slider keyboard model:

* Tab and Shift+Tab move among thumbs and surrounding controls.
* Arrow Right and Arrow Up increase the focused value by `step`.
* Arrow Left and Arrow Down decrease the focused value by `step`.
* Home and End move the focused thumb to its permitted bounds.
* Page Up and Page Down make larger changes.

Directional behavior follows the user's locale where appropriate. Pointer, touch, and keyboard interaction all use the same scale and constraints.

Markers are decorative and hidden from the accessibility tree. Ensure the field label, thumb labels, bounds, step, and formatted values communicate all required information without relying on marker appearance.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Use an array only when every entry has a clear, independently adjustable meaning.
* Keep `value`, `thumbLabels`, and `thumbNames` aligned by index.
* Use thumb labels that explain purpose instead of repeating the current number.
* Keep array values in a stable semantic order. If crossing or reordering thumbs would make their meaning ambiguous, enforce the appropriate ordering in product state.
* Avoid large value arrays. Every entry creates another focusable control, which increases keyboard effort and cognitive load.
* Set meaningful `minValue`, `maxValue`, and `step` values. The scale should match the precision users actually need.
* Use markers only when there are few enough steps to scan. Tiny steps across a large range can create an excessive number of DOM elements.
* Use `formatOptions` for currency, percentages, measurements, and other locale-sensitive units so values display and announce their meaning.
* Use `description` for persistent guidance and `isRequired` when a value is required.
* Use `isDisabled` when the value should remain visible but unavailable for interaction.
* Use `onChange` for lightweight immediate feedback and `onChangeEnd` for expensive requests, filtering, or calculations.
* Use a text-entry control when exact numeric input is essential. A track is best for exploring or adjusting values within known bounds.

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### A thumb is missing a label or form value [#a-thumb-is-missing-a-label-or-form-value]

Check the same index in `thumbLabels` and `thumbNames`. Each array entry renders a thumb, and its accessible label and form name are read from the corresponding positions. A form name does not replace an accessible label.

### TypeScript reports the wrong callback value type [#typescript-reports-the-wrong-callback-value-type]

Keep the controlled or default value and callback signatures consistent. When inference is unavailable, provide the generic explicitly: `<RangeField<number>>` for a scalar or `<RangeField<number[]>>` for an array.

```tsx
const [targets, setTargets] = useState<number[]>([20, 80]);

<RangeField<number[]>
  label="Target range"
  value={targets}
  onChange={setTargets}
  thumbLabels={['Minimum target', 'Maximum target']}
/>;
```

### The controlled thumbs do not move [#the-controlled-thumbs-do-not-move]

The `value` prop is the source of truth. Update the scalar or array in `onChange` without changing its intended shape. For arrays, return a new array so application state observes the update.

### Values snap unexpectedly [#values-snap-unexpectedly]

Verify that `step` represents the intended interval from `minValue`. Every thumb snaps to valid positions on the same configured scale.

### The final marker is missing [#the-final-marker-is-missing]

Markers begin at `minValue` and appear at complete step positions. `maxValue` receives a marker only when the range is evenly divisible by `step`.

### Markers are crowded or rendering is slow [#markers-are-crowded-or-rendering-is-slow]

Increase `step` or omit `markers`. Large ranges with small steps can produce many decorative elements even when users cannot distinguish them visually.

### The value or endpoint labels are blank [#the-value-or-endpoint-labels-are-blank]

Enable automatic current-value output with `valueLabel={true}` or provide custom content. `minLabel` and `maxLabel` display only explicitly supplied content; neither defaults to a numeric bound or receives `formatOptions`.

### Negative values do not behave as expected [#negative-values-do-not-behave-as-expected]

Negative values are supported. Set a negative `minValue` and ensure every scalar or array value remains within the configured bounds.

### The range configuration is invalid [#the-range-configuration-is-invalid]

Provide finite bounds where `minValue` is less than `maxValue`, a finite `step` greater than zero, and finite values inside the configured range.


# SegmentedController























<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

An uncontrolled segmented controller with a default selection. The component manages its own state internally via \`defaultValue\`.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { SegmentedController, SegmentedControllerItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;View\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</SegmentedControllerItem>\n    </SegmentedController>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

Use \`value\` and \`onSelectionChange\` to fully control the selected segment from parent state.

<Story of="ControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { SegmentedController, SegmentedControllerItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function ControlledExample() {\n  const [selected, setSelected] = useState('week');\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;View\&#x22; value={selected} onSelectionChange={setSelected}>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      </SegmentedController>\n      <p>Current selection: {selected}</p>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Sizes [#sizes]

Three sizes are available: \`sm\`, \`md\` (default), and \`lg\`.

<Story of="SizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, SegmentedController, SegmentedControllerItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>\n      <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;View (small)\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day sm</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week sm</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month sm</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      </SegmentedController>\n\n      <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;View (medium)\&#x22; size=\&#x22;md\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day md</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week md</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month md</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      </SegmentedController>\n\n      <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;View (large)\&#x22; size=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day lg</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week lg</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month lg</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      </SegmentedController>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Icon + Text [#icon--text]

Segments can include an \`Icon\` alongside text for added visual context.

<Story of="IconExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Icon, SegmentedController, SegmentedControllerItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function IconExample() {\n  return (\n    <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;Layout\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;list\&#x22;>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;list\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;bulleted-list\&#x22; />\n        List\n      </SegmentedControllerItem>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;grid\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;grid\&#x22; />\n        Grid\n      </SegmentedControllerItem>\n    </SegmentedController>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Icon Only [#icon-only]

For compact layouts, segments can contain only icons. Provide an \`aria-label\` on each item so screen readers can identify the action.

<Story of="IconOnlyExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Icon, SegmentedController, SegmentedControllerItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function IconOnlyExample() {\n  return (\n    <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;Layout\&#x22;>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;list\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;List view\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;bulleted-list\&#x22; />\n      </SegmentedControllerItem>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;grid\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Grid view\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;grid\&#x22; />\n      </SegmentedControllerItem>\n    </SegmentedController>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Overflow [#overflow]

When the number of options exceeds the width of the container, the component automatically shows scroll buttons to let users navigate. Users can also scroll horizontally to navigate the options.

<Story of="OverflowExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { SegmentedController, SegmentedControllerItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function OverflowExample({ maxWidth = '300px' }: { maxWidth?: string }) {\n  return (\n    <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;Category\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;electronics\&#x22; style={{ maxWidth }}>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;electronics\&#x22;>Electronics</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;clothing\&#x22;>Clothing</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;home\&#x22;>Home</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;sports\&#x22;>Sports</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;toys\&#x22;>Toys</SegmentedControllerItem>\n    </SegmentedController>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### RTL Direction [#rtl-direction]

The segmented controller follows the current layout direction (LTR or RTL), detected automatically from the browser or system settings.

<Story of="RTLExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RTLProvider } from '../../../utils/rtl-locale-provider.tsx';\nimport { OverflowExample } from './overflow.tsx';\n\nexport function RTLExample() {\n  return (\n    <RTLProvider>\n      <OverflowExample />\n    </RTLProvider>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled States [#disabled-states]

Disable the entire group with \`isDisabled\` on the container, or disable individual segments with \`isDisabled\` on specific items.

<Story of="DisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { SegmentedController, SegmentedControllerItem, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DisabledExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>\n      <label>Disabled group</label>\n      <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;Disabled group\&#x22; isDisabled defaultValue=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      </SegmentedController>\n\n      <label>Individual disabled</label>\n      <SegmentedController aria-label=\&#x22;Individual disabled\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;week\&#x22; isDisabled>\n          Week\n        </SegmentedControllerItem>\n        <SegmentedControllerItem value=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</SegmentedControllerItem>\n      </SegmentedController>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

Components automatically add data attributes for styling different states:

**SegmentedController Container:** `data-disabled`

**SegmentedControllerItem:** `data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard Navigation [#keyboard-navigation]

* **Tab**: Moves focus to/from the segmented controller
* **Arrow Left/Right**: Move to next/previous segment
* **Space/Enter**: Select the focused segment

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

* `role="radiogroup"` on the container
* `role="radio"` on each segment
* `aria-checked` indicates selection state
* `aria-disabled` for disabled segments
* `aria-label` required on the container for screen readers

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use a Segmented Controller [#when-to-use-a-segmented-controller]

* When switching between 2-5 related views within the same context
* When all options should be visible at once
* When the selection immediately changes the displayed content

### When Not to Use [#when-not-to-use]

* For more than 5 options (use Tabs or Select instead)
* For form input (use RadioGroup instead)

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# Select





















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* **Label, description, error**: Optional label, helper text, and error message with proper accessibility
* **Single or multiple selection**: Set `selectionMode="multiple"` to allow multiple values
* **Controlled or uncontrolled**: Use `value` and `onChange` for controlled state, or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled
* **Validation states**: Use `isInvalid` with `errorMessage` and `isDisabled` for validation and disabled state
* **Form integration**: Set `name` and the value submits as part of a native `<form>` (multiple values submit as repeated entries)
* **React Aria integration**: Built on React Aria Select for accessibility, keyboard navigation, and typeahead

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Minimal usage with a label and a placeholder.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Select, SelectItem, type SelectProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: Omit<SelectProps<object>, 'children'> = {}) {\n  return (\n    <Select label=\&#x22;Coffee\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Pick a drink\&#x22; description=\&#x22;Select your favorite coffee\&#x22; {...props}>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</SelectItem>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</SelectItem>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</SelectItem>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;americano\&#x22;>Americano</SelectItem>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;mocha\&#x22;>Mocha</SelectItem>\n    </Select>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Select Controlled [#select-controlled]

Use \`value\` and \`onChange\` for controlled state.

<Story of="SelectControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Select, SelectItem, Text, type SelectKey } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SelectControlledExample() {\n  const [value, setValue] = useState<SelectKey | null>('latte');\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <Select label=\&#x22;Coffee\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Pick a drink\&#x22; value={value} onChange={setValue}>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;americano\&#x22;>Americano</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;mocha\&#x22;>Mocha</SelectItem>\n      </Select>\n      <Text>\n        <strong>Value:</strong> {String(value ?? '(none)')}\n      </Text>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Select Multiple [#select-multiple]

Set \`selectionMode="multiple"\` to allow multiple values. \`value\` is an array of keys.

<Story of="SelectMultipleExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Select, SelectItem, Text, type SelectKey } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SelectMultipleExample() {\n  const [value, setValue] = useState<readonly SelectKey[]>(['latte', 'mocha']);\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <Select\n        label=\&#x22;Coffees you like\&#x22;\n        placeholder=\&#x22;Pick one or more\&#x22;\n        selectionMode=\&#x22;multiple\&#x22;\n        value={value}\n        onChange={setValue}\n      >\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;americano\&#x22;>Americano</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;mocha\&#x22;>Mocha</SelectItem>\n      </Select>\n      <Text>\n        <strong>Selected:</strong> {value.length === 0 ? '(none)' : value.join(', ')}\n      </Text>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Select Invalid [#select-invalid]

Use \`isInvalid\` with \`errorMessage\` for validation feedback.

<Story of="SelectInvalidExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Select, SelectItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SelectInvalidExample() {\n  return (\n    <Select label=\&#x22;Coffee\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Pick a drink\&#x22; errorMessage=\&#x22;Please choose a drink\&#x22; isInvalid isRequired>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</SelectItem>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</SelectItem>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</SelectItem>\n    </Select>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Select Disabled [#select-disabled]

Use \`isDisabled\` to prevent interaction.

<Story of="SelectDisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Select, SelectItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SelectDisabledExample() {\n  return (\n    <Select label=\&#x22;Coffee\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;latte\&#x22; isDisabled>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</SelectItem>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</SelectItem>\n      <SelectItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</SelectItem>\n    </Select>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Select Form [#select-form]

Set \`name\` to submit the value with a native \`\<form>\`. Multiple-mode values submit as repeated entries with the same \`name\`.

<Story of="SelectFormExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';\nimport { Box, Button, Flex, Select, SelectItem, Text } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SelectFormExample() {\n  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState<Record<string, string | string[]> | null>(null);\n\n  function handleSubmit(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {\n    event.preventDefault();\n    const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget);\n    const entries: Record<string, string | string[]> = {};\n    for (const [key, value] of data.entries()) {\n      const stringValue = String(value);\n      const existing = entries[key];\n      if (existing === undefined) {\n        entries[key] = stringValue;\n      } else if (Array.isArray(existing)) {\n        entries[key] = [...existing, stringValue];\n      } else {\n        entries[key] = [existing, stringValue];\n      }\n    }\n    setSubmitted(entries);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <Flex as=\&#x22;form\&#x22; direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; onSubmit={handleSubmit}>\n      <Select name=\&#x22;drink\&#x22; label=\&#x22;Drink\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Pick a drink\&#x22; isRequired>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</SelectItem>\n      </Select>\n      <Select name=\&#x22;extras\&#x22; label=\&#x22;Extras\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Pick any extras\&#x22; selectionMode=\&#x22;multiple\&#x22;>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;oat-milk\&#x22;>Oat milk</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;extra-shot\&#x22;>Extra shot</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;vanilla\&#x22;>Vanilla syrup</SelectItem>\n      </Select>\n      <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Button type=\&#x22;submit\&#x22;>Submit</Button>\n        <Button type=\&#x22;reset\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;minimal\&#x22; onPress={() => setSubmitted(null)}>\n          Reset\n        </Button>\n      </Flex>\n      {submitted && (\n        <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n          <Text>\n            <strong>Submitted:</strong> {JSON.stringify(submitted)}\n          </Text>\n        </Box>\n      )}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Sizes [#sizes]

Compare the supported \`md\` and \`sm\` visual sizes.

<Story of="SelectSizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Select, SelectItem } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SelectSizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <Select label=\&#x22;Coffee (md)\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Pick a drink\&#x22;>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</SelectItem>\n      </Select>\n      <Select label=\&#x22;Coffee (sm)\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Pick a drink\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;espresso\&#x22;>Espresso</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;latte\&#x22;>Latte</SelectItem>\n        <SelectItem id=\&#x22;cappuccino\&#x22;>Cappuccino</SelectItem>\n      </Select>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

# Switch





















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* Renders a horizontal toggle with a sliding thumb inside a pill-shaped track
* Communicates state to assistive technologies via the WAI-ARIA `switch` role
* Toggles on click or tap anywhere in the control — track, thumb, or label
* Toggles with the `Space` key when focused
* Optional label, positioned at the `start` or `end` of the track, or omitted entirely
* Two sizes: `md` (default) and `sm`
* Supports controlled (`isSelected` + `onChange`) and uncontrolled (`defaultSelected`) usage
* Takes effect immediately — no form submission required

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

An uncontrolled switch, off by default, with the label at the start.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Switch } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <Switch>Wi-Fi</Switch>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Switch Selected [#switch-selected]

A switch that starts in the on state via \`defaultSelected\`.

<Story of="SwitchSelectedExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Switch } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SwitchSelectedExample() {\n  return <Switch defaultSelected>Wi-Fi</Switch>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Switch Sizes [#switch-sizes]

The \`size\` prop accepts \`md\` (default) or \`sm\`.

<Story of="SwitchSizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Switch } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SwitchSizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <Switch size=\&#x22;md\&#x22; defaultSelected>\n        Medium\n      </Switch>\n      <Switch size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; defaultSelected>\n        Small\n      </Switch>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Switch Label Position [#switch-label-position]

The \`labelPosition\` prop places the label at the \`start\` or \`end\` of the track.

<Story of="SwitchLabelPositionExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Switch } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SwitchLabelPositionExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <Switch labelPosition=\&#x22;start\&#x22; defaultSelected>\n        Label on the start\n      </Switch>\n      <Switch labelPosition=\&#x22;end\&#x22; defaultSelected>\n        Label on the end\n      </Switch>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### No Label [#no-label]

When no label is provided, pass \`aria-label\` so the switch has an accessible name.

<Story of="SwitchNoLabelExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Switch } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SwitchNoLabelExample() {\n  return <Switch aria-label=\&#x22;Wi-Fi\&#x22; />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Switch Disabled [#switch-disabled]

A disabled switch prevents interaction and renders at reduced opacity, whether off or on.

<Story of="SwitchDisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Switch } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SwitchDisabledExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <Switch isDisabled>Disabled off</Switch>\n      <Switch isDisabled defaultSelected>\n        Disabled on\n      </Switch>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Switch Controlled [#switch-controlled]

Manage switch state programmatically with \`isSelected\` and \`onChange\`.

<Story of="SwitchControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Switch } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function SwitchControlledExample() {\n  const [isSelected, setIsSelected] = useState(false);\n\n  return (\n    <Switch isSelected={isSelected} onChange={setIsSelected}>\n      Wi-Fi\n    </Switch>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

The interactive switch control exposes data attributes for styling different states:

`data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focused`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, `data-size`

```css
.my-switch [data-focus-visible] {
  outline: 2px solid Highlight;
}

.my-switch [data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.4;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Design Tokens [#design-tokens]

The track and thumb read from Antares curated tokens, falling back to legacy `--ux-*` custom properties:

| Element           | Token                               | Legacy fallback |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Track (off)       | —                                   | `--ux-1m9ys0v`  |
| Track (on)        | `--color-input-background-selected` | `--ux-sywk25`   |
| Thumb             | `--color-input-background-default`  | `--ux-1nu8itt`  |
| Thumb inset       | —                                   | `--ux-1sbfig8`  |
| Label             | `--color-input-text-default`        | `--ux-1glcx6s`  |
| Focus ring radius | —                                   | `--ux-zvaw3s`   |

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Pass a `className` or `style` to customize the field container. Target the interactive descendant's data attributes for state-based styling:

```jsx
<Switch className="custom-switch">Wi-Fi</Switch>
```

Use the interactive root data attributes for state-based customization. The track and thumb are internal implementation details and do not expose class-name hooks.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

* Renders with the WAI-ARIA `switch` role via the native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`
* `Space` toggles the switch when it has focus
* Displays a visible focus ring (`outline: 2px solid Highlight`) for keyboard focus
* Disabled switches render at `40%` opacity and are excluded from tab order
* When `children` is omitted, provide `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` so the switch has an accessible name

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use Switch [#when-to-use-switch]

* ✅ For settings that take effect immediately, without a form submission
* ✅ For binary on/off preferences (e.g. Wi-Fi, notifications, dark mode)
* ❌ For selections that require a "Save" or "Submit" action (use `Checkbox` instead)
* ❌ For choosing one of several mutually exclusive options (use `Radio` or `SegmentedController` instead)

### Labeling [#labeling]

* Prefer a visible label that names the setting being toggled (e.g. "Wi-Fi", not "On/Off")
* If the label is omitted, always provide `aria-label`
* Keep labels short and describe the setting, not its current state

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Controlled State Not Updating [#controlled-state-not-updating]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: isSelected without onChange leaves the switch stuck
<Switch isSelected={isOn}>Wi-Fi</Switch>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<Switch isSelected={isOn} onChange={setIsOn}>Wi-Fi</Switch>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<Switch defaultSelected>Wi-Fi</Switch>
```

### Missing Accessible Name [#missing-accessible-name]

```jsx
// ❌ No children and no aria-label — screen readers announce nothing useful
<Switch />

// ✅ Provide a label
<Switch>Wi-Fi</Switch>

// ✅ Or an aria-label when the label is visual-only elsewhere
<Switch aria-label="Wi-Fi" />
```

## Props [#props]

The `Switch` component has the following props:

# Tag





















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A minimal tag with the default emphasis and size.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Tag, type TagProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: Partial<TagProps>) {\n  return <Tag {...props}>Tag</Tag>;\n}&#x22;" />

### Emphasis [#emphasis]

Nine emphasis options are available. Choose the one that fits the visual tone of your context.

<Story of="EmphasesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Tag } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst emphases = [\n  'passive',\n  'critical',\n  'warning',\n  'success',\n  'info',\n  'highlight',\n  'premium',\n  'internal',\n  'neutral'\n] as const;\n\nexport function EmphasesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      {emphases.map((emphasis) => (\n        <Tag key={emphasis} emphasis={emphasis}>\n          {emphasis}\n        </Tag>\n      ))}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Sizes [#sizes]

Choose a size that fits the surrounding content. Smaller tags work well in compact layouts like tables; larger tags suit headings or hero sections.

<Story of="SizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Tag } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      <Tag size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; emphasis=\&#x22;info\&#x22;>\n        Small\n      </Tag>\n      <Tag size=\&#x22;md\&#x22; emphasis=\&#x22;info\&#x22;>\n        Medium\n      </Tag>\n      <Tag size=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; emphasis=\&#x22;info\&#x22;>\n        Large\n      </Tag>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Inline [#inline]

Use \`design="inline"\` to embed a tag within a sentence. The background and border are removed so the tag blends into the text flow.

<Story of="InlineExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Tag } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function InlineExample() {\n  return (\n    <p>\n      This domain is{' '}\n      <Tag emphasis=\&#x22;success\&#x22; design=\&#x22;inline\&#x22;>\n        Active\n      </Tag>{' '}\n      and your plan is{' '}\n      <Tag emphasis=\&#x22;premium\&#x22; design=\&#x22;inline\&#x22;>\n        Pro\n      </Tag>\n      .\n    </p>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### High Contrast [#high-contrast]

A bolder color treatment for when tags need to stand out more - for example, on colored backgrounds.

<Story of="HighContrastExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Tag } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst emphases = [\n  'passive',\n  'critical',\n  'warning',\n  'success',\n  'info',\n  'highlight',\n  'premium',\n  'internal',\n  'neutral'\n] as const;\n\nexport function HighContrastExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      {emphases.map((emphasis) => (\n        <Tag key={emphasis} emphasis={emphasis} highContrast>\n          {emphasis}\n        </Tag>\n      ))}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### With Icon [#with-icon]

Icons reinforce the tag's meaning at a glance. Add an \`Icon\` as a child - it inherits the tag's color and scales with its size.

<Story of="IconsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Icon, Tag } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function IconsExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      <Tag emphasis=\&#x22;critical\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;alert\&#x22; aria-hidden=\&#x22;true\&#x22; />\n        Critical\n      </Tag>\n      <Tag emphasis=\&#x22;success\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;checkmark\&#x22; aria-hidden=\&#x22;true\&#x22; />\n        Success\n      </Tag>\n      <Tag emphasis=\&#x22;warning\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;alert\&#x22; aria-hidden=\&#x22;true\&#x22; />\n        Warning\n      </Tag>\n      <Tag emphasis=\&#x22;info\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;information\&#x22; aria-hidden=\&#x22;true\&#x22; />\n        Info\n      </Tag>\n      <Tag emphasis=\&#x22;highlight\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;star\&#x22; aria-hidden=\&#x22;true\&#x22; />\n        Highlight\n      </Tag>\n      <Tag emphasis=\&#x22;premium\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;diamond\&#x22; aria-hidden=\&#x22;true\&#x22; />\n        Premium\n      </Tag>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Indicator [#indicator]

A minimal style that pairs a small colored dot with a neutral background. Well suited for dense layouts like tables or dashboards where multiple tags in close proximity would otherwise compete for attention.

<Story of="IndicatorExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, Tag } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst emphases = [\n  'passive',\n  'critical',\n  'warning',\n  'success',\n  'info',\n  'highlight',\n  'premium',\n  'internal',\n  'neutral'\n] as const;\n\nexport function IndicatorExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      {emphases.map((emphasis) => (\n        <Tag key={emphasis} emphasis={emphasis} indicator>\n          {emphasis}\n        </Tag>\n      ))}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Screen readers [#screen-readers]

Tags are `<span>` elements with no special ARIA role. Screen readers announce the tag's text as part of normal page content — no extra markup is needed.

### Decorative icons [#decorative-icons]

Icons passed as children must include `aria-hidden="true"` so they are skipped by screen readers. The text label is the sole carrier of meaning.

```tsx
<Tag emphasis="critical">
  <Icon icon="alert" aria-hidden="true" />
  Expired
</Tag>
```

### Indicator dot [#indicator-dot]

The colored dot is decorative and invisible to screen readers. The text label must convey the status on its own — never rely on the dot alone to communicate meaning.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Use the indicator style in dense layouts like tables and dashboards. Use the filled style when the tag is a prominent, standalone element on a card or hero section.
* Default to the small size in compact layouts like tables and lists. Use medium or large only when the tag needs to stand out as a primary piece of information.
* Use the inline design only within running prose. In grouped or standalone contexts, the filled style provides better visual separation.
* Do not stack multiple tags of different emphasis on the same item. Choose the most important one — too many competing labels lose their meaning.

## When to Use [#when-to-use]

* Showing the status of an item on a card, table row, or list entry (e.g. "Active", "Expired", "Pending")
* Categorizing or grouping content so users can scan and filter quickly (e.g. "New", "Sale", "Beta")
* Surfacing metadata about an item (e.g. "Pro", "Free trial", "Internal")
* Communicating priority or category in project management and collaboration tools (e.g. "High priority", "In review")

## When Not to Use [#when-not-to-use]

* If users need to click or dismiss it — use a **Button** instead.
* If the label is part of a sentence with no visual distinction — just use text.

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# Text

















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

The `Text` component prepares content with a few properties.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Basic text content.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Text, type TextProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(args: TextProps) {\n  return <Text {...args}>Hello, world!</Text>;\n}&#x22;" />

### As [#as]

Setting the \`as\` prop allows you to change the HTML tag of the \`Text\` component.

<Story of="AsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Text, type TextProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function AsExample(args: TextProps) {\n  return (\n    <Text {...args} as=\&#x22;marquee\&#x22;>\n      A scrolling marquee\n    </Text>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Align [#align]

Setting the \`align\` prop allows you to change the alignment of the text. Choose from \`start\`, \`center\`, \`end\`, or \`justify\`; the logical keywords support RTL languages.

<Story of="AlignExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Text, type TextProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function AlignExample(args: TextProps) {\n  return (\n    <Text {...args} as=\&#x22;p\&#x22; align=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      Text is aligned to the center\n    </Text>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Max Lines [#max-lines]

Setting the \`maxLines\` prop limits the number of displayed lines using an ellipsis.

<Story of="MaxLinesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Text, type TextProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function MaxLinesExample(args: TextProps) {\n  return (\n    <div style={{ width: '300px', border: '1px solid red' }}>\n      <Text {...args} as=\&#x22;p\&#x22; maxLines={2}>\n        This will have a maximum of two lines. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod\n        tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.\n      </Text>\n    </div>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Wrap [#wrap]

Setting the \`wrap\` prop controls text wrapping with values such as \`wrap\`, \`nowrap\`, \`balance\`, \`pretty\`, or \`stable\`.

<Story of="WrapExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Text, type TextProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function WrapExample(args: TextProps) {\n  return (\n    <div style={{ width: '300px', border: '1px solid red' }}>\n      <Text {...args} as=\&#x22;p\&#x22; wrap=\&#x22;pretty\&#x22;>\n        Text is wrapped in a way that best balances the number of characters on each line, enhancing layout quality and\n        legibility. Because counting characters and balancing them across multiple lines is computationally expensive,\n        this value is only supported for blocks of text spanning a limited number of lines\n      </Text>\n    </div>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

# TextField





















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* **Label, description, error**: Optional label, helper text, and error message with proper accessibility
* **Adornments**: Optional `leadingText` and `trailingText` for fixed text before or after the input (e.g. `$`, `.00`, `px`)
* **Controlled or uncontrolled**: Use `value` and `onChange` for controlled state, or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled
* **Multiline**: Set `multiline` to render a textarea instead of a single-line input
* **Validation states**: Use `isInvalid` with `errorMessage` and `isDisabled` for validation and disabled state
* **React Aria integration**: Built on React Aria TextField for accessibility and behavior

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Minimal usage with label and placeholder.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { TextField, type TextFieldProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: TextFieldProps) {\n  return <TextField label=\&#x22;Name\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Enter your name\&#x22; {...props} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Text Field Controlled [#text-field-controlled]

Use \`value\` and \`onChange\` for controlled state.

<Story of="TextFieldControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { Text, TextField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TextFieldControlledExample() {\n  const [value, setValue] = useState('');\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <TextField label=\&#x22;Email\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;you@example.com\&#x22; value={value} onChange={setValue} />\n      <Text>\n        <strong>Value:</strong> {value || '(empty)'}\n      </Text>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Text Field Invalid [#text-field-invalid]

Use \`isInvalid\` with \`errorMessage\` for validation feedback.

<Story of="TextFieldInvalidExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { TextField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TextFieldInvalidExample() {\n  return (\n    <TextField\n      label=\&#x22;Email\&#x22;\n      placeholder=\&#x22;you@example.com\&#x22;\n      errorMessage=\&#x22;Please enter a valid email address\&#x22;\n      isInvalid\n      isRequired\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Text Field Disabled [#text-field-disabled]

Use \`isDisabled\` to prevent input.

<Story of="TextFieldDisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { TextField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TextFieldDisabledExample() {\n  return <TextField label=\&#x22;Name\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Enter your name\&#x22; defaultValue=\&#x22;Disabled value\&#x22; isDisabled />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Text Field Adornments [#text-field-adornments]

Use \`leadingText\` and \`trailingText\` for fixed text before and after the input, such as currency.

<Story of="TextFieldAdornmentsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { TextField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TextFieldAdornmentsExample() {\n  return (\n    <TextField\n      description=\&#x22;Use leadingText and trailingText to show fixed text before and after the input (e.g. currency).\&#x22;\n      label=\&#x22;Amount\&#x22;\n      leadingText=\&#x22;$\&#x22;\n      placeholder=\&#x22;0.00\&#x22;\n      trailingText=\&#x22;.00\&#x22;\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Text Field Multiline [#text-field-multiline]

Use \`multiline\` to render a textarea.

<Story of="TextFieldMultilineExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { TextField, type TextFieldProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TextFieldMultilineExample(props: TextFieldProps) {\n  return <TextField label=\&#x22;Comment\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;Enter your comment\&#x22; multiline {...props} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Sizes [#sizes]

Compare the supported \`md\` and \`sm\` visual sizes.

<Story of="TextFieldSizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, TextField } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TextFieldSizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <TextField label=\&#x22;Email (md)\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;you@example.com\&#x22; />\n      <TextField label=\&#x22;Email (sm)\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;you@example.com\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />
