# ToggleButton

























<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A \`ToggleButton\` toggles between selected and unselected. Wrap multiple inside a \`ToggleButtonGroup\` to link them with shared selection and keyboard navigation.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ToggleButtonGroup, ToggleButton } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return (\n    <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label=\&#x22;View\&#x22; defaultSelectedKeys={['day']} selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</ToggleButton>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week</ToggleButton>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</ToggleButton>\n    </ToggleButtonGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Multiple Selection [#multiple-selection]

Use \`selectionMode="multiple"\` to allow more than one item to be active at a time.

<Story of="MultipleSelectionExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ToggleButtonGroup, ToggleButton } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function MultipleSelectionExample() {\n  return (\n    <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label=\&#x22;Text formatting\&#x22; selectionMode=\&#x22;multiple\&#x22; defaultSelectedKeys={['bold']}>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;bold\&#x22;>Bold</ToggleButton>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;italic\&#x22;>Italic</ToggleButton>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;underline\&#x22;>Underline</ToggleButton>\n    </ToggleButtonGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Controlled [#controlled]

Use \`selectedKeys\` and \`onSelectionChange\` to control selection from parent state.

<Story of="ControlledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ToggleButtonGroup, ToggleButton } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nexport function ControlledExample() {\n  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set(['week']));\n\n  return (\n    <>\n      <ToggleButtonGroup\n        aria-label=\&#x22;View\&#x22;\n        selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;\n        selectedKeys={selected}\n        onSelectionChange={(keys) => setSelected(keys as Set<string>)}\n      >\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</ToggleButton>\n      </ToggleButtonGroup>\n      <p>Current selection: {Array.from(selected).join(', ')}</p>\n    </>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Disabled States [#disabled-states]

Disable the entire group with \`isDisabled\` on the container, or disable individual items with \`isDisabled\` on specific \`ToggleButton\` elements.

<Story of="DisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ToggleButtonGroup, ToggleButton, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DisabledExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>\n      <label>Disabled group</label>\n      <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label=\&#x22;Disabled group\&#x22; isDisabled defaultSelectedKeys={['day']} selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</ToggleButton>\n      </ToggleButtonGroup>\n\n      <label>Individual disabled item</label>\n      <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label=\&#x22;Individual disabled\&#x22; defaultSelectedKeys={['day']} selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;week\&#x22; isDisabled>\n          Week\n        </ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</ToggleButton>\n      </ToggleButtonGroup>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Sizes [#sizes]

Two sizes are available: \`sm\` and \`md\` (default).

<Story of="SizesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ToggleButtonGroup, ToggleButton, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SizesExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;start\&#x22;>\n      <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label=\&#x22;Size sm\&#x22; size=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; defaultSelectedKeys={['day']} selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</ToggleButton>\n      </ToggleButtonGroup>\n\n      <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label=\&#x22;Size md\&#x22; size=\&#x22;md\&#x22; defaultSelectedKeys={['day']} selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;day\&#x22;>Day</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;week\&#x22;>Week</ToggleButton>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;month\&#x22;>Month</ToggleButton>\n      </ToggleButtonGroup>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Icon + Text [#icon--text]

Items can include an \`Icon\` alongside text for added visual context.

<Story of="IconAndTextExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ToggleButtonGroup, ToggleButton, Icon } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function IconAndTextExample() {\n  return (\n    <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label=\&#x22;Layout\&#x22; defaultSelectedKeys={['list']} selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;list\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;bulleted-list\&#x22; />\n        List\n      </ToggleButton>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;grid\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;grid\&#x22; />\n        Grid\n      </ToggleButton>\n    </ToggleButtonGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Icon Only [#icon-only]

For compact layouts, items can contain only icons. Always provide an \`aria-label\` on each icon-only item.

<Story of="IconOnlyExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { ToggleButtonGroup, ToggleButton, Icon } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function IconOnlyExample() {\n  return (\n    <ToggleButtonGroup aria-label=\&#x22;Layout\&#x22; defaultSelectedKeys={['list']} selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;list\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;List view\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;bulleted-list\&#x22; />\n      </ToggleButton>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;grid\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Grid view\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;grid\&#x22; />\n      </ToggleButton>\n    </ToggleButtonGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### With Dropdown [#with-dropdown]

Wrap a \`ToggleButton\` in a \`MenuTrigger\` to add sub-options to a group item.

<Story of="WithDropdownExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useState } from 'react';\nimport { ToggleButtonGroup, ToggleButton, Icon, Menu, MenuItem, MenuTrigger } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\ntype Alignment = 'left' | 'center' | 'right';\n\nconst ALIGNMENT_ICONS: Record<Alignment, string> = {\n  left: 'align-left',\n  center: 'align-center',\n  right: 'align-right'\n};\n\nconst ALIGNMENT_LABELS: Record<Alignment, string> = {\n  left: 'Align Left',\n  center: 'Align Center',\n  right: 'Align Right'\n};\n\nexport function WithDropdownExample() {\n  const [formatting, setFormatting] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set());\n  const [[alignment], setAlignment] = useState<Set<Alignment>>(new Set(['left']));\n\n  return (\n    <ToggleButtonGroup\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Text formatting\&#x22;\n      selectionMode=\&#x22;multiple\&#x22;\n      selectedKeys={formatting}\n      onSelectionChange={(keys) => setFormatting(new Set([...(keys as Set<string>)].filter((k) => k !== 'align')))}\n    >\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;bold\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Bold\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;bold\&#x22; />\n      </ToggleButton>\n      <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;italic\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Italic\&#x22;>\n        <Icon icon=\&#x22;italic\&#x22; />\n      </ToggleButton>\n\n      <MenuTrigger>\n        <ToggleButton id=\&#x22;align\&#x22; aria-label={ALIGNMENT_LABELS[alignment]}>\n          <Icon icon={ALIGNMENT_ICONS[alignment]} />\n          <Icon icon=\&#x22;chevron-down\&#x22; />\n        </ToggleButton>\n        <Menu\n          selectionMode=\&#x22;single\&#x22;\n          selectedKeys={[alignment]}\n          onSelectionChange={(keys) => setAlignment(new Set([...(keys as Set<Alignment>)]))}\n        >\n          <MenuItem id=\&#x22;left\&#x22;>{ALIGNMENT_LABELS.left}</MenuItem>\n          <MenuItem id=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>{ALIGNMENT_LABELS.center}</MenuItem>\n          <MenuItem id=\&#x22;right\&#x22;>{ALIGNMENT_LABELS.right}</MenuItem>\n        </Menu>\n      </MenuTrigger>\n    </ToggleButtonGroup>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### RTL Direction [#rtl-direction]

The group follows the document's layout direction, detected automatically from the browser locale.

<Story of="RTLExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RTLProvider } from '../../../utils/rtl-locale-provider.tsx';\nimport { DefaultExample } from './default.tsx';\n\nexport function RTLExample() {\n  return (\n    <RTLProvider>\n      <DefaultExample />\n    </RTLProvider>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

Components automatically add data attributes for styling different states:

**ToggleButtonGroup Container:** `data-size`

**ToggleButton Item:** `data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`

```css
.my-toggle-group [data-selected] {
  background-color: #09757a;
  color: #fff;
}

.my-toggle-group [data-focus-visible] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

.my-toggle-group [data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.4;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Individual components can be styled by passing `className` props:

```jsx
<ToggleButtonGroup aria-label="View" className="custom-toggle-group">
  <ToggleButton id="list" className="custom-item">List</ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton id="grid" className="custom-item">Grid</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButtonGroup>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard Navigation [#keyboard-navigation]

| Key                    | Action                                                       |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Tab**                | Moves focus to/from the button group (single tab stop)       |
| **Arrow Left / Right** | Move focus between items (RAC automatically reverses in RTL) |
| **Space / Enter**      | Toggle the focused item                                      |
| **Home**               | Move focus to the first item                                 |
| **End**                | Move focus to the last item                                  |

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

* `selectionMode="single"` → `role="radiogroup"` on container, `role="radio"` + `aria-checked` per item
* `selectionMode="multiple"` → `role="toolbar"` on container, `role="button"` + `aria-pressed` per item
* `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) is required on the group container
* Icon-only items require `aria-label` on each `ToggleButton`

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Selection Not Updating [#selection-not-updating]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: Using both selectedKeys and defaultSelectedKeys
<ToggleButtonGroup selectedKeys={keys} defaultSelectedKeys={['day']}>
  <ToggleButton id="day">Day</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButtonGroup>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<ToggleButtonGroup selectedKeys={keys} onSelectionChange={setKeys}>
  <ToggleButton id="day">Day</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButtonGroup>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<ToggleButtonGroup defaultSelectedKeys={['day']}>
  <ToggleButton id="day">Day</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButtonGroup>
```

### Styling Overrides Not Applying [#styling-overrides-not-applying]

```css
/* ❌ May not have enough specificity */
.my-custom-item {
  background-color: red;
}

/* ✅ Use data attributes with className for higher specificity */
.my-toggle-group [data-selected] {
  background-color: red;
}
```

### Keyboard Navigation Not Working [#keyboard-navigation-not-working]

```css
/* ❌ Don't remove focus outlines without replacement */
[data-focus-visible] {
  outline: none;
}

/* ✅ Provide visible focus indicator */
.my-toggle-group [data-focus-visible] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use [#when-to-use]

* ✅ For grouped contextual actions — two or more closely related actions that belong together (e.g. Bold / Italic / Underline, Align Left / Center / Right)
* ✅ For compact action grouping — related actions in space-constrained layouts (e.g. Undo / Redo, Zoom In / Out / Reset)
* ✅ For multi-select scenarios — when users need to select multiple options simultaneously
* ❌ For unrelated actions that perform disconnected tasks without shared context
* ❌ For more than 5 choices — cognitive overload; consider a **Select** instead
* ❌ When actions require strong visual distinction (e.g. Save vs. Delete)
* ❌ When selecting an option leads to a different page or workflow — use navigation instead
* ❌ For mutually exclusive content views (e.g. Monthly / Yearly) — use **SegmentedController** instead

### Keep Variants Consistent [#keep-variants-consistent]

Avoid mixing different content types (text-only, icon-only, icon+text) within the same group. Mixing styles creates visual noise and makes the set feel fragmented rather than unified.

### Balance Label Lengths [#balance-label-lengths]

Keep button labels of similar length. Large differences in text length cause irregular button widths and make the group appear uneven. Prefer short, concise wording.

### Alignment [#alignment]

Align the group to reflect its relationship to surrounding content:

* **Left** — when the group controls content directly below or within the same column (dashboards, tables).
* **Center** — when the group acts as a prominent toggle affecting an entire section or page.
* **Right** — when the group represents utility or contextual controls (e.g. grid/list view toggle).

### Label Guidelines [#label-guidelines]

* Use **title case**: capitalize the first letter of each word, except short prepositions.
* Keep labels to one or two words. Omit articles (a, an, the) and filler words.
* Prefer action-focused or descriptive language that communicates the option instantly.

### Icon-Only Items [#icon-only-items]

Use icon-only items only when the icon's meaning is universally recognized. Always provide an `aria-label` on each icon-only `ToggleButton`:

```tsx
<ToggleButton id="list" aria-label="List view">
  <Icon icon="bulleted-list" />
</ToggleButton>
```

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# Tooltip











<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

Tooltips appear after a short delay when hovering, and immediately when the element receives focus.
Once a tooltip has been shown, subsequent tooltips appear without delay.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Use it with \`TooltipTrigger\`, which wraps both the tooltip content and a focusable element such as a \`Button\`. The tooltip appears on hover and focus.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, Button, type TooltipTriggerProps, type TooltipProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: {\n  tooltipTriggerProps?: Partial<TooltipTriggerProps>;\n  tooltipProps?: Partial<TooltipProps>;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <TooltipTrigger {...props.tooltipTriggerProps}>\n      <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Hover me</Button>\n      <Tooltip {...props.tooltipProps}>This is the tooltip content!</Tooltip>\n    </TooltipTrigger>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Custom Anchor [#custom-anchor]

To position a tooltip relative to a different focusable element, use the \`triggerRef\` prop. \`TooltipTrigger\` still handles showing and hiding on hover and focus.

<Story of="CustomAnchorExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, Box, Flex, Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { useRef } from 'react';\n\nexport function CustomAnchorExample() {\n  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      <TooltipTrigger>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Hover me</Button>\n        <Tooltip triggerRef={triggerRef}>Tooltip positioned relative to the box</Tooltip>\n      </TooltipTrigger>\n\n      <Box elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; ref={triggerRef}>\n        Tooltip appears here\n      </Box>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key    | Description                                                |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab    | Moves focus to the focusable element and shows the tooltip |
| Escape | Closes the tooltip                                         |

### ARIA [#aria]

* The tooltip uses `role="tooltip"` and is associated with its focusable element via `aria-describedby`.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

* Keep tooltip content short and informative.
* Tooltips are not shown on touch screen interactions. Ensure your UI is usable without tooltips.
* Do not place interactive content inside tooltips. Use a `Popover` instead.

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# DonutChart

















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

You give the chart a \`data\` array (\`id\`, \`name\`, \`value\`) and a \`label\` in the middle - this is the everyday setup when you want several categories on one ring and a headline number or title in the hole.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DonutChart, type DonutChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst data = [\n  { id: '1', name: 'Category A', value: 35 },\n  { id: '2', name: 'Category B', value: 25 },\n  { id: '3', name: 'Category C', value: 18 },\n  { id: '4', name: 'Category D', value: 12 },\n  { id: '5', name: 'Category E', value: 10 }\n];\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: Partial<DonutChartProps>) {\n  return <DonutChart data={data} label=\&#x22;100%\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Donut chart with five categories\&#x22; {...props} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Single slice [#single-slice]

When there is only one slice, the ring is full. Add \`subLabel\` if you want a smaller second line under the main center text.

<Story of="SingleSliceExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DonutChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SingleSliceExample() {\n  return (\n    <DonutChart\n      data={[{ id: 'only', name: 'Total', value: 100 }]}\n      label=\&#x22;$1,000\&#x22;\n      subLabel=\&#x22;Sub label\&#x22;\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Donut chart with a single full ring\&#x22;\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Legend placement [#legend-placement]

Switch \`legend\` to \`right\` to sit the legend beside the donut, or \`bottom\` to stack it underneath. \`legendLabel\` is there when you want a title above the legend items.

<Story of="LegendLayoutExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DonutChart, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst data = [\n  { id: '1', name: 'Product A', value: 40 },\n  { id: '2', name: 'Product B', value: 30 },\n  { id: '3', name: 'Product C', value: 20 },\n  { id: '4', name: 'Product D', value: 10 }\n];\n\nexport function LegendLayoutExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;xl\&#x22;>\n      <DonutChart\n        data={data}\n        label=\&#x22;100%\&#x22;\n        legend=\&#x22;right\&#x22;\n        legendLabel=\&#x22;Legend title\&#x22;\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Donut with legend to the right\&#x22;\n      />\n      <DonutChart\n        data={data}\n        label=\&#x22;100%\&#x22;\n        legend=\&#x22;bottom\&#x22;\n        legendLabel=\&#x22;Legend title\&#x22;\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Donut with legend below\&#x22;\n      />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Small slices [#small-slices]

Very thin slices can be noisy to hover. Anything at or below \`smallSliceThreshold\` (default \`0.05\` of the total) is treated as “small,” and if those slices sit next to each other on the ring, one hover opens a single tooltip that lists the whole group.

<Story of="SmallSlicesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DonutChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\n/** Two large slices with two separate clusters of small slices — hover a small slice to see only that adjacent group (A–C or E–G) in the tooltip. */\nconst data = [\n  { id: 'main', name: 'Primary', value: 88 },\n  { id: 'a', name: 'Slice A', value: 3 },\n  { id: 'b', name: 'Slice B', value: 3 },\n  { id: 'c', name: 'Slice C', value: 3 },\n  { id: 'd', name: 'Slice D', value: 90 },\n  { id: 'e', name: 'Slice E', value: 5 },\n  { id: 'f', name: 'Slice F', value: 4 },\n  { id: 'g', name: 'Slice G', value: 3 }\n];\n\nexport function SmallSlicesExample() {\n  return <DonutChart data={data} label=\&#x22;88%\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Donut with small slices for combined tooltip\&#x22; />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Format value [#format-value]

Use \`formatValue\` when the raw numbers in the tooltip should read like money, counts with separators, or whatever your product expects. The percentage of the total still formats on its own; your function only shapes the value column.

<Story of="FormatValueExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { DonutChart, type DonutChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nconst data = [\n  { id: '1', name: 'Sales', value: 42 },\n  { id: '2', name: 'Services', value: 35 },\n  { id: '3', name: 'Support', value: 23 }\n];\n\nexport function FormatValueExample(props: Partial<DonutChartProps>) {\n  return (\n    <DonutChart\n      data={data}\n      label=\&#x22;$100.00\&#x22;\n      formatValue={function format(v: number) {\n        return `$${v}.00`;\n      }}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Donut with formatted tooltip values for multiple revenue categories\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# Bar Chart























<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

* **Single and multi-series support**: Display one or multiple data series with grouped bars
* **Vertical and horizontal orientations**: Choose the best layout for your data and use case
* **Responsive behavior**: Auto-sizing with horizontal scrolling for many data points, sticky axes
* **Design system alignment**: 8px border radius, 12px bar width (1.5 GU), consistent spacing
* **Interactive tooltips**: Hover to see exact values, with smart positioning and scroll-awareness
* **Customizable axes**: Control gridlines, tick marks, axis titles, and tick formatting
* **Custom domains**: Set explicit x and y ranges for controlled scales across multiple charts
* **RTL support*&#x2A;: Full right-to-left layout support for international audiences &#x2A;(in development)*
* **Accessibility ready**: Keyboard navigation, screen reader support, and semantic HTML
* **TypeScript support**: Fully typed with comprehensive prop interfaces
* **VisX integration**: Leverages VisX primitives for scales, axes, shapes, and responsive layout

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

You give the chart a \`series\` array plus \`xAccessor\` and \`yAccessor\` so it knows which field is the category and which is the value - this is the everyday setup for one set of vertical bars.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: any) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'new-york-series',\n      name: 'New York',\n      data: cityTemperature.slice(0, 10)\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <BarChart\n      series={series}\n      xAccessor={(d: any) => d.date}\n      yAccessor={(d: any) => d['New York']}\n      xAxisTitle=\&#x22;Date\&#x22;\n      yAxisTitle=\&#x22;Temperature (°F)\&#x22;\n      xBaseline={true}\n      yBaseline={true}\n      xTickMarks={true}\n      yTickMarks={true}\n      yGridlines={true}\n      xGridlines={true}\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Multi-series [#multi-series]

Pass more than one entry in \`series\` and the bars group by category, with a legend naming each series. Use it when the comparison between series matters as much as the values themselves.

<Story of="MultiSeriesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\n\nexport function MultiSeriesExample(props: any) {\n  const cities = ['New York', 'San Francisco', 'Austin'] as const;\n\n  const series = cities.map(function mapCity(city, index) {\n    return {\n      id: `city-${city.toLowerCase().replace(/\\s+/g, '-')}`,\n      name: city,\n      data: cityTemperature.slice(0, 10).map(function mapData(d) {\n        return {\n          x: d.date,\n          y: parseFloat(d[city as keyof typeof d])\n        };\n      })\n    };\n  });\n\n  return (\n    <BarChart\n      series={series}\n      xAccessor={(d: any) => d.x}\n      yAccessor={(d: any) => d.y}\n      xAxisTitle=\&#x22;Date\&#x22;\n      yAxisTitle=\&#x22;Temperature (°F)\&#x22;\n      yDomain={[0, 100]}\n      xBaseline={true}\n      yBaseline={true}\n      xTickMarks={true}\n      yTickMarks={true}\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Horizontal single series [#horizontal-single-series]

\`orientation="horizontal"\` swaps the axes: categories run down the side and values across the bottom. Reach for it when the labels are long or the chart is really a ranking.

<Story of="HorizontalSingleSeriesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { exoplanets as allExoplanets, type Exoplanets } from '@visx/mock-data';\n\nconst largestExoplanets = [...allExoplanets.filter((d) => d.distance && d.distance > 0)]\n  .sort((a, b) => b.radius - a.radius)\n  .slice(0, 30);\n\nconst series = [{ id: 'radius', name: 'Radius', data: largestExoplanets }];\n\nexport function HorizontalSingleSeriesExample(props: any) {\n  return (\n    <BarChart\n      series={series}\n      orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22;\n      xAccessor={(d: Exoplanets) => d.radius}\n      yAccessor={(d: Exoplanets) => d.name}\n      xAxisTitle=\&#x22;Radius (Rj)\&#x22;\n      yAxisTitle=\&#x22;Exoplanet\&#x22;\n      xBaseline={true}\n      yBaseline={true}\n      xTickMarks={true}\n      yTickMarks={true}\n      yGridlines={true}\n      xGridlines={true}\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Horizontal multi-series [#horizontal-multi-series]

Grouped bars work horizontally too. With many categories the chart scrolls vertically, which is usually easier on a phone than scrolling sideways.

<Story of="HorizontalMultiSeriesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { exoplanets as allExoplanets } from '@visx/mock-data';\n\ninterface ExoplanetSurveyPoint {\n  name: string;\n  value: number;\n}\n\n// Take 90 real exoplanets and use the first 15 names as the shared category axis.\n// Each series maps a different group of 15 planets' radius onto those same category names,\n// demonstrating multi-series grouped bars with real exoplanet data.\nconst trueExoplanets = allExoplanets.filter((d) => d.distance && d.distance > 0).slice(0, 60);\nconst categoryNames = trueExoplanets.slice(0, 15).map((d) => d.name);\n\nfunction toSurveyData(planets: typeof trueExoplanets): ExoplanetSurveyPoint[] {\n  return planets.slice(0, 15).map((d, i) => ({ name: categoryNames[i], value: d.radius }));\n}\n\nconst series = [\n  { id: 'survey-a', name: 'Survey A', data: toSurveyData(trueExoplanets.slice(0, 15)) },\n  { id: 'survey-b', name: 'Survey B', data: toSurveyData(trueExoplanets.slice(15, 30)) },\n  { id: 'survey-c', name: 'Survey C', data: toSurveyData(trueExoplanets.slice(30, 45)) },\n  { id: 'survey-d', name: 'Survey D', data: toSurveyData(trueExoplanets.slice(45, 60)) }\n];\n\nexport function HorizontalMultiSeriesExample(props: any) {\n  return (\n    <BarChart\n      series={series}\n      orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22;\n      xAccessor={(d: ExoplanetSurveyPoint) => d.value}\n      yAccessor={(d: ExoplanetSurveyPoint) => d.name}\n      xAxisTitle=\&#x22;Radius (Rj)\&#x22;\n      yAxisTitle=\&#x22;Exoplanet\&#x22;\n      xBaseline={true}\n      yBaseline={true}\n      xTickMarks={true}\n      yTickMarks={true}\n      yGridlines={true}\n      xGridlines={true}\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Custom domain [#custom-domain]

\`xDomain\` and \`yDomain\` pin down exactly which categories and value range to draw. Here category \`F\` has no data and still gets an empty slot, and the Y range stays \`\[0, 40]\` even though the largest bar is 30 - handy when several charts need to share a scale.

<Story of="CustomDomainExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CustomDomainExample() {\n  const data = [\n    { category: 'A', value: 10 },\n    { category: 'B', value: 20 },\n    { category: 'C', value: 15 },\n    { category: 'D', value: 30 },\n    { category: 'E', value: 5 }\n  ];\n  // Example: set xDomain and yDomain explicitly\n  const xDomain = ['A', 'B', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'C']; // F will show as empty slot\n  const yDomain: [number, number] = [0, 40];\n  return (\n    <BarChart\n      series={[\n        {\n          id: 'series1',\n          name: 'Sample Series',\n          data\n        }\n      ]}\n      xAccessor={(d: { category: string; value: number }) => d.category}\n      yAccessor={(d: { category: string; value: number }) => d.value}\n      height={400}\n      width={600}\n      xAxisTitle=\&#x22;Category\&#x22;\n      yAxisTitle=\&#x22;Value\&#x22;\n      xDomain={xDomain}\n      yDomain={yDomain}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Formatted tick marks [#formatted-tick-marks]

\`xTickFormat\` and \`yTickFormat\` shape the axis labels - abbreviated dates on one axis, thousands separators on the other. The functions receive the raw accessor value, so they also cover currency, units, or percentages.

<Story of="FormattedTickMarksExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function FormattedTickMarksExample() {\n  // Example data with Date categories\n  const data = [\n    { category: new Date(2024, 0, 1), value: 1000 }, // Jan 1\n    { category: new Date(2024, 1, 15), value: 2500 }, // Feb 15\n    { category: new Date(2024, 2, 10), value: 1750 }, // Mar 10\n    { category: new Date(2024, 3, 5), value: 3000 }, // Apr 5\n    { category: new Date(2024, 4, 20), value: 1250 } // May 20\n  ];\n\n  // Format x-axis as abbreviated month and day\n  function formatDateTick(value: Date | string | number) {\n    if (value instanceof Date) {\n      return value.toLocaleString('en-US', { month: 'short', day: 'numeric' });\n    }\n    return String(value);\n  }\n\n  // Format y-axis as comma-separated number\n  function formatNumberWithCommas(value: number | string | Date) {\n    if (typeof value === 'number') {\n      return value.toLocaleString();\n    }\n    return String(value);\n  }\n\n  return (\n    <BarChart\n      series={[\n        {\n          id: 'series1',\n          name: 'Sales',\n          data\n        }\n      ]}\n      xAccessor={(d: { category: Date; value: number }) => d.category}\n      yAccessor={(d: { category: Date; value: number }) => d.value}\n      height={600}\n      width={600}\n      xAxisTitle=\&#x22;Date\&#x22;\n      yAxisTitle=\&#x22;Sales Amount\&#x22;\n      xTickFormat={formatDateTick}\n      yTickFormat={formatNumberWithCommas}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### RTL multi-series [#rtl-multi-series]

The chart follows the current layout direction, which is normally detected from the browser or system settings. In right-to-left it mirrors the axes, bars, and labels; this example forces RTL so you can see it in a left-to-right page. RTL support is still being refined - axis rendering and tick spacing in particular.

<Story of="RTLMultiSeriesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { RTLProvider } from '../../../../utils/rtl-locale-provider.tsx';\n\nexport function RTLMultiSeriesExample(props: any) {\n  const cities = ['New York', 'San Francisco', 'Austin'] as const;\n\n  const series = cities.map(function mapCity(city) {\n    return {\n      id: `city-${city.toLowerCase().replace(/\\s+/g, '-')}`,\n      name: city,\n      data: cityTemperature.slice(0, 10).map(function mapData(d) {\n        return {\n          x: d.date,\n          y: parseFloat(d[city as keyof typeof d])\n        };\n      })\n    };\n  });\n\n  return (\n    <RTLProvider>\n      <BarChart\n        series={series}\n        xAccessor={(d: any) => d.x}\n        yAccessor={(d: any) => d.y}\n        xAxisTitle=\&#x22;Date\&#x22;\n        yAxisTitle=\&#x22;Temperature (°F)\&#x22;\n        xBaseline={true}\n        yBaseline={true}\n        xTickMarks={true}\n        yTickMarks={true}\n        yGridlines={true}\n        {...props}\n      />\n    </RTLProvider>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### RTL horizontal multi-series [#rtl-horizontal-multi-series]

Horizontal grouped bars in a right-to-left layout: bars grow from the right edge and the category axis moves to the right side.

<Story of="RTLHorizontalMultiSeriesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\nimport { exoplanets as allExoplanets } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { RTLProvider } from '../../../../utils/rtl-locale-provider.tsx';\n\ninterface ExoplanetSurveyPoint {\n  name: string;\n  value: number;\n}\n\nconst trueExoplanets = allExoplanets.filter((d) => d.distance && d.distance > 0).slice(0, 60);\nconst categoryNames = trueExoplanets.slice(0, 15).map((d) => d.name);\n\nfunction toSurveyData(planets: typeof trueExoplanets): ExoplanetSurveyPoint[] {\n  return planets.slice(0, 15).map((d, i) => ({ name: categoryNames[i], value: d.radius }));\n}\n\nconst series = [\n  { id: 'survey-a', name: 'Survey A', data: toSurveyData(trueExoplanets.slice(0, 15)) },\n  { id: 'survey-b', name: 'Survey B', data: toSurveyData(trueExoplanets.slice(15, 30)) },\n  { id: 'survey-c', name: 'Survey C', data: toSurveyData(trueExoplanets.slice(30, 45)) },\n  { id: 'survey-d', name: 'Survey D', data: toSurveyData(trueExoplanets.slice(45, 60)) }\n];\n\nexport function RTLHorizontalMultiSeriesExample(props: any) {\n  return (\n    <RTLProvider>\n      <BarChart\n        series={series}\n        orientation=\&#x22;horizontal\&#x22;\n        xAccessor={(d: ExoplanetSurveyPoint) => d.value}\n        yAccessor={(d: ExoplanetSurveyPoint) => d.name}\n        xAxisTitle=\&#x22;Radius (Rj)\&#x22;\n        yAxisTitle=\&#x22;Exoplanet\&#x22;\n        xBaseline={true}\n        yBaseline={true}\n        xTickMarks={true}\n        yTickMarks={true}\n        yGridlines={true}\n        xGridlines={true}\n        {...props}\n      />\n    </RTLProvider>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Design System Alignment [#design-system-alignment]

### Spacing and Sizing [#spacing-and-sizing]

* **Bar width**: 12px (1.5 grid units)
* **Bar padding** (multi-series): 4px between bars within a group
* **Group gap**: Minimum 24px between bar groups
* **Border radius**: 8px on all bars
* **Margins**: 20px top/right, 60px bottom/left for axes and labels

### Responsive Behavior [#responsive-behavior]

* **Auto-sizing**: Uses VisX's `useParentSize` hook to adapt to container width
* **Horizontal scrolling**: When data points exceed available width, the chart becomes horizontally scrollable
* **Sticky y-axis**: The y-axis remains visible during horizontal scroll
* **Minimum spacing**: Group gaps never fall below 24px, triggering scroll instead

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

* **Keyboard navigation**: Bar groups are keyboard accessible with `tabIndex={0}` and `role="group"`
* **Screen reader support**: Semantic HTML structure with proper ARIA attributes
* **Tooltips**: Show on both hover and focus for keyboard users

## Performance Considerations [#performance-considerations]

### Rendering Strategy [#rendering-strategy]

The component uses VisX primitives for optimal SVG rendering:

* **Scales**: VisX's `scaleBand` and `scaleLinear` for efficient coordinate mapping
* **Grouped rendering**: Bars are rendered in SVG `<Group>` elements for logical organization
* **Responsive sizing**: `useParentSize` hook provides efficient resize detection with debouncing (15ms)

### Scrolling Strategy [#scrolling-strategy]

* **Vertical charts**: Horizontal scrolling when many data points exceed container width
* **Horizontal charts**: Vertical scrolling when many categories exceed container height
* **Sticky axes**: Positioned absolutely to remain visible during scroll

### Recommendations [#recommendations]

* For charts with **many data points** (>20), consider enabling horizontal scroll (default behavior)
* For **horizontal bar charts**, vertical scrolling is more mobile-friendly than horizontal
* Use **custom domains** to maintain consistent scales across multiple charts
* **Tooltips** use absolute positioning and scroll-aware calculations for accurate placement

## Development Status [#development-status]

The BarChart component is in active development. Current focus areas:

* ✅ Single and multi-series support
* ✅ Vertical and horizontal orientations
* ✅ Responsive behavior with sticky axes
* ✅ Interactive tooltips
* ✅ Custom domains
* ✅ Design system alignment
* 🚧 RTL compatibility (axis rendering and spacing refinement)
* 🚧 Tick mark positioning improvements
* 🚧 Additional customization options (tick formatting, axis configuration)

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Bars Not Showing [#bars-not-showing]

If bars are not visible:

1. **Check data**: Ensure `series` array has data and `xAccessor`/`yAccessor` return valid values
2. **Check domains**: Verify `yDomain` (if set) includes your data values
3. **Check dimensions**: Ensure container has non-zero width and height

### Tooltip Positioning Issues [#tooltip-positioning-issues]

If tooltips appear in the wrong location:

1. **Check scroll position**: The component accounts for horizontal scroll automatically
2. **Check container**: Ensure the chart container is not transformed or positioned in a complex layout
3. **Verify event targets**: Tooltips use mouse event coordinates and bar group positions

### Performance Issues [#performance-issues]

For better performance:

1. **Limit data points**: Consider pagination or filtering for very large datasets (>100 points)
2. **Debounce resize**: The default 15ms debounce on `useParentSize` balances smoothness and performance
3. **Simplify tooltips**: If tooltips are complex, consider using simpler content or disabling them

# Gauge Chart



















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

A continuous gauge with a single label.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { GaugeChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample() {\n  return <GaugeChart value={50} label=\&#x22;50%\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Basic gauge\&#x22; style={{ maxWidth: '200px', margin: 'auto' }} />;\n}&#x22;" />

### Continuous Values [#continuous-values]

Multiple continuous gauges showing different fill percentages.

<Story of="ContinuousExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, GaugeChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ContinuousExample() {\n  const values = [0, 25, 50, 75, 100];\n\n  return (\n    <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr))\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; alignContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      {values.map(function renderGauge(v) {\n        return <GaugeChart key={v} value={v} label={`${v}%`} subLabel=\&#x22;Progress\&#x22; aria-label={`Gauge at ${v}%`} />;\n      })}\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Segmented [#segmented]

Segmented gauges divide the arc into discrete sections (1–5). The \`value\` prop selects how many segments are filled.

<Story of="SegmentedExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, GaugeChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SegmentedExample() {\n  return (\n    <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(2, 200px)\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      <GaugeChart segments={5} value={0} label=\&#x22;0/5\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Empty\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Gauge with 0 of 5 filled\&#x22; />\n      <GaugeChart segments={5} value={2} label=\&#x22;2/5\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Partial\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Gauge with 2 of 5 filled\&#x22; />\n      <GaugeChart segments={5} value={5} label=\&#x22;5/5\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Full\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Gauge with 5 of 5 filled\&#x22; />\n      <GaugeChart segments={3} value={1} label=\&#x22;1/3\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Three segments\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Gauge with 1 of 3 filled\&#x22; />\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### With Range Labels [#with-range-labels]

Min/max labels positioned below the gauge arc at the left and right edges. Both \`min\` and \`max\` must be provided.

<Story of="WithRangeLabelsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, GaugeChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function WithRangeLabelsExample() {\n  return (\n    <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(2, 1fr)\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      <GaugeChart\n        value={65}\n        label=\&#x22;65%\&#x22;\n        subLabel=\&#x22;CPU Usage\&#x22;\n        rangeLabel={{ min: 0, max: 100 }}\n        aria-label=\&#x22;CPU usage gauge\&#x22;\n      />\n      <GaugeChart\n        value={3}\n        segments={5}\n        label=\&#x22;3/5\&#x22;\n        subLabel=\&#x22;Risk Level\&#x22;\n        rangeLabel={{ min: 'Low', max: 'High' }}\n        variant=\&#x22;warning\&#x22;\n        aria-label=\&#x22;Risk level gauge\&#x22;\n      />\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Variants [#variants]

Color variants convey meaning at a glance — use \`success\`, \`warning\`, or \`critical\` alongside descriptive text.

<Story of="VariantsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, GaugeChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function VariantsExample() {\n  return (\n    <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(2, 1fr)\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      <GaugeChart value={50} label=\&#x22;50%\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Default\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;default\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Default variant gauge\&#x22; />\n      <GaugeChart value={50} label=\&#x22;50%\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Success\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;success\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Success variant gauge\&#x22; />\n      <GaugeChart value={50} label=\&#x22;50%\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Warning\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;warning\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Warning variant gauge\&#x22; />\n      <GaugeChart value={50} label=\&#x22;50%\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Critical\&#x22; variant=\&#x22;critical\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Critical variant gauge\&#x22; />\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Label Type [#label-type]

Control the font size of the primary label using \`labelType\`. Use \`'value'\` for numeric or percentage values and \`'text'\` for short descriptive strings.

<Story of="LabelTypeExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, GaugeChart } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function LabelTypeExample() {\n  return (\n    <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(2, 1fr)\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22;>\n      <GaugeChart value={72} label=\&#x22;72%\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Completion\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Gauge with numeric value label\&#x22; />\n      <GaugeChart value={72} label=\&#x22;Good\&#x22; labelType=\&#x22;text\&#x22; subLabel=\&#x22;Completion\&#x22; aria-label=\&#x22;Gauge with text label\&#x22; />\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Gauge Not Sizing Correctly [#gauge-not-sizing-correctly]

The component uses `container-type: inline-size` and fills its parent width. Ensure the parent has a defined width:

```tsx
// ❌ No width constraint — gauge may stretch to full viewport
<GaugeChart label="50%" value={50} aria-label="Progress" />

// ✅ Parent provides width context
<div style={{ width: 200 }}>
  <GaugeChart label="50%" value={50} aria-label="Progress" />
</div>

// ✅ Or use className for max-width
<GaugeChart className="my-gauge" label="50%" value={50} aria-label="Progress" />
```

### Value Out of Range [#value-out-of-range]

Values outside the valid range are clamped silently at runtime. For continuous mode the range is 0–100; for segmented mode the range is 0 to the segment count.

```tsx
// ✅ Continuous: 0–100
<GaugeChart label="75%" value={75} aria-label="Score" />

// ✅ Segmented: 0 to segments
<GaugeChart label="3/5" value={3} segments={5} aria-label="Risk level" />
```
