<PropTable />


# LineChart























































<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

One line, a time-scale X axis, and almost nothing else configured - the everyday starting point. You give the chart a \`series\` array and it reads \`x\`/\`y\` from each point.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      yZero={false}\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Single series example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating single series with minimal configuration\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Multiple series [#multiple-series]

Several lines sharing one X axis, with a legend naming each of them. Reach for this when the comparison between series is the story.

<Story of="MultipleSeriesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function MultipleSeriesExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Product A',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    },\n    {\n      id: 'series-2',\n      name: 'Product B',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['San Francisco']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    },\n    {\n      id: 'series-3',\n      name: 'Product C',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['Austin']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    },\n    {\n      id: 'series-4',\n      name: 'Product D',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) * 1.1 }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      yZero={false}\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Multiple series example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating multiple series comparison\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Gridlines [#gridlines]

\`xGridlines\` and \`yGridlines\` add faint lines across the plot so it is easier to read a value back off an axis.

<Story of="GridlinesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function GridlinesExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      yZero={false}\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      xGridlines={true}\n      yGridlines={true}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Gridlines example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating gridlines only\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Titles [#titles]

\`xTitle\` and \`yTitle\` label what each axis actually measures, e.g. "Month" and "Temperature (°F)".

<Story of="TitlesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TitlesExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      yZero={false}\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      xTitle=\&#x22;Date\&#x22;\n      yTitle=\&#x22;Value\&#x22;\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Titles example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating axis titles only\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Labels [#labels]

\`xLabels\` and \`yLabels\` toggle the tick labels on each axis. Turn them off for sparklines or when the surrounding UI already names the values.

<Story of="LabelsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function LabelsExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Labels example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating axis labels only\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Ticks [#ticks]

\`xTickMarks\` and \`yTickMarks\` draw the short lines at each tick value, which helps tie a label to its exact position on the axis.

<Story of="TicksExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TicksExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      xTickMarks={true}\n      yTickMarks={true}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Ticks example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating tick marks only\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Baselines [#baselines]

\`xBaseline\` and \`yBaseline\` control the main axis lines themselves. Dropping them gives a lighter, more editorial chart.

<Story of="BaselinesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function BaselinesExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      xBaseline={true}\n      yBaseline={true}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Baselines example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating axis baselines only\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Legend [#legend]

\`legendPosition\` puts the legend above or below the plot, or hides it with \`null\`. Multi-series charts get a bottom legend by default.

<Story of="LegendExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function LegendExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    },\n    {\n      id: 'series-2',\n      name: 'Series 2',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['San Francisco']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    },\n    {\n      id: 'series-3',\n      name: 'Series 3',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['Austin']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      yZero={false}\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      legendPosition=\&#x22;bottom\&#x22;\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Legend example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating legend only\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Axis and tooltip formatting [#axis-and-tooltip-formatting]

\`xTickFormat\` and \`yTickFormat\` shape the axis labels - dates, currency, units, percentages - and the tooltip follows the same formatting.

<Story of="FormattingExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps, type DataPoint } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nfunction formatDate(value: number | string | Date): string {\n  if (value instanceof Date) {\n    return value.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', day: 'numeric' });\n  }\n  return String(value);\n}\n\nfunction formatCurrency(value: number): string {\n  return `$${value.toLocaleString('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`;\n}\n\nfunction formatTooltipCurrency(d: DataPoint): string {\n  return `$${d.y!.toLocaleString('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`;\n}\n\nexport function FormattingExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xTickFormat={formatDate}\n      yTickFormat={formatCurrency}\n      tooltipValueFormatter={formatTooltipCurrency}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Formatting example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating axis and tooltip formatting\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Custom accessors [#custom-accessors]

When your data does not use \`x\`/\`y\`, point \`xAccessor\` and \`yAccessor\` at the fields it does use (here \`date\` and \`value\`) instead of reshaping the data first.

<Story of="CustomAccessorsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { type DateValue, cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CustomAccessorsExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps<DateValue>>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ date: new Date(d.date), value: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.date.getTime() - b.date.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xAccessor={(d) => d.date}\n      yAccessor={(d) => d.value}\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Custom accessors example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating custom data types with accessors\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Missing values [#missing-values]

A \`null\` Y value breaks the line instead of drawing through the gap, so missing data reads as missing rather than as a straight interpolation.

<Story of="MissingValuesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { appleStock } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function MissingValuesExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const missingPeriodStart = new Date('2010-01-01');\n  const missingPeriodEnd = new Date('2010-12-31T23:59:59.999');\n\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'apple-stock-missing',\n      name: 'Apple Stock Price',\n      data: appleStock.map(function mapStockData(d) {\n        const date = new Date(d.date);\n        const isInMissingPeriod = date >= missingPeriodStart && date <= missingPeriodEnd;\n        return {\n          x: date,\n          y: isInMissingPeriod ? null : d.close\n        };\n      })\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Missing values example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating null values handling with visual breaks\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Fixed domain [#fixed-domain]

\`xDomain\` and \`yDomain\` pin the visible range. Use them to keep a fixed scale, or to keep several charts comparable.

<Story of="FixedDomainExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { appleStock } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function FixedDomainExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const data = appleStock\n    .slice(0, 150)\n    .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: d.close }))\n    .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime());\n\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Stock Price',\n      data: data\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xDomain={[new Date('2007-04-01'), new Date('2007-06-01')]}\n      yDomain={[80, 200]}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Fixed domain example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating explicit domain values with axis labels. Shows Apple stock data for the year 2007 with a fixed X-axis domain.\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Nice values [#nice-values]

\`xNice\` and \`yNice\` round the domain out to friendlier numbers (e.g. 0.2 to 1.0), so ticks land on values people expect.

<Story of="NiceValuesExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NiceValuesExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xNice={true}\n      yNice={true}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Nice values example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating nice rounded values\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Zero included [#zero-included]

\`xZero\` and \`yZero\` stretch the domain to include zero. Worth doing when the absolute size of the values matters, not just their movement.

<Story of="ZeroIncludedExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { appleStock } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ZeroIncludedExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: appleStock.slice(0, 40).map((d, i) => ({ x: i, y: d.close }))\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;linear\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xZero={true}\n      yZero={true}\n      height={500}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Zero included example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating zero included in domain\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Custom ticks [#custom-ticks]

Choose the ticks yourself with \`xTickValues\`/\`yTickValues\`, or just ask for roughly how many you want with \`xNumTicks\`/\`yNumTicks\`.

<Story of="CustomTicksExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CustomTicksExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xNumTicks={5}\n      yNumTicks={9}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Custom ticks example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating custom tick values/counts\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Band padding [#band-padding]

\`xPaddingOuter\` and \`yPaddingOuter\` add breathing room at the ends of a band or point scale so the first and last values are not pinned to the edges.

<Story of="BandPaddingExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function BandPaddingExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const xDomain = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4'];\n\n  const series = [\n    {\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: [\n        { x: 'Q1', y: '100' },\n        { x: 'Q2', y: '200' },\n        { x: 'Q3', y: '150' },\n        { x: 'Q4', y: '300' }\n      ]\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;band\&#x22;\n      yType=\&#x22;band\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xDomain={xDomain}\n      xPaddingOuter={0.1}\n      yPaddingOuter={0.1}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Band padding example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating band scale padding\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Tooltip disabled [#tooltip-disabled]

Turn off the hover affordances entirely with \`tooltip=\{false}\`, \`showCrosshair=\{false}\`, and \`showDataPoints=\{false}\` - useful for a static or print-style chart.

<Story of="TooltipDisabledExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function TooltipDisabledExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      tooltip={false}\n      showCrosshair={false}\n      showDataPoints={false}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Tooltip disabled example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating no tooltip or interactive features\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Crosshair only [#crosshair-only]

Keep the vertical crosshair for orientation while hiding the tooltip and the data point glyphs.

<Story of="CrosshairOnlyExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function CrosshairOnlyExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      tooltip={false}\n      showCrosshair={true}\n      showDataPoints={true}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Crosshair only example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating crosshair without tooltip\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Custom tooltip formatting [#custom-tooltip-formatting]

\`tooltipValueFormatter\` shapes only the tooltip values, so you can show full currency or units there while the axis stays compact.

<Story of="CustomTooltipFormattingExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps, type DataPoint } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nfunction formatTooltipValue(d: DataPoint): string {\n  return `Value: ${(d.y as number).toFixed(2)} units`;\n}\n\nexport function CustomTooltipFormattingExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      yZero={false}\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      tooltipValueFormatter={formatTooltipValue}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Custom tooltip formatting example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating custom tooltip formatter\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Fixed size [#fixed-size]

Pass \`width\` and \`height\` to size the chart explicitly instead of letting it fill its container.

<Story of="FixedSizeExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function FixedSizeExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'series-1',\n      name: 'Series 1',\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .slice(0, 10)\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d['New York']) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={false}\n      yLabels={false}\n      width={800}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Fixed size example chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart demonstrating fixed width/height\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Bitcoin price [#bitcoin-price]

A real time series: date formatting on the X axis, currency on the Y axis, gridlines, and a nice-rounded domain.

<Story of="BitcoinPriceExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { bitcoinPrice } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps, type DataPoint } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nfunction formatDate(value: number | string | Date): string {\n  if (value instanceof Date) {\n    return value.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: 'numeric' });\n  }\n  return String(value);\n}\n\nfunction formatLargeCurrency(value: number): string {\n  return `$${value.toLocaleString('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`;\n}\n\nfunction formatTooltipCurrency(d: DataPoint): string {\n  return `$${(d.y as number).toLocaleString('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`;\n}\n\nexport function BitcoinPriceExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const series = [\n    {\n      id: 'bitcoin-price',\n      name: 'Bitcoin Price',\n      data: bitcoinPrice.prices\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.time), y: Number(d.price) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    }\n  ];\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xTitle=\&#x22;Date\&#x22;\n      yTitle={`Price (${bitcoinPrice.currency})`}\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xTickFormat={formatDate}\n      yTickFormat={formatLargeCurrency}\n      yGridlines={true}\n      yNice={true}\n      tooltipValueFormatter={formatTooltipCurrency}\n      height={600}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Bitcoin price chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart showing Bitcoin price over time with complete configuration including large number currency formatting, date formatting, gridlines, tick marks, baselines, and nice rounded values\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### City temperature [#city-temperature]

Several cities over the same period, with a legend and a shared time axis - the multi-series case as it usually looks in a product.

<Story of="CityTemperatureExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { cityTemperature } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps, type DataPoint } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nfunction formatDate(value: number | string | Date): string {\n  if (value instanceof Date) {\n    return value.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', year: 'numeric' });\n  }\n  return String(value);\n}\n\nfunction formatTemperature(value: number): string {\n  return `${value.toFixed(1)}°F`;\n}\n\nfunction formatTooltipTemperature(d: DataPoint): string {\n  return `${(d.y as number).toFixed(1)}°F`;\n}\n\nexport function CityTemperatureExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const cities = ['New York', 'San Francisco', 'Austin'] as const;\n\n  const series = cities.map(function mapCity(city) {\n    return {\n      id: `city-${city.toLowerCase().replace(/\\s+/g, '-')}`,\n      name: city,\n      data: cityTemperature\n        .map((d) => ({ x: new Date(d.date), y: parseFloat(d[city as keyof typeof d] as string) }))\n        .sort((a, b) => a.x.getTime() - b.x.getTime())\n    };\n  });\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;time\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xTickMarks={true}\n      yTickMarks={true}\n      xBaseline={true}\n      yBaseline={true}\n      xNice={true}\n      yNice={true}\n      xTickFormat={formatDate}\n      yTickFormat={formatTemperature}\n      legendPosition=\&#x22;top\&#x22;\n      tooltipValueFormatter={formatTooltipTemperature}\n      height={400}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;City temperature comparison chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart showing temperature comparisons across multiple cities over time with complete axis configuration including gridlines, tick marks, baselines, date formatting, and unit formatting\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Browser usage [#browser-usage]

A categorical X axis (band scale) with several series and percentage formatting, for when the X values are names rather than numbers or dates.

<Story of="BrowserUsageExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { browserUsage } from '@visx/mock-data';\nimport { LineChart, type LineChartProps, type DataPoint } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nfunction formatPercentage(value: number): string {\n  return `${value.toFixed(2)}%`;\n}\n\nfunction formatTooltipPercentage(d: DataPoint): string {\n  return `${(d.y as number).toFixed(2)}%`;\n}\n\nexport function BrowserUsageExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  const browserNames = ['Google Chrome', 'Internet Explorer', 'Firefox', 'Safari', 'Microsoft Edge', 'Opera'] as const;\n\n  const series = browserNames.map(function mapBrowser(browser) {\n    return {\n      id: `browser-${browser.toLowerCase().replace(/\\s+/g, '-')}`,\n      name: browser,\n      data: browserUsage.map((d) => ({ x: d.date, y: parseFloat(d[browser as keyof typeof d] as string) }))\n    };\n  });\n\n  return (\n    <LineChart\n      series={series}\n      xType=\&#x22;band\&#x22;\n      xTitle=\&#x22;Date\&#x22;\n      yTitle=\&#x22;Market Share (%)\&#x22;\n      xLabels={true}\n      yLabels={true}\n      xTickMarks={true}\n      yTickMarks={true}\n      xBaseline={true}\n      yBaseline={true}\n      xGridlines={true}\n      yGridlines={true}\n      xNice={true}\n      yNice={true}\n      yTickFormat={formatPercentage}\n      tooltipValueFormatter={formatTooltipPercentage}\n      legendPosition=\&#x22;bottom\&#x22;\n      height={600}\n      aria-label=\&#x22;Browser usage market share chart\&#x22;\n      desc=\&#x22;Line chart showing browser market share percentages over time with multiple series, complete axis configuration including gridlines, tick marks, baselines, date formatting, and percentage formatting\&#x22;\n      {...props}\n    />\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### RTL [#rtl]

The chart follows the current layout direction, normally detected from the browser or system settings. In right-to-left it mirrors the axes and labels; this example forces RTL so you can see it in a left-to-right page.

<Story of="RTLExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { RTLProvider } from '../../../../utils/rtl-locale-provider.tsx';\nimport { CityTemperatureExample } from './city-temperature.tsx';\nimport type { LineChartProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function RTLExample(props: Partial<LineChartProps>) {\n  return (\n    <RTLProvider>\n      <CityTemperatureExample {...props} />\n    </RTLProvider>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

The chart root exposes data attributes that reflect prop state for styling:

**Chart container:** `data-width`, `data-height`, `data-x-labels`, `data-y-labels`, `data-x-labels-vertical`, `data-x-baseline`, `data-y-baseline`, `data-x-tick-marks`, `data-y-tick-marks`

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Use the `className` prop on the chart container to add or override styles:

```tsx
<LineChart series={series} className="my-custom-chart" />
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

* Provide &#x2A;*`aria-label`** to describe the chart (e.g. "Monthly sales revenue from January to May 2024").
* Use &#x2A;*`desc`** for a longer description rendered in the SVG `<desc>` for screen readers.
* The component sets ARIA attributes on interactive and structural elements as needed.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use LineChart [#when-to-use-linechart]

* Use for trends over time or along a continuous scale.
* Use when comparing a few series (e.g. 2-5 lines); avoid too many overlapping lines.
* Prefer a single chart with a legend over multiple small charts when comparing the same X range.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Chart Not Sizing or Empty [#chart-not-sizing-or-empty]

Ensure the chart has a non-zero size. Place it in a container with explicit dimensions or use `width` and `height`:

```tsx
// ✅ Container with size
<div style={{ width: '100%', height: 400 }}>
  <LineChart series={series} />
</div>

// ✅ Or fixed dimensions on the component
<LineChart series={series} width={600} height={400} />
```

### Dates Not Displaying Correctly [#dates-not-displaying-correctly]

Use `xType="time"` when the X-axis values are Date objects:

```tsx
// ❌ Without xType="time", Date objects may not scale correctly
<LineChart series={seriesWithDates} />

// ✅ Use time scale for Date X values
<LineChart series={seriesWithDates} xType="time" />
```

### Tooltip or Crosshair Not Showing [#tooltip-or-crosshair-not-showing]

Ensure `tooltip`, `showCrosshair`, or `showDataPoints` are not set to `false`, and that the chart receives pointer events (e.g. no overlay blocking hover).

## Props [#props]

<PropTable />


# Box

















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

`Box` is a polymorphic layout component that renders as any HTML element or custom component via the `as` prop. It provides consistent spacing, elevation, rounding, and self-alignment within flex or grid containers.

**Important**: Since `Flex` and `Grid` extend `Box`, prefer them for layouts. Use `Box` only when you need a non-flex, non-grid container.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Scale Sizes [#scale-sizes]

The spacing props use semantic t-shirt sizes for padding, gap, and other spacing properties:

* `xs` - Extra small spacing
* `sm` - Small spacing
* `md` - Medium spacing
* `lg` - Large spacing
* `xl` - Extra large spacing
* `2xl` - 2x extra large spacing

Custom CSS values are also supported for edge cases.

## Polymorphic `as` details [#polymorphic-as-details]

**HTML Elements:** When using `as="button"`, TypeScript enforces button-specific props like `type`, `disabled`, and `onClick`.

**Custom Components:** When using `as={MyComponent}`, Box accepts that component's props. If there's a prop name conflict, Box's props take priority.

**Typed Refs:** Refs are correctly typed based on the `as` value - `useRef<HTMLButtonElement>` works with `as="button"`.

## Examples [#examples]

### Padding [#padding]

The padding props support t-shirt sizes and CSS logical properties for RTL support.

<Story of="PaddingExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Box, Flex, type BoxProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function PaddingExample(attrs: BoxProps) {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; {...attrs}>\n        Padding: md\n      </Box>\n      <Box blockPadding=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        Block Padding: lg\n      </Box>\n      <Box inlinePadding=\&#x22;xl\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        Inline Padding: xl\n      </Box>\n      <Box blockPaddingStart=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; blockPaddingEnd=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        Block Padding Start: sm, End: lg\n      </Box>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Elevation [#elevation]

The elevation prop adds visual depth using box-shadow.

<Story of="ElevationExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Box, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ElevationExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n        Elevation: base\n      </Box>\n\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        Elevation: card\n      </Box>\n\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;raised\&#x22;>\n        Elevation: raised\n      </Box>\n\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;overlay\&#x22;>\n        Elevation: overlay\n      </Box>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Rounding [#rounding]

The rounding prop sets border-radius. Use \`full\` for fully rounded corners.

<Story of="RoundingExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Box, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function RoundingExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex wrap=\&#x22;wrap\&#x22; direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        xs\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        sm\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        md\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        lg\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;xl\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        xl\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;2xl\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        2xl\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;full\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; style={{ width: '80px', height: '80px' }}>\n        full\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; rounding=\&#x22;full\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22; style={{ width: '200px', height: '80px' }}>\n        pill\n      </Box>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Polymorphic as Prop [#polymorphic-as-prop]

Box is fully polymorphic - the \`as\` prop allows rendering as any HTML element or custom component while preserving type-safe props.

<Story of="AsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { useRef } from 'react';\nimport { Box, Flex, type BoxProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function AsExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n      <AsSemanticElements />\n      <AsInteractiveElements />\n      <AsWithTypedRefs />\n      <AsCustomComponent />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction AsSemanticElements() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n        Default (div)\n      </Box>\n      <Box as=\&#x22;section\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n        As section\n      </Box>\n      <Box as=\&#x22;article\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n        As article\n      </Box>\n      <Box as=\&#x22;span\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n        As span\n      </Box>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\n/** Interactive elements with their specific props. */\nfunction AsInteractiveElements() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <Box as=\&#x22;button\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22; type=\&#x22;button\&#x22;>\n        As button (click me)\n      </Box>\n\n      {/* Anchor with href - TypeScript enforces anchor-specific props */}\n      <Box as=\&#x22;a\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22; href=\&#x22;https://example.com\&#x22; target=\&#x22;_blank\&#x22; rel=\&#x22;noopener noreferrer\&#x22;>\n        As anchor (link)\n      </Box>\n\n      {/* Input element */}\n      <Box as=\&#x22;input\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22; type=\&#x22;text\&#x22; placeholder=\&#x22;As input element\&#x22; />\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\n/** Demonstrating typed refs for different elements. */\nfunction AsWithTypedRefs() {\n  // Each ref is typed to match the \&#x22;as\&#x22; element\n  const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);\n  const anchorRef = useRef<HTMLAnchorElement>(null);\n  const divRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);\n\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <Box as=\&#x22;button\&#x22; ref={buttonRef} padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n        Button with typed ref\n      </Box>\n\n      <Box as=\&#x22;a\&#x22; ref={anchorRef} href=\&#x22;#\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n        Anchor with typed ref\n      </Box>\n\n      <Box ref={divRef} padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n        Div with typed ref (default)\n      </Box>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\n/** Using Box with a custom component. */\nfunction AsCustomComponent() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <Box as={Card} type=\&#x22;A\&#x22;>\n        Custom Card\n      </Box>\n\n      <Box as={Card} type=\&#x22;B\&#x22;>\n        Custom Card\n      </Box>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n\n/** Custom component to demonstrate polymorphism with custom components. */\nfunction Card(props: BoxProps & { type?: 'A' | 'B' }) {\n  return (\n    <Box {...props}>\n      {props.type === 'A' ? 'type A! ' : 'type B! '}\n      {props.children}\n    </Box>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Alignment [#alignment]

Self-alignment props allow Box to position itself within flex or grid containers.

<Story of="AlignmentExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Box, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function AlignmentExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ height: '150px' }}>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignSelf=\&#x22;start\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        align-self: start\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignSelf=\&#x22;center\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        align-self: center\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignSelf=\&#x22;end\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        align-self: end\n      </Box>\n      <Box padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignSelf=\&#x22;stretch\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;card\&#x22;>\n        align-self: stretch\n      </Box>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## RTL Support [#rtl-support]

Box uses CSS logical properties (`padding-inline-start`, `padding-block-end`, etc.) which automatically adapt to RTL layouts. No additional configuration is needed.

## Design Tokens [#design-tokens]

All spacing, elevation, and rounding values are derived from the theme. If no theme is provided, default values are used. This ensures consistency across the design system.

## Props [#props]

The `Box` component accepts the following props:

<PropTable />


# Flex





















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

`Flex` is a one-dimensional layout component for arranging children in rows or columns with alignment and spacing control. It extends `Box`, inheriting all `Box` capabilities (padding, elevation, rounding, self-alignment, and polymorphic `as` prop).

**Recommended default**: Use `Flex` for most layouts. Since it extends `Box`, you get all `Box` capabilities without needing to nest components.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Scale Sizes [#scale-sizes]

We use the same scale sizes as the `Box` component. For more information, see the [**Box component documentation**](../box/README.mdx#scale-sizes).

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Basic horizontal flex layout with gap.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, type FlexProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: FlexProps) {\n  return (\n    <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; {...props}>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 1\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 2\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 3\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Direction [#direction]

The \`direction\` prop controls the main axis orientation.

<Story of="DirectionExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DirectionExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>Row (default)</Flex>\n        <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 1\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 2\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 3\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>Column</Flex>\n        <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 1\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 2\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 3\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>Row Reverse</Flex>\n        <Flex direction=\&#x22;row-reverse\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 1\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 2\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 3\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Alignment [#alignment]

Use \`justifyContent\` for main-axis distribution and \`alignItems\` for cross-axis alignment.

<Story of="AlignmentExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function AlignmentExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>justifyContent: space-between</Flex>\n        <Flex justifyContent=\&#x22;space-between\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Start\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Middle\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            End\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>justifyContent: center</Flex>\n        <Flex justifyContent=\&#x22;center\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 1\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 2\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>justifyContent: end</Flex>\n        <Flex justifyContent=\&#x22;end\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 1\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 2\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>alignItems: center (with varying heights)</Flex>\n        <Flex alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ height: '100px' }}>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Short\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;lg\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Tall\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Short\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>alignItems: stretch (default)</Flex>\n        <Flex alignItems=\&#x22;stretch\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ height: '100px' }}>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 1\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 2\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 3\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Gap [#gap]

The \`gap\` prop controls spacing between children. Use \`rowGap\` and \`columnGap\` for independent control.

<Story of="GapExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function GapExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>gap: sm</Flex>\n        <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>gap: md</Flex>\n        <Flex gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>gap: lg</Flex>\n        <Flex gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; ### Wrap [#wrap]

The \`wrap\` prop controls whether items wrap to multiple lines.

<Story of="WrapExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function WrapExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; ### Navbar [#navbar]

A common navigation bar pattern using space-between and nested Flex containers.

<Story of="NavbarExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, LinkButton, Button } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function NavbarExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex as=\&#x22;nav\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; justifyContent=\&#x22;space-between\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;xs\&#x22;>\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;h1\&#x22;>Logo</Flex>\n\n      <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22;>Home</LinkButton>\n        <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22;>About</LinkButton>\n        <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22;>Contact</LinkButton>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;primary\&#x22;>Sign In</Button>\n        <Button variant=\&#x22;secondary\&#x22;>Sign Up</Button>\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Sidebar [#sidebar]

A sidebar layout demonstrating Flex child props (\`flexShrink\`, \`flexGrow\`).

<Story of="SidebarExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Flex, LinkButton } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function SidebarExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex rounding=\&#x22;reduced\&#x22;>\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;aside\&#x22; direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;xs\&#x22; flexShrink=\&#x22;0\&#x22; style={{ width: '200px' }}>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;h3\&#x22;>Navigation</Flex>\n        <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22;>Dashboard</LinkButton>\n        <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22;>Settings</LinkButton>\n        <LinkButton href=\&#x22;#\&#x22;>Profile</LinkButton>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;main\&#x22; direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; flexGrow=\&#x22;1\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;h2\&#x22;>Main Content</Flex>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;p\&#x22;>\n          This main content area uses flexGrow=\&#x22;1\&#x22; to fill the remaining space. The sidebar uses flexShrink=\&#x22;0\&#x22; to\n          maintain its fixed width.\n        </Flex>\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## RTL Support [#rtl-support]

Flex uses CSS logical properties which automatically adapt to RTL layouts. The `direction` prop values (`row`, `row-reverse`) respect the document direction.

## Design Tokens [#design-tokens]

All gap and padding values are derived from the theme. If no theme is provided, default values are used. This ensures consistency across the design system.

## Migration from @ux/box [#migration-from-uxbox]

| Current `@ux/box`                    | New Pattern                      |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `<Box orientation="horizontal">`     | `<Flex direction="row" >`        |
| `<Box orientation="vertical">`       | `<Flex direction="column" >`     |
| `<Box blockAlignChildren="center">`  | `<Flex justifyContent="center">` |
| `<Box inlineAlignChildren="center">` | `<Flex alignItems="center">`     |

## Props [#props]

The `Flex` component accepts the following props:

<PropTable />


# Grid





















<Meta of="Stories" name="Overview" />

`Grid` is a two-dimensional CSS Grid layout component for complex grid-based layouts. It extends `Box`, inheriting all `Box` capabilities (padding, elevation, rounding, self-alignment, and polymorphic `as` prop).

**Use `Grid` when**: You need explicit two-dimensional layouts with rows and columns, named grid areas, or responsive auto-fill patterns.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Scale Sizes [#scale-sizes]

We use the same scale sizes as the `Box` component. For more information, see the [**Box component documentation**](../box/README.mdx#scale-sizes).

## Examples [#examples]

### Default [#default]

Basic 3-column grid layout with gap.

<Story of="DefaultExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, Flex, type GridProps } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function DefaultExample(props: GridProps) {\n  return (\n    <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(3, 1fr)\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; {...props}>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 1\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 2\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 3\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 4\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 5\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Item 6\n      </Flex>\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Columns [#columns]

The \`columns\` prop defines grid column tracks using CSS grid-template-columns syntax.

<Story of="ColumnsExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ColumnsExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>columns: 1fr 2fr 1fr</Flex>\n        <Grid columns=\&#x22;1fr 2fr 1fr\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Narrow\n          </Flex>\n        </Grid>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>columns: auto 1fr auto</Flex>\n        <Grid columns=\&#x22;auto 1fr auto\&#x22; ### Gap [#gap]

The \`gap\` prop controls spacing between grid cells. Use \`rowGap\` and \`columnGap\` for independent control.

<Story of="GapExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function GapExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>gap: xl</Flex>\n        <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(3, 1fr)\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;xl\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item\n          </Flex>\n        </Grid>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 3\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 4\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 5\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Item 6\n          </Flex>\n        </Grid>\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Named Areas [#named-areas]

Use \`areas\` to define named grid regions. Children use the \`gridArea\` prop for placement.

<Story of="AreasExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function AreasExample() {\n  return (\n    <Grid\n      areas={['header header header', 'sidebar main main', 'footer footer footer']}\n      columns=\&#x22;200px 1fr 1fr\&#x22;\n      rows=\&#x22;auto 1fr auto\&#x22;\n      gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;\n      style={{ height: '300px' }}\n    >\n      <Flex gridArea=\&#x22;header\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#c0c0c0' }}>\n        Header\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex gridArea=\&#x22;sidebar\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#d0d0d0' }}>\n        Sidebar\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex gridArea=\&#x22;main\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Main Content\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex gridArea=\&#x22;footer\&#x22; padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#c0c0c0' }}>\n        Footer\n      </Flex>\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Responsive Grid [#responsive-grid]

Use CSS \`auto-fill\` and \`minmax()\` for responsive column counts without media queries.

<Story of="ResponsiveExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function ResponsiveExample() {\n  return (\n    <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(auto-fill, minmax(150px, 1fr))\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Card 1\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Card 2\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Card 3\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Card 4\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Card 5\n      </Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;md\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n        Card 6\n      </Flex>\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Alignment [#alignment]

Use \`justifyItems\` and \`alignItems\` to control default alignment of all grid children.

<Story of="AlignmentExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function AlignmentExample() {\n  return (\n    <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;lg\&#x22;>\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>justifyItems: center</Flex>\n        <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(3, 1fr)\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; justifyItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Centered\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Centered\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Centered\n          </Flex>\n        </Grid>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>alignItems: center (with fixed row height)</Flex>\n        <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(3, 1fr)\&#x22; rows=\&#x22;100px\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Centered\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Centered\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            Centered\n          </Flex>\n        </Grid>\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex direction=\&#x22;column\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22;>\n        <Flex as=\&#x22;strong\&#x22;>justifyItems: end, alignItems: end</Flex>\n        <Grid columns=\&#x22;repeat(3, 1fr)\&#x22; rows=\&#x22;80px\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; justifyItems=\&#x22;end\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;end\&#x22; elevation=\&#x22;base\&#x22;>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            End\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            End\n          </Flex>\n          <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#e0e0e0' }}>\n            End\n          </Flex>\n        </Grid>\n      </Flex>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

### Form [#form]

A common two-column form pattern with auto-sized label column.

<Story of="FormExample" />

<Source language="tsx" code="&#x22;import { Grid, Flex } from '@godaddy/antares';\n\nexport function FormExample() {\n  return (\n    <Grid columns=\&#x22;auto 1fr\&#x22; gap=\&#x22;md\&#x22; alignItems=\&#x22;center\&#x22; style={{ width: '400px' }}>\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;label\&#x22;>Name</Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#f5f5f5' }}>\n        Input placeholder\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;label\&#x22;>Email</Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#f5f5f5' }}>\n        Input placeholder\n      </Flex>\n\n      <Flex as=\&#x22;label\&#x22;>Message</Flex>\n      <Flex padding=\&#x22;sm\&#x22; style={{ background: '#f5f5f5' }}>\n        Textarea placeholder\n      </Flex>\n    </Grid>\n  );\n}&#x22;" />

## RTL Support [#rtl-support]

Grid uses CSS logical properties which automatically adapt to RTL layouts. Grid areas and alignment respect the document direction.

## Grid vs Flex [#grid-vs-flex]

| Use Case                   | Recommended      |
| -------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Single row/column of items | Flex             |
| Two-dimensional layouts    | Grid             |
| Named layout regions       | Grid             |
| Auto-wrapping cards        | Grid (auto-fill) |
| Navigation bars            | Flex             |
| Form layouts               | Grid             |
